title: Unrealistic emissions scenarios help AI climate models prepare for unfamiliar futures
summary: MIT researchers with Imperial College London designed a small synthetic set of deliberately unrealistic emissions scenarios to train climate emulators, which normally need six to eight full Earth system model runs that each take months. The method needs only one model run, and the emulator predicted unseen scenarios and local pollutant-control effects where traditional emulators failed. It was validated with a simple climate model rather than a full Earth system model, and the article reports no quantitative accuracy metrics.
ai_technology: Climate emulator trained on optimized synthetic scenarios
organization: MIT; Imperial College London

evidence.tested: An emulator trained on a small set of synthetic scenarios predicted unseen scenarios and a local pollutant-control effect where traditional emulators failed. The source says it was validated with a simple climate model.
evidence.unknown: The source says the method still needs testing on a full Earth system model scenario and on other climate model types; it does not say whether this has been done.
evidence.ai_role: An optimization algorithm generated the synthetic training scenarios; an AI emulator was trained on them to predict climate outcomes.

title: Signs of hypertension detected by a smartwatch
summary: Prospective study of 196 people at five US sites, compared with 24-hour ambulatory blood pressure measurement: 65.8% sensitivity and 90.0% specificity for screening, and 78.4% and 90.9% in the confirmatory test (48 participants). A feasibility study; it does not replace the cuff, and many cases are missed.
ai_technology: AI-PPG-ACC-HTN (photoplethysmography and accelerometer)
organization: Google Research

evidence.tested: A prospective study of 196 participants at five US sites compared smartwatch screening with 24-hour ambulatory blood pressure monitoring: 65.8% sensitivity and 90.0% specificity, with 78.4% and 90.9% in a confirmatory subgroup of 48.
evidence.unknown: The authors call it early feasibility research; the smartwatch does not replace a cuff, many true cases are missed, the confirmatory subgroup is small, and generalizability is unclear.
evidence.ai_role: A 1-D convolutional network pretrained with self-supervised contrastive learning on PPG and accelerometer waveforms produced embeddings; a logistic regression output a hypertension probability.

title: AlphaFold-Multimer predicts 2,895 interactions among human mitochondrial proteins
summary: Texas A&M AgriLife Research screened 630,003 protein pairs from about 1,100 human mitochondrial proteins with AlphaFold-Multimer and identified 2,895 likely interactions, more than half not previously reported, giving 85 uncharacterized proteins their first probable partners. The paper appeared in Nature Communications on 25 August 2026 and the institutional release on 5 November. Lab experiments in yeast and human cells confirmed several of the partnerships; most predictions remain untested, and the disease links are potential targets, not established ones. Predictions are shared through the MitoMatch web tool.
ai_technology: AlphaFold-Multimer
organization: Texas A&M AgriLife Research; and Washington University School of Medicine in St. Louis

evidence.tested: AlphaFold-Multimer screened about 630,000 protein pairs; lab experiments in yeast and human cells confirmed several of the predicted partnerships, while the release does not say how many of the 2,895 were tested.
evidence.unknown: Only several predictions were confirmed, most remain unverified, the interactions are described as likely rather than established, and disease links are potential targets.
evidence.ai_role: AlphaFold-Multimer predicted pairwise interactions among mitochondrial proteins; the predictions were released as the MitoMatch web resource.

title: First 3D structure of a prokaryotic vault particle, with Claude
summary: Claude searched protein databases, designed DNA constructs, reduced purification from about three days to about 90 minutes, and processed cryo-EM data into an initial model in 34 hours. The result is a particle made of 96 copies of a bacteriophage protein, with about 25% more internal volume than the mammalian version. Its biological function is unknown; this is a preprint, and Claude made errors that humans corrected.
ai_technology: Claude
organization: Anthropic

evidence.tested: The 3D structure was determined by cryo-EM; cryo-EM confirmed the vault shape for four of seven particle-forming proteins, and fifteen altered protein versions were tested, with a reviewer checking the structure.
evidence.unknown: The biological function is unknown, vaults were made only in E. coli, and an unidentified pocket molecule resembling coenzyme A is unconfirmed.
evidence.ai_role: Claude searched protein databases, designed DNA constructs, optimized purification, and ran RELION cryo-EM processing to an initial model in 34 hours; it also made errors that humans corrected.

title: Agentic cheminformatics: new macrocycles from literature analysis
summary: An agent using Cheminformatics Skills for Antigravity collected thousands of compounds analogous to crizotinib and lorlatinib, analyzed 568, and proposed new rigidified macrocycles with synthesis routes in about an hour. The proposals are computational hypotheses that still need to be synthesized and validated.
ai_technology: Google Antigravity, Cheminformatics Skills
organization: Google DeepMind

evidence.tested: The source describes computational evaluation only: benchmarks of several machine learning architectures on four readouts with scaffold splits, and predicted potency; no synthesis or experimental validation is reported.
evidence.unknown: Every proposed design must still be synthesized and validated; the data are sparse and assay noise is high; the designs are testable hypotheses, not finished drugs.
evidence.ai_role: An agent searched literature for crizotinib and lorlatinib analogues, curated 568 compounds, ran matched molecular pair analysis, benchmarked models, and proposed macrocycles and synthesis routes.

title: Writing seen in PHerc. 306B for the first time in 2000 years
summary: Vesuvius Challenge awarded a $50K First Letters Prize for scroll PHerc. 306B, where the winning submission reached the 10-character target and the papyrology team agreed on a reading, tentatively a Greek phrase with parallels in Aristotle and Philodemus. Ink was detected by multiplying two models (TRACE v3B and a fine-tuned A-hn). Letters remain faint, the readable area is small, and the work relied on hundreds of hours of manual labeling.
ai_technology: ML ink-detection models (TRACE v3B, A-hn) with VC3D GrowPatch
organization: Vesuvius Challenge

evidence.tested: The reading was checked by the papyrology team, which agreed on the letters with the winning submission, and was compared against 25 community submissions and a 10-character target; the page describes no independent replication.
evidence.unknown: The reading is partial and uncertain, letters remain faint, training on machine-generated labels could compound errors (not assessed), and the Grand Prize is not yet awarded.
evidence.ai_role: Machine-learning ink-detection models (TRACE v3B and a fine-tuned A-hn) produced the ink maps; the readings and prize review were done by humans.

title: Evo 2 uses in-context learning to design de novo regulatory sequences with only tens of examples
summary: Arc Institute reports that Evo 2 designs functional regulatory sequences from 4 to 64 in-context examples without extra training, with 30-50% yield. Of nine AI-designed enhancers delivered by AAV to mice, seven drove detectable expression and two labeled layer 5 extratelencephalic neurons with 73% and 95% specificity. Results are bioRxiv preprints; in vivo work covers only layer 5 enhancers, and other designs (proteins, CRISPR loci, antibodies, phage genomes) are computational only.
ai_technology: Evo 2 (genomic language model); in-context learning; reinforcement learning post-training
organization: Arc Institute; Stanford University

evidence.tested: Nine AI-designed enhancers were delivered by AAV to mice: seven drove detectable expression and two labeled layer 5 extratelencephalic neurons with 73% and 95% specificity.
evidence.unknown: Only layer 5 enhancers were tested in vivo; the authors plan other cell types, and designs beyond enhancers (proteins, CRISPR loci, antibodies, phage genomes) are computational only.
evidence.ai_role: Evo 2 generated regulatory sequences from 4 to 64 in-context examples; reinforcement learning with predictive reward models sharpened cell-type specificity.

title: Claude's early progress in drug development
summary: Anthropic reports early results with six partners: a CAR T-cell receptor design about 70% shorter that enabled immune cells to produce about 10 times more receptors; about 35,000 antibody designs in one month, yielding 20 candidates; and a document review that found all 11 human-identified issues plus seven more in 89% less time. The work is mostly preclinical and reported by Anthropic.
ai_technology: Claude
organization: Anthropic

evidence.tested: Partner lab tests and a document review reported by Anthropic: a CAR T receptor design was tested in immune cells, antibody designs were screened for IgE binding, and a review of 1,061 pages was compared with 11 human-identified issues.
evidence.unknown: The work is mostly preclinical with no human tests; partner reports give limited methodological detail, and the page does not say whether the seven extra flags were confirmed.
evidence.ai_role: Claude proposed molecular and receptor designs, generated about 35,000 antibody designs, reviewed manufacturing documents, and drafted regulatory documents.

title: OpenAI presents three results in harmonic analysis, complexity, and quantum theory
summary: OpenAI announces results on local smoothing, a disproof of the exponential time hypothesis, and the construction of quantum field theories. The source presents these as research results to be understood with academic groups: physical artifacts are not yet public, and independent verification is not established here.
ai_technology: OpenAI internal models
organization: OpenAI

evidence.tested: The local-smoothing proof was formalized in Lean the day after the AI output; the refutation of the Exponential Time Hypothesis was verified in Lean and is being checked by an external group led by Impagliazzo, Paturi and Williams.
evidence.unknown: The physics result was not released; the external groups had not reported conclusions on the page.
evidence.ai_role: OpenAI internal models produced the proofs; external experts were asked to shepherd and explain the results.

title: Chest X-rays and AI for tuberculosis screening
summary: Nexus AI says it has deployed Google Research's chest X-ray AI as a certified diagnostic tool at about 40 facilities in six countries: more than 25,000 X-rays assessed by over 90 clinicians, with response times under 45 seconds. These are author-reported deployment figures, with no sensitivity or patient outcome data; WHO and FDA approvals are still in progress.
ai_technology: Foundation models for chest X-rays
organization: Google Research

evidence.tested: The post reports deployment figures (about 40 facilities, over 25,000 X-rays, over 90 clinicians) without sensitivity, specificity or patient outcome data from this deployment; it cites earlier peer-reviewed studies for performance.
evidence.unknown: Deployment-level accuracy and outcomes are not given, WHO prequalification and FDA clearance are not granted, and the facility count across countries is unclear.
evidence.ai_role: The AI analyzed chest X-rays and flagged TB-suggestive findings for triage in under 45 seconds; clinicians made final decisions.

title: ForTy 2020: global map of forest types at 10 meters
summary: A 10-meter map classifies each land area into six forest or land-use types (including primary forest, plantations, and tree crops), with an initial time series from 2017–2025. Validation across more than 9,000 sites identifies the correct type in 90% of cases and distinguishes forest from non-forest in 95%.
ai_technology: Satellite-image classification models
organization: Google DeepMind; Google Research, World Resources Institute, IIASA

evidence.tested: The map was validated at more than 9,000 random sites, where two trained experts checked high-resolution imagery to determine land type: correct forest type in 90% of cases and forest vs non-forest in 95%.
evidence.unknown: Per-class accuracy and regional breakdowns are not reported, the time series is early-release without separate validation, and results depend on the probability threshold chosen.
evidence.ai_role: A custom remote-sensing model trained on about 1.7 million labeled locations, using AlphaEarth embeddings, outputs probabilities for six forest and land-use classes.

title: AI-assisted ultrasound for dating pregnancy
summary: Prospective study of 385 pregnant women in Chicago and Nairobi: the model estimates gestational age from scans taken by minimally trained operators with a mean error of 4.18 days, non-inferior to the 4.48 days of expert sonographers. This is a non-inferiority result from only two sites, both relatively urban.
ai_technology: Ultrasound model for estimating gestational age
organization: Google Research

evidence.tested: A prospective multi-center study of 385 pregnant women at two sites (Chicago and Nairobi) compared AI gestational-age estimates from blind sweep scans by minimally trained operators with expert sonographer biometry: mean error 4.18 vs 4.48 days.
evidence.unknown: The source does not state the non-inferiority margin or confidence intervals; only two relatively urban sites and one commercial probe were used, and clinical trust and confidence safeguards are not validated.
evidence.ai_role: The model estimated gestational age from blind sweep ultrasound scans and ran live on mobile devices in clinics.

title: GPT-Rosalind agents connect genetic perturbations and neuronal signals
summary: Analysis of a CRISPR atlas of mouse brain cells identified differences between Tsc1 and Tsc2 and a possible relationship between DCTN1 and cholesterol regulation. Experts assessed the interpretations, but the proposed mechanisms remain hypotheses to be tested in new experiments.
ai_technology: GPT-Rosalind and distributed agents
organization: OpenAI; PerturbAI and Scripps Research

evidence.tested: Thousands of GPT-Rosalind agents reanalyzed an existing whole-brain CRISPR atlas; they reproduced findings from human analyses, and their novelty and value assessments aligned with blinded human experts.
evidence.unknown: The proposed biological mechanisms still need experiments to test them.
evidence.ai_role: Each agent investigated one gene disruption, searched the literature and proposed explanations; reports were combined into a reasoning atlas.

title: Claude designs binders against five scorpion neurotoxins
summary: In a mostly autonomous 64-hour campaign, Claude designed minibinders against five neurotoxins. External labs tested 211 designs, 17 of which met the criteria; the best (Cn2-B1 and Cn2-B2) had affinities in the low nanomolar range. Only recombinant toxins were tested, with no neutralization tests in cells or animals; Anthropic does not claim to have produced an antivenom.
ai_technology: Claude
organization: Anthropic

evidence.tested: External labs tested 211 designs by surface plasmon resonance: Adaptyv Bio in cell-free expression and Twist Bioscience in human kidney cells; a binder needed KD of 1 µM or tighter in every replicate at both labs and no CLEC12A signal, giving 17 binders. The two collaborating external laboratories tested candidates from the discovery project; this establishes direct testing rather than a separately established independent follow-up replication.
evidence.unknown: Only recombinant toxins were tested, with no neutralization in cells or animals; the authors do not know whether the binders neutralize venom and do not claim an antivenom; multitoxin designs failed.
evidence.ai_role: Claude selected toxin structures and hotspots, generated 318,484 designs, filtered and co-folded them, ran about 24 hours autonomously, then produced 180 selected designs after human follow-ups.

title: AI agents in the lab: aptamers and proteins designed in a closed loop
summary: AI agents designed DNA aptamers and protein binders, which were then tested in the lab over multiple rounds. Target success rates reached 33.5% for myoglobin and 42.1% for α-thrombin (98.5% specificity). The post summarizes three arXiv papers whose peer review is unconfirmed; it also reports initial failures.
ai_technology: AI agents with laboratory robots
organization: Google Research

evidence.tested: Agents ran three design-test-iterate rounds of DNA aptamers against myoglobin and alpha-thrombin in the lab, reaching 33.5% and 42.1% hit rates with 98.5% specificity for thrombin; protein binders against FAP were reported at single-digit nanomolar affinity.
evidence.unknown: Peer review of the cited arXiv papers is unconfirmed; there are two protein targets and three rounds; initial rounds failed, and protein expression adds steps to each loop.
evidence.ai_role: Agents designed and revised sequences across rounds and adjusted design rules after reading wet-lab data, under human oversight of protocols and robot runs.

title: Claude designs more efficient quantum circuits
summary: Claude designed circuits for eight basic operations (chemistry, optimization, physical simulation, and number theory), assessed by an automated verifier. In several cases they outperform the best published circuits; for example, a point addition used 17 times fewer gates at the cost of 12% more qubits. Key identities were checked with simulation and Lean; a memory shortcut in the decoder fails about once in 10,000 times.
ai_technology: Claude
organization: Anthropic

evidence.tested: An automated evaluator checked each circuit for correctness and scored qubits times gates; results were compared with published designs, divsteps was checked by simulation and Lean, and decoder memory was measured over 403 million simulated decodings.
evidence.unknown: The decoder memory shortcut fails about once in 10,000 runs; gains apply to individual primitives, not a full fault-tolerant machine; Claude was conservative and needed prompts to broaden its search.
evidence.ai_role: Claude wrote circuits as Python code and revised them in a closed loop with evaluator feedback, with no human input between rounds, and reconstructed branch information to reduce memory.

title: Searching for antimicrobial peptides with Google Antigravity
summary: An agentic workflow searched UniProt for antimicrobial candidates in Streptococcus pseudopneumoniae and found a 97-amino-acid bacteriocin with no homologues among manually reviewed Swiss-Prot proteins. This is a computational candidate now undergoing laboratory validation; no potency or toxicity data are available.
ai_technology: Google Antigravity (agentic platform)
organization: Google DeepMind

evidence.tested: Nothing was tested in the lab: the candidate's novelty was checked by BLAST against Swiss-Prot, its predicted structure was compared with a known bacteriocin fold, and its genomic context was examined; the wet-lab plan is underway with no results.
evidence.unknown: No potency or toxicity results exist; the wet-lab assays outcomes are unknown; the session covered a narrow sequence window in one species.
evidence.ai_role: An agent queried databases, filtered candidates, ran BLAST and structure comparisons, analyzed genomic neighborhoods, synthesized literature and drafted a wet-lab plan under researcher direction.

title: Earth AI for public health: geospatial models across five use cases
summary: The PDFM model increased the explained variance in MMR vaccination coverage from 16% to 22% across 146 counties on the US–Canada border, and improved weekly correct cholera-risk-area rankings in the DRC from 1.78 to 2.10. Gains for cardiovascular mortality and postpartum depression were small or not significant.
ai_technology: Population Dynamics Foundation Model (PDFM), TimesFM
organization: Google Research

evidence.tested: Five partner-led evaluations compared PDFM embeddings with baselines: MMR explained variance rose from 16% to 22% across 146 border counties and cholera Precision@5 improved from 1.78 to 2.10; cardiovascular gains were not significant.
evidence.unknown: Several results were non-significant or small, cholera gains were not significant at one or two weeks, and the authors cite static embeddings as a limitation.
evidence.ai_role: PDFM combines search trends, mobility, built-environment and environmental data into location embeddings used without task fine-tuning; for dengue it was paired with TimesFM 2.0.

title: SynthID Bio: watermarking for proteins and synthetic structures
summary: Methods insert a detectable signal into protein sequences and predicted structures. For binders designed against three targets (VEGF-A, SARS-CoV-2 RBD, and PD-L1), watermarked designs matched the others in success rate and affinity. This is a proof of concept that needs to be made more robust against tampering.
ai_technology: SynthID Bio, AlphaFold 3 (optimized component)
organization: Google DeepMind

evidence.tested: Wet-lab tests on three targets (VEGF-A, SARS-CoV-2 RBD, PD-L1), with Adaptyv Bio helping, showed watermarked designs matched unwatermarked ones in hit rate, affinity and diversity; the phage was tested only in bacterial cultures.
evidence.unknown: The watermark must become more robust against deliberate tampering, the bacteriophage work is early-stage, and the post says no single biosecurity measure is a silver bullet.
evidence.ai_role: SynthID Bio guided amino acid choice in a ProteinMPNN variant, adjusted predicted atomic coordinates, fine-tuned part of AlphaFold 3, and was integrated into Evo 2 to watermark a designed phage genome.

title: Catalysts without iridium or ruthenium for acidic oxygen evolution
summary: An AI-guided, human-supervised platform assessed 2,942 catalysts and identified complex palladium oxides. InMnPdOx maintained an overpotential below 0.5 V for more than 1,000 hours in sulfuric acid at 10 mA/cm². This is a preprint and laboratory result, without validation in a PEM electrolyzer.
ai_technology: Sequential learning, composition–property models, and LLMs
organization: Lila Sciences

evidence.tested: Lead catalysts were tested in 1 M H2SO4 at 10 mA/cm2: InMnPdOx kept overpotential below 0.5 V for over 1,000 hours; a retrospective benchmark compared the agent with Bayesian optimization and in-context language-model selection.
evidence.unknown: Testing in a full PEM electrolyzer is not reported, and 'stable' means overpotential under 0.5 V rather than a broader durability assessment.
evidence.ai_role: A sequential-learning agent with ML composition models, adaptive optimization and LLM reasoning ran a human-supervised closed loop with over 90% automation.

title: Claude identifies a new enzyme system: array-associated reverse transcriptases
summary: About 950 Claude agents searched a DNA-sequence database for 21 hours (210 million tokens) and flagged an uncharacterized enzyme system, found mostly in bacteriophages, with a DNA repeat array similar to CRISPR. Scientists performed the laboratory work; the function remains unknown, and the work is a preprint, not a peer-reviewed publication.
ai_technology: Claude (agents)
organization: Anthropic

evidence.tested: Human scientists expressed the protein in laboratory strains and characterized it biochemically and structurally; early experiments showed the array is expressed as distinct short RNAs.
evidence.unknown: The primary function of the enzyme system is unknown; findings are preliminary, and most Claude-proposed candidates are eliminated in follow-up review.
evidence.ai_role: About 950 agents used 210 million tokens over 21 hours to search DNA sequences, narrowing about 3,500 candidate systems to 20; one agent noticed the repeat array and filed a report.

title: RetroChimera: predicting small-molecule synthesis
summary: Published in Nature, the method combines a Transformer model (R-SMILES 2) and a template-based graph model (NeuralLoc) through a learned vote. In blind tests with expert chemists, 90% of complete routes were accepted, compared with 20–50% for the component models or a baseline, and nine of ten difficult targets were solved. Evaluation covered only ten targets; one wrong prediction invalidates an entire route.
ai_technology: RetroChimera (Transformer and template-based model)
organization: Microsoft Research

evidence.tested: Blind tests by PhD-level chemists rated individual steps and complete routes for ten difficult targets: 90% of RetroChimera routes were accepted, and nine of ten targets were solved, versus 20-50% for the component models or baseline.
evidence.unknown: The route-level evaluation covers only ten targets; one incorrect prediction invalidates a route; NeuralLoc is constrained on reactions outside its template library, and R-SMILES 2 may hallucinate.
evidence.ai_role: An ensemble of a Transformer (R-SMILES 2) predicting precursors and a graph neural network (NeuralLoc) selecting templates, combined by a learned rank-dependent vote.

title: Claude optimizes more than 30 open models for biology
summary: In just under four weeks, Claude optimized over 30 models for structure, protein design, and genomics. They were on average four times faster with a small accuracy loss, and nearly twice as fast with identical outputs. It also created a low-memory mode for systems over 10,000 tokens on a single GPU node. Design results are in silico only, and comparisons are internal to Anthropic.
ai_technology: Claude (in Claude Science)
organization: Anthropic

evidence.tested: Accelerated models were checked against their downstream tasks (for example structure prediction) and FlashPairformer kernels were compared with cuEquivariance (2.7-2.9x faster on triangle attention); design results are in silico with internal comparisons.
evidence.unknown: Design results have no wet-lab validation, large viral capsid predictions were incorrect, ColabFold kernels were not benchmarked, and the model is not reproducible.
evidence.ai_role: Claude wrote custom FlashPairformer kernels, optimized more than 30 models, built a low-memory Big mode, and ran autonomous protein binder design.

title: AlphaGenome Atlas: predictive map of human DNA variation
summary: A precomputed database of predicted molecular effects for about 9 billion possible single-letter changes in the human genome, generated by AlphaGenome. Researchers can access it free through a portal and API. The predictions are a research tool, do not replace experiments, and are not validated for clinical use.
ai_technology: AlphaGenome, AlphaGenome Variant Impact (AVI)
organization: Google DeepMind

evidence.tested: Validation described is the company's own testing of the AlphaGenome Variant Impact score on pathogenicity benchmarks, plus case studies: a DNM1 variant prioritized with GREGoR and 22% more non-coding associations in UK Biobank.
evidence.unknown: The page does not detail how individual predictions were checked; AlphaGenome is not validated or approved for clinical use.
evidence.ai_role: AlphaGenome predicted variant effects across cell types and tissues; these were precomputed for about 9 billion variants and combined with AlphaMissense into a single score.

title: OpenAI proposes a solution to the Navier–Stokes problem
summary: OpenAI announces a proof that three-dimensional solutions to the Navier–Stokes equations can develop a singularity in finite time and publishes a text formalized in Lean. This is the source's claim: this record does not establish community consensus, correctness of the artifacts, or recognition as a Millennium Prize problem.
ai_technology: OpenAI internal model
organization: OpenAI

evidence.tested: OpenAI shared an analytical proof and a Lean formalization that an initially smooth fluid at rest can develop a finite-time singularity under a smooth force with finite energy.
evidence.unknown: Not stated in the reviewed material
evidence.ai_role: An internal OpenAI model, described as more capable than GPT-6 Astra, produced the proof and the Lean formalization.

title: Codex agents perform measurements and calibrations on a six-qubit chip
summary: Connected to MIT EQuS lab software, GPT-5.6 Sol selected parameters, ran measurements, and calibrated a six-qubit superconducting chip, measuring its frequencies and coherence. The demonstration covers known procedures on real hardware; weak or noisy signals sometimes required expert assistance, and no new physical property was demonstrated.
ai_technology: GPT-5.6 Sol and Codex
organization: OpenAI; and MIT EQuS

evidence.tested: Connected to MIT EQuS lab software, GPT-5.6 Sol ran measurements on an uncalibrated six-qubit chip of a standard type, chose parameters, operated the hardware and analyzed results.
evidence.unknown: Not assessed: the technical case study with the detailed results was not read.
evidence.ai_role: GPT-5.6 Sol in Codex ran routine measurement workflows with measurement-specific skills provided by the researcher.

title: Claude formalizes Fermat's theorem in Lean
summary: A proof of Fermat's Last Theorem fully machine-verified in Lean: Claude produced most of it independently over 11 days, with about 13 million lines and 29,500 intermediate theorems, and a comparator confirms that its statement matches Mathlib's. It follows a simplified version of Wiles's proof, uses Mathlib and parts of an Imperial College project, and is probably longer than necessary.
ai_technology: Claude, Lean
organization: Anthropic

evidence.tested: The proof was checked by Lean using only standard axioms; a comparator tool confirmed the theorem statement matches Mathlib's, and mathematician Kevin Buzzard reviewed it.
evidence.unknown: The proof is about 13 million lines and likely much longer than needed; it follows a simplified version of Wiles's proof and is presented as verification, not new mathematics.
evidence.ai_role: Dozens of agents worked for 11 days on the Prove2Me platform, producing about 30,300 computer-verified theorems; humans gave occasional high-level instructions.

title: WeatherNext 3: a global AI model for weather forecasting
summary: A model that learns from real-time geostationary satellite data and produces hourly forecasts, at resolutions down to 5 km for temperature and humidity (about five times finer than WeatherNext 2). For short-term precipitation, Google reports improvements of up to 60% over NASA's IMERG. These are ‘up to’ figures from Google's evaluations, with an independent ranking by Brightband.
ai_technology: WeatherNext 3
organization: Google DeepMind; and Google Research

evidence.tested: Precipitation forecasts were scored with CRPS against baselines: gains of up to 60% over IMERG, 30% over MRMS and 10% over rain gauges for early lead times; independent live evaluations by Brightband ranked the model.
evidence.unknown: The 'up to' figures lack full test setup, longer-range gains are largest where forecasts are weak, and the atmosphere retains unpredictability.
evidence.ai_role: The model ingests live geostationary satellite data and historical analyses, trains on station observations and produces gridded fields, cyclone tracks and station-level forecasts.

title: Claude designs protein binders for 15 targets
summary: After an initial prompt, Claude selected binding sites, used design and folding models, and chose candidates, with success on 14 of 15 targets. Of 1,320 designs, 354 bound, for rates of 22–35% versus a typical 10–15%. None of the 90 designs for the maltose-binding protein worked. External labs ran the tests.
ai_technology: Claude (Mythos Preview and Opus 4.8)
organization: Anthropic

evidence.tested: External labs (Adaptyv Bio and Twist Bioscience) produced and tested the designs: 354 of 1,320 designs bound, with hit rates of 22-35% versus a typical 10-15%; none of 90 designs for maltose-binding protein bound. The collaborating external laboratories performed candidate production and binding assays within the discovery project; separate independent follow-up replication is not established by this account.
evidence.unknown: Anthropic plans further characterization to confirm hit rates and affinities; BBF-14 affinities are modest, GDF-8 data were inconclusive and excluded, and the TNFa result is unexplained.
evidence.ai_role: Claude chose binding sites, generated candidate structures and sequences by orchestrating structure, sequence and co-folding models, ran in silico optimization and chose candidates.

title: RAI-939: an autonomous-lab alloy tested with a torch
summary: Radical AI reports that AI-generated hypotheses and an autonomous lab produced new alloys, which were then tested by Purdue Applied Research Institute. During one minute under a torch, RAI-939 gained 0.25% mass while C103 lost 32%. This is a company announcement without peer review or replication details; scaling production remains to be developed.
ai_technology: AI-generated hypotheses and autonomous laboratory
organization: Radical AI; and Purdue Applied Research Institute

evidence.tested: A head-to-head torch test run by Purdue Applied Research Institute: RAI-939 gained 0.25% mass in one minute while C103 lost 32%; the page describes no repeated trials, sample sizes or replication.
evidence.unknown: Replication details are missing, the test articles were small, and production scaling is still to be developed.
evidence.ai_role: AI-generated hypotheses and an autonomous lab produced over 300 novel materials over 16 weeks.

title: WeatherNext Cyclones: forecasting cyclones one day earlier
summary: Three-day forecasts match what earlier models achieved at two days: about 100 km trajectory error and 11 knots intensity error, compared with ECMWF-ENS and HWRF. The work is with the National Hurricane Center, CIRA, and the Met Office. The comparison uses historical 2023–2024 cyclones; why results are good at 28 km remains an open question.
ai_technology: WeatherNext Cyclones
organization: Google DeepMind

evidence.tested: Historical cyclones from 2023-2024 were benchmarked deterministically and probabilistically against ECMWF-ENS (track) and HWRF (intensity): three-day errors matched earlier two-day forecasts; a 2025 storm is cited only as an anecdote.
evidence.unknown: Why the model is accurate at 28 km resolution is an open question; the 'extra day' is an average dependent on the chosen benchmarks, and the evaluation window is slightly unclear.
evidence.ai_role: A single model using Functional Generative Networks produced track, intensity and wind-structure ensembles of up to 1,000 members.

title: OpenAI presents ten results in mathematics and theoretical computer science
summary: OpenAI announces ten results on codes, non-sofic groups, arithmetic circuits, quantum games, lattices, and combinatorics, accompanied, according to the source, by Lean certificates. This record groups one announcement; it does not mean this collection independently verified ten results.
ai_technology: OpenAI internal model
organization: OpenAI

evidence.tested: Each of the ten arguments was prepared into a manuscript by humans with the model and then formalized by the model in a Lean certificate.
evidence.unknown: Not stated in the reviewed material
evidence.ai_role: An internal version of Astra found the results; humans prepared the manuscripts with the same model.

title: A quantum computer that learns from its own errors
summary: A reinforcement-learning agent tuned over 1,000 control parameters on the Willow chip: logical stability was 3.5 times higher under injected drift, with a further 20% reduction in logical error after expert calibration, and error below one per thousand cycles in the surface code. Drift was injected artificially, and scalability was shown only in simulation; published in Nature.
ai_technology: Reinforcement learning for quantum control
organization: Google Quantum AI

evidence.tested: On the Willow chip, drift was injected artificially into control parameters; RL steering raised logical stability 3.5-fold, and a further 20% error reduction followed expert calibration; scalability was tested only in simulation.
evidence.unknown: The drift was artificial rather than natural; scalability evidence is simulation-only; environmental decoherence cannot be fully prevented; fuller results need tighter integration.
evidence.ai_role: An RL agent used error-detection events as a learning signal and adjusted frequencies, amplitudes and phases during the computation without stopping it for recalibration.

title: FastNet: physically realistic AI forecasts from the Met Office
summary: Trained with a loss function that preserves energy across scales, it reaches a mean squared error equal to the Met Office global model and exceeds it on some metrics, with more realistic storm cores in Hurricane Ian and Storm Ciarán. The announcement gives no figures, covers only two extreme cases, and the system is not operational.
ai_technology: FastNet (spherical-harmonic loss)
organization: Met Office; and Alan Turing Institute

evidence.tested: FastNet was compared with the Met Office global model on verification measures (RMSE and some other metrics, shown only in a figure) and qualitatively on Hurricane Ian and Storm Ciaran storm cores.
evidence.unknown: The model is not operational, the text gives no numerical results, only two extreme cases are described, and comparable skill does not establish the same validation as the Global Model.
evidence.ai_role: A machine-learning weather model co-developed with the Alan Turing Institute, trained with a modified spherical-harmonic loss to keep energy across scales physically realistic.

title: A1: deep learning identifies an antibiotic candidate against gonorrhea
summary: A screen of about six million compounds found candidates active against resistant Neisseria gonorrhoeae. A1 reduced bacteria in animal models, and proteomics, genetics, and biochemistry confirmed its target, alanine racemase. These are preclinical results, published in Science Translational Medicine.
ai_technology: Deep learning for molecule screening
organization: MIT; Karolinska Institutet, and collaborators

evidence.tested: Phenotypic screen of 38,650 molecules trained a graph neural network, which screened about 6 million compounds; 213 were validated experimentally, 83 inhibited growth. Two hits were tested in vitro against multidrug-resistant strains, by proteomics (alanine racemase target), in a vagina-on-a-chip model and in a mouse vaginal infection model.
evidence.unknown: Not reported (the abstract describes the in vivo and organ-chip results as showing only early promise).
evidence.ai_role: A graph neural network trained on phenotypic screening data, used to virtually screen the compound library before experimental validation.

title: Genetic reanalysis assisted by o3 contributes to 18 diagnoses
summary: Among 376 unresolved cases, o3 Deep Research proposed explanations reviewed by specialists: 18 diagnoses were clinically confirmed, seven of which had already been established elsewhere but were missing from local records. This was a retrospective study across heterogeneous cohorts, without a measure of time saved or effect on care; clinicians made the decisions.
ai_technology: o3 Deep Research
organization: OpenAI; Boston Children’s Hospital, and Harvard University

evidence.tested: Retrospective multicohort reanalysis of 376 unresolved cases; a diagnosis required a pathogenic or likely pathogenic variant confirmed in a CLIA-certified lab and returned to families, and seven rediscoveries were also reported.
evidence.unknown: The abstract states that the retrospective design motivates prospective multicenter evaluation with predefined endpoints, calibration reporting and comparator baselines.
evidence.ai_role: An LLM ingested clinician notes, HPO terms and a filtered variant table and proposed candidate hypotheses for expert adjudication under ACMG/AMP criteria; experts made the classifications.

title: An AI system improves a Chan–Lam coupling reaction
summary: The system identified TEMPO as a useful additive for coupling primary sulfonamides; chemists reproduced yield improvements in 11 of 14 substrate pairs at bench scale. The work retains human supervision and specialized infrastructure; independent reproducibility and generalization remain to be checked.
ai_technology: GPT-5.4 and Maria
organization: OpenAI; and Molecule.one

evidence.tested: Over two cycles in an automated lab, yields improved for 88% of boronic acids and 83% of sulfonamides tested (mean 16.6% to 25.2%); human chemists repeated representative reactions at bench scale, with higher yields for 11 of 14 substrate pairs.
evidence.unknown: Not stated in the reviewed material
evidence.ai_role: GPT-5.4 connected to Molecule.one Maria proposed, designed and analyzed experiments; humans steered prompts, selected proposals, made limited corrections and validated the final result.

title: ElectrolyteGPT can generate new formulations for battery development
summary: University of Chicago researchers trained a GPT model with a new notation (fLine) to generate complete battery electrolyte formulations, including solvent ratios, salt concentrations and temperature. Several AI-proposed compositions were synthesized and, per the release, performed on par with the state of the art in lithium metal batteries. No cycling or capacity figures are given, the work is early, and generated candidates still need experimental verification.
ai_technology: ElectrolyteGPT (GPT with fLine notation)
organization: University of Chicago Pritzker School of Molecular Engineering

evidence.tested: Generated solvents and formulations were synthesized and fabricated, found to meet the target property requirements, and enabled long-term cycling in anode-free lithium metal batteries.
evidence.unknown: The release states the limited data and parameter set, and that the results matched but did not exceed top existing electrolytes; the abstract states no limitations.
evidence.ai_role: A transformer-based generative model (ElectrolyteGPT) generated candidate solvents and electrolyte formulations conditioned on property targets.

title: OpenAI presents a disproof of the unit-distance conjecture
summary: OpenAI presents a construction of planar point configurations with more unit-distance pairs than predicted by the Erdős conjecture. The announcement says mathematicians outside the team checked it and provides a complementary explanation; this record checks the source, not an independent reconstruction of the proof.
ai_technology: OpenAI internal model
organization: OpenAI

evidence.tested: The proof was checked by a group of external mathematicians, who also wrote a companion paper explaining the argument.
evidence.unknown: Not stated in the reviewed material
evidence.ai_role: A general-purpose internal OpenAI reasoning model produced the proof while being evaluated on Erdős problems.

title: Co-Scientist: repurposed drugs against liver fibrosis
summary: In Gary Peltz's Stanford lab, two of the three existing drugs proposed by Co-Scientist blocked fibrosis and promoted regeneration in human liver cells, while Peltz's own two choices showed no benefit. The anticancer drug vorinostat blocked 91% of a damage response that can lead to scarring. Cell experiments only; published in Advanced Science.
ai_technology: Co-Scientist
organization: Google DeepMind; and Stanford

evidence.tested: The anti-fibrotic efficacy and toxicity of 25 drugs were assessed serially in human liver organoids grown in microwells; Co-Scientist's candidates were tested in cells alongside the authors' own picks.
evidence.unknown: Not reported.
evidence.ai_role: The AI co-scientist multi-agent system proposed three candidate drugs with reasoning, and helped direct their experimental characterization.

title: Co-Scientist and aging: metabolism and the integrated stress response
summary: Calico Life Sciences used Co-Scientist to formulate the hypothesis that metabolism regulates the cellular integrated stress response, refined experiments with the tool, and reports new findings. The post gives no numerical data, and the results have not yet been published or peer reviewed.
ai_technology: Co-Scientist
organization: Google DeepMind; and Calico Life Sciences

evidence.tested: Calico reports that experiments were run with the Co-Scientist hypothesis and produced new findings; the post does not describe the experiments, assays or results.
evidence.unknown: Not reported (the results are not yet published; the team plans to publish them).
evidence.ai_role: Co-Scientist generated the hypothesis that metabolism regulates the integrated stress response, and was used to refine experimental design.

title: Co-Scientist and mechanisms of metabolic steatohepatitis (MASH)
summary: Filippo Menolascina (Edinburgh) used Co-Scientist to search the literature for combinations of MASH therapies. The tool proposed the NLRP3 inflammasome as a link between inflammation and metabolism, and the post says the hypothesis was later tested experimentally. No numbers are given; the drug combinations were suggested for testing, not demonstrated.
ai_technology: Co-Scientist
organization: Google DeepMind; and University of Edinburgh

evidence.tested: The article says the NLRP3 hypothesis was later experimentally verified but does not describe the experiments, who carried them out, or their results.
evidence.unknown: Not reported (the article does not state limitations or whether the work is published).
evidence.ai_role: Co-Scientist searched the literature, proposed drug combinations for MASH therapy and proposed the NLRP3 inflammasome as the link between inflammation and metabolism.

title: Co-Scientist: genetic factors to rejuvenate cells
summary: Omar Abudayyeh and Jonathan Gootenberg used Co-Scientist to search tens of thousands of papers, obtaining over 20 proposed genetic factors for reversing cellular aging, a couple of which were validated in the lab, and reducing analysis of genetic-screening data from six months to a few days. The post gives no sample size or peer review status.
ai_technology: Co-Scientist
organization: Google DeepMind

evidence.tested: Lab tests validated a couple of the more than 20 proposed genetic factors, which pushed cells toward a younger state; the experiments and exact number are not described.
evidence.unknown: Not reported (the post gives no sample size or peer-review status and contains only the investigators' quotes).
evidence.ai_role: Co-Scientist scanned tens of thousands of papers, proposed genetic factors for reversing cellular aging and analysed screening data alongside the literature.

title: WeatherNext and Hurricane Melissa: earlier warning in Jamaica
summary: WeatherNext forecast a Category 5 landfall in Jamaica five days ahead with 80% probability, rising to nearly 100% at three days. According to the post, it was the best single model for track and intensity in the National Hurricane Center's 2025 verification report, which used it alongside its HAFS model. The post gives no numerical comparisons; rapid intensification remains very hard to predict.
ai_technology: WeatherNext
organization: Google DeepMind

evidence.tested: The National Hurricane Center's 2025 annual verification report found WeatherNext the top-performing individual model for track and intensity; the Melissa forecast is presented as a single case.
evidence.unknown: The page notes that predicting rapid intensification is very difficult and that Weather Lab is experimental; no dedicated limitations section.
evidence.ai_role: WeatherNext, an AI weather model with 50-member ensembles, forecast the Hurricane Melissa landfall alongside physics-based HAFS and was used by NHC forecasters.

title: MatterSim and tantalum phosphide as a good heat conductor
summary: A candidate identified with MatterSim-v1, tetragonal tantalum phosphide, was synthesized and showed thermal conductivity of 152 W/m/K in the best samples, close to silicon. MatterSim-v1 inference is 3–5 times faster, and the new multi-task model MatterSim-MT predicts energies, forces, and properties. Battery and other property results are predictions, not experimental confirmations.
ai_technology: MatterSim-v1 and MatterSim-MT
organization: Microsoft Research

evidence.tested: A MatterSim-v1 screen of over 240,000 candidates picked tetragonal tantalum phosphide, which was synthesized at UT Dallas and whose thermal conductivity was measured at UIUC, reaching 152 W/m/K in the best samples; the page does not describe the measurement method or number of samples.
evidence.unknown: The page states that practical constraints such as mass density, elemental abundance and environmental stability are needed, but does not say whether TaP meets them.
evidence.ai_role: MatterSim-v1 machine-learning interatomic potentials estimated phonon thermal conductivity to screen candidates before experimental validation; MatterSim-MT is a multi-task model.

title: REDMOD: pancreatic cancer signals in CT scans taken before diagnosis
summary: Among nearly 2,000 abdominal CT scans originally considered normal, an AI radiomics model identified 73% of prediagnostic pancreatic cancers, with a median lead time of about 16 months. Validation included images from multiple institutions and protocols. This analysis used scans taken before diagnosis; clinical benefit and false positives in practice still need prospective evaluation.
ai_technology: REDMOD (Radiomics-based Early Detection Model)
organization: Mayo Clinic

evidence.tested: REDMOD was trained on 969 patients from a multi-institutional cohort and tested on an independent set of 493 patients (63 pre-diagnostic), with external specificity checks on further datasets and a comparison with radiologists; AUC 0.82 and 73.0% sensitivity, versus 38.9% for radiologists.
evidence.unknown: The article states that prospective validation in high-risk cohorts is the necessary next step; no explicit limitations section.
evidence.ai_role: A fully automated radiomics framework with AI segmentation and an ensemble classifier on a 40-feature signature from standard-of-care CT scans.

title: GPT-5.5 and a proof about Ramsey numbers
summary: OpenAI reports that an internal version of GPT-5.5, with a purpose-built scaffold, found a proof of a known asymptotic result on off-diagonal Ramsey numbers, then verified in Lean. The announcement appeared with the model launch on April 23, 2026; the full proof is in a separate PDF now linked. Page rechecked November 12, 2026: the text matches.
ai_technology: GPT-5.5 (internal version)
organization: OpenAI

evidence.tested: GPT-5.5 found a proof of an asymptotic fact about off-diagonal Ramsey numbers, later verified in Lean.
evidence.unknown: Not stated in the reviewed material
evidence.ai_role: An internal version of GPT-5.5 with a custom harness found the proof.

title: Theoretical physics with Claude: the Sudakov shoulder in the C parameter
summary: Physicist Matthew Schwartz (Harvard) guided Claude Opus 4.5 through a resummation calculation for e+e− collisions, producing a paper with a new factorization theorem and testable predictions against data in about two weeks. Schwartz checked every step; the model claimed checks it had not done and made errors.
ai_technology: Claude Opus 4.5
organization: Anthropic

evidence.tested: Results are validated against EVENT2 Monte Carlo simulations, with analytic curves matching the histograms; the paper does not describe a comparison with experimental data, and the author checked each step, with GPT and Gemini cross-checking the written calculations.
evidence.unknown: The paper does not describe comparison with experimental data (the author mentions a follow-up project for this); the author states that LLMs cannot yet do original theoretical physics autonomously and that the work needed expert evaluation.
evidence.ai_role: Claude Opus 4.5, run through Claude Code, performed the calculations including the factorization derivation, numerical analysis, simulations and manuscript preparation, under physicist supervision.

title: GPT-5.2 Pro extends a scattering-amplitude result to gravitons
summary: Building on work on gluons, GPT-5.2 Pro helped derive formulas for nonzero single-minus gravitational amplitudes in a special semi-collinear regime. The authors report analytical verification and checks against known physical limits; this is a theoretical preprint without experimental confirmation.
ai_technology: GPT-5.2 Pro
organization: OpenAI; and academic collaborators

evidence.tested: The preprint derives explicit formulas for single-minus graviton tree amplitudes in the half-collinear regime and shows they follow from symmetry principles and recursion relations; no experimental test is described.
evidence.unknown: The page calls it a small step towards reconciling quantum mechanics with general relativity.
evidence.ai_role: Researchers used GPT-5.2 Pro to help find the result; the paper is authored by named physicists on behalf of OpenAI.

title: GPT-5.2 proposes a formula for nonzero gluon amplitudes
summary: GPT-5.2 conjectured a formula for gluon scattering amplitudes with a single negative helicity in a special semi-collinear regime. An internal model produced a proof that the authors analytically verified; the announcement describes a preprint, not experimental confirmation.
ai_technology: GPT-5.2 Pro
organization: OpenAI; and academic collaborators

evidence.tested: The arXiv abstract reports that the gluon formula satisfies several consistency conditions, including Weinberg's soft theorem, and that the formula is restricted to half-collinear configurations; no experimental test is described.
evidence.unknown: Not reported (the abstract states no limitations beyond the restricted half-collinear and complexified-momentum setting).
evidence.ai_role: GPT-5.2 conjectured the formula; an internal model produced a proof that the authors verified analytically.

title: Gemini Deep Think on research problems in mathematics, physics, and computer science
summary: The Aletheia mathematical agent scored up to 90% on IMO-ProofBench Advanced and independently solved four open Erdős questions; work with experts covered 18 research problems, including a disproof of a submodular optimization conjecture. Its score on doctoral-level problems falls to about 38–46%; no result is claimed as a breakthrough, and the papers were submitted to journals.
ai_technology: Gemini Deep Think, Aletheia agent
organization: Google DeepMind

evidence.tested: Aletheia was evaluated on IMO-ProofBench Advanced (about 90%, human experts graded), an internal PhD-level benchmark (about 46%), a semi-autonomous run over 700 open Erdős problems (four autonomous solutions), and expert collaborations; Level 2 papers were submitted to journals.
evidence.unknown: The article states that no Level 3 or Level 4 results are claimed; the abstract states no limitations, and the PhD-level score falls to about 38-46%.
evidence.ai_role: Aletheia, a math research agent built on Gemini Deep Think, generated, verified and revised proofs and used search, with varying autonomy across projects.

title: Fel's conjecture proved and verified in Lean
summary: Axiom Prover generated a proof of Fel's conjecture on syzygies of numerical semigroups, verified in Lean 4 with Mathlib, without hints, lemmas, or manual corrections after the run began. This is a case study and an unreviewed preprint, with no data on attempts or time taken.
ai_technology: Axiom Prover, Lean
organization: Axiom Math

evidence.tested: The proof of Fel's conjecture was generated by AxiomProver with no hints, lemmas or manual corrections after kickoff and checked by Lean 4 with Mathlib; the formalization is publicly available and the mathematical results appear in a human-written arXiv preprint.
evidence.unknown: The authors state the limiting factor is often the quality of the shared library (Mathlib), and the post describes a single case study with no claim about automating research.
evidence.ai_role: AxiomProver translated the statement into Lean, generated intermediate lemmas and assembled the complete Lean proof.

title: GPT-5 reduces the cost of cell-free protein synthesis
summary: A cycle between GPT-5 and a robotic lab explored over 36,000 compositions and reduced protein-production cost by 40% compared with the previous baseline. This is an experimental result in one CFPS setup; it does not establish the same reduction for other proteins, scales, or facilities.
ai_technology: GPT-5
organization: OpenAI; and Ginkgo Bioworks

evidence.tested: Over six rounds in a cloud laboratory, the system tested more than 36,000 reaction compositions on 580 plates and reached a 40% lower protein production cost (57% lower reagent cost).
evidence.unknown: Not stated in the reviewed material
evidence.ai_role: GPT-5 proposed and analyzed experiments in a closed loop with Ginkgo Bioworks automation.

title: DinoTracker: AI classifies dinosaur footprints
summary: An unsupervised model trained on nearly 2,000 fossil footprints and millions of simulated variations identifies eight features of variation and agrees with experts about 90% of the time. Some tracks over 200 million years old resemble bird feet, which could suggest bird origins tens of millions of years earlier. The interpretation is open: they could be early dinosaurs whose feet happened to look similar.
ai_technology: DinoTracker (unsupervised model)
organization: Helmholtz-Zentrum Berlin; and University of Edinburgh

evidence.tested: An unsupervised variational autoencoder was trained on 1,974 fossil footprints; after labeling, its groupings agreed with published expert identifications in 80-93% of cases (the press release says about 90%).
evidence.unknown: The interpretation is open: the tracks could be early dinosaurs whose feet resembled birds' feet; the study states no limitations section.
evidence.ai_role: An unsupervised disentangled variational autoencoder found eight shape-variation features without prior labels, and predicted which dinosaur made each track.

title: AnomalyMatch finds over 1,300 unusual objects in the Hubble archive
summary: The neural network scanned about 100 million cutouts from the Hubble Legacy Archive in roughly two and a half days: nearly 1,400 anomalies were flagged and over 1,300 confirmed, including more than 800 not previously documented in the literature (mergers, lenses, and jellyfish galaxies). AI only ranks candidates; the two counts are not explained, and no false-positive rate is given.
ai_technology: AnomalyMatch (neural network)
organization: ESA; and ESA-Hubble

evidence.tested: The neural network screened about 100 million Hubble Legacy Archive cutouts, and the authors personally inspected the top-ranked sources; more than 1,300 were confirmed as true anomalies, of which more than 800 were not previously documented; no false-positive rate is given.
evidence.unknown: The release gives no false-positive rate, does not state how many candidates were inspected, notes that several dozen objects defied classification, and says expert review is still required.
evidence.ai_role: AnomalyMatch, a neural network, screened the archive and ranked candidate anomalies for expert inspection.

title: Claude in biology labs: Biomni, MozzareLLM, and others
summary: Anthropic describes three cases: Biomni (Stanford) completed a GWAS analysis in 20 minutes in an initial trial and suggested new transcription factors in embryonic development; MozzareLLM (MIT and Whitehead) interprets gene clusters from CRISPR screens; a third lab is still testing. This is an Anthropic account without independent evaluation; some figures are estimates.
ai_technology: Claude (Biomni, MozzareLLM)
organization: Anthropic

evidence.tested: Biomni's case studies (GWAS analysis, cloning design blind-evaluated against a postdoc, embryonic-tissue cell analysis) were checked by the Biomni team, citing a bioRxiv preprint; MozzareLLM was assessed qualitatively by its lab, with no quantitative benchmark.
evidence.unknown: The article says the validation is not independent, some figures are estimates (such as the three-week human comparison), and Biomni cannot yet do everything out of the box.
evidence.ai_role: A Claude-powered agent (Biomni) analysed GWAS and embryonic cell data and suggested transcription factors; a Claude-powered system (MozzareLLM) interprets gene clusters from CRISPR screens.

title: A double-Lambda hypernucleus of boron-13 found with deep learning
summary: Neural networks selected images from the J-PARC E07 emulsion plates; microscopy and kinematic analysis then confirmed an event as a double-Lambda hypernucleus of boron-13. The discovery comes from analysis of 0.2% of the emulsions and is based on a single event; published in Nature Communications.
ai_technology: Deep learning for nuclear-emulsion analysis
organization: RIKEN; and J-PARC E07 collaboration

evidence.tested: Neural networks pre-selected candidate images from 0.2% of the J-PARC E07 emulsion data; microscopy and detailed kinematic analysis then confirmed one event as a boron-13 double-Lambda hypernucleus.
evidence.unknown: Only one event is confirmed; the estimate of more than 2,000 events in the full dataset is an extrapolation from the detection rate, and the article has no limitations section.
evidence.ai_role: Deep learning networks trained to recognize double-strangeness signatures selected candidate images for microscopic examination.

title: NOAA puts three AI-based global models into operation
summary: AIGFS (retrained from GraphCast) uses up to 99.7% less computing than GFS (a 16-day forecast in about 40 minutes); AIGEFS has skill comparable to GEFS with 9% of the computing; and HGEFS (62 hybrid members) outperforms GEFS and AIGEFS on most metrics. Cyclone intensity worsened in AIGFS v1.0; the announcement gives no numerical scores.
ai_technology: AIGFS, AIGEFS, and HGEFS (GraphCast-derived)
organization: NOAA

evidence.tested: The release describes initial or early testing and claims skill comparable to GEFS and better ensemble performance, but gives no metrics, verification datasets or time periods.
evidence.unknown: The release states that AIGFS v1.0 degraded tropical cyclone intensity forecasts, that AIGEFS ensemble spread is still being improved, and that HGEFS hurricane intensity is being improved.
evidence.ai_role: AI global models: AIGFS forecasts with up to 99.7% less compute; AIGEFS is a 31-member AI ensemble with 9% of the GEFS computing; HGEFS combines 31 GEFS and 31 AIGEFS members.

title: GPT-5 and molecular cloning: 79-fold greater efficiency
summary: In a cycle with Red Queen Bio, GPT-5 optimized a cloning protocol, introducing RecA and gp32 as a new mechanism: 2.6-fold improvement with the enzymatic reaction, 36-fold with transformation, and 79-fold when combined. This applies to the model system used, with scientists carrying out the protocols; reported by OpenAI.
ai_technology: GPT-5
organization: OpenAI

evidence.tested: Scientists carried out GPT-5-modified cloning protocols over several rounds; the final protocol recovered 79 times more sequence-verified clones for a fixed amount of input DNA than the baseline.
evidence.unknown: The work used a benign experimental system with a limited task scope.
evidence.ai_role: GPT-5 reasoned about the protocol and proposed modifications, including a RecA and gp32 mechanism; humans only ran the protocol and uploaded data.

title: Graph neural networks identify oxides for hydrogen production
summary: A model of oxygen-vacancy properties selected twelve oxides to test for thermochemical hydrogen production; about 80% were active in experiments. Some were comparable to or better than the baseline only under certain reactor conditions; further study and optimization are needed.
ai_technology: Graph neural networks for crystal defects
organization: Sandia National Laboratories; and HydroGEN collaborators

evidence.tested: Twelve metal oxides selected by the model for oxygen-vacancy properties were tested experimentally for thermochemical hydrogen production; about 80% were effective, and some matched or beat the state-of-the-art material only under certain reactor conditions.
evidence.unknown: The method so far covers only thermochemical hydrogen materials, the model needs more diverse training data and more precise calculations, and the page gives no baseline numbers.
evidence.ai_role: A graph neural network trained on first-principles calculations predicted oxygen-vacancy formation energies and screened materials from existing databases.

title: GPT-5.2 Pro and an open problem about learning curves
summary: GPT-5.2 Pro solved an open problem in statistical learning theory (learning curves are monotonic in the Gaussian case with known mean and unknown standard deviation), then extended it to higher dimensions. The authors checked the proof, including with outside experts. Reported by OpenAI.
ai_technology: GPT-5.2 Pro
organization: OpenAI

evidence.tested: The authors verified and transcribed the model's proofs of monotonicity of the maximum likelihood estimator's KL divergence for Gaussian and Gamma families, with no outside expert review described.
evidence.unknown: The guarantees cover only the listed well-specified parametric settings, and the reverse-KL result relies on a folklore trick; the page shows only the abstract.
evidence.ai_role: All results were derived by variants of GPT-5.2 Pro, with humans prompting for further results and verifying the proofs.

title: Heat-resistant crops: a hybrid photosynthesis enzyme
summary: At Michigan State University, AlphaFold predicted the 3D structure of glycerate kinase in a crop and a heat-loving alga. Replacing three flexible loops with rigid loops from the alga produced a hybrid that remained stable up to 65 °C. The enzyme has not yet been tested in whole plants.
ai_technology: AlphaFold
organization: Google DeepMind; and Michigan State University

evidence.tested: Hybrid glycerate kinase enzymes with three loops replaced by rigid loops from a heat-loving alga were tested in the lab, and one stayed stable up to 65 °C; whole-plant testing has not been done.
evidence.unknown: It is not yet known whether the hybrid enzyme improves heat resilience in a whole plant; the page does not say whether the AlphaFold-predicted structures were experimentally validated.
evidence.ai_role: AlphaFold predicted the enzyme's 3D structures, which were then used in molecular simulations to identify loops to modify.

title: The structure of the LDL protein apoB100
summary: At the University of Missouri, Zachary Berndsen and Keith Cassidy used AlphaFold to predict the structure of apoB100, the scaffold of LDL particles, and refined it using cryo-electron microscopy data. The result is a cage-like shell with a ribbon belt. The post gives no figures such as resolution and no clinical validation.
ai_technology: AlphaFold
organization: Google DeepMind; and University of Missouri

evidence.tested: Cryo-EM images were refined with AlphaFold2 predictions; the resulting apoB100 structure was compared with more than 200 intramolecular cross-links and showed close agreement, with subnanometre resolution in most regions.
evidence.unknown: The article states that clinical applications will take time and the structure's implications are not yet realized; it gives no resolution figures or clinical validation, and the abstract states that resolution is subnanometre only in most regions.
evidence.ai_role: AlphaFold2 generated the initial atomic-resolution structure predictions, which were refined against cryo-EM data.

title: Healthier bees: AlphaFold predicts vitellogenin's structure
summary: With the Norwegian University of Life Sciences, predicted structures of honeybee vitellogenin were confirmed by electron microscopy in July 2025; AlphaFold 3 helped study its interactions with other molecules. Early evidence suggests breeding times for resilient bees could fall from months to weeks, a still preliminary claim.
ai_technology: AlphaFold, AlphaFold 3
organization: Google DeepMind; and Norwegian University of Life Sciences

evidence.tested: AlphaFold-predicted vitellogenin structures were confirmed by electron microscopy in July 2025, per the post; the linked paper reports a cryo-EM structure of native honey bee vitellogenin, and the breeding-time claim comes from early trials.
evidence.unknown: The breeding-time benefit (months to weeks) is preliminary and not cited to a publication, and implications for other egg-laying species are possibilities, not established findings.
evidence.ai_role: AlphaFold 3 predicted the vitellogenin structures and helped study how it binds other molecules inside the bee.

title: popEVE: diagnosing rare developmental disorders
summary: Applied to about 30,000 patients with severe undiagnosed developmental disorders, it led to a diagnosis in about one-third of cases and identified variants in 123 previously unknown genes, 25 of which were independently confirmed by other labs. This is preliminary clinical use; further checks are needed before adoption, and the page gives no detailed metrics.
ai_technology: popEVE (variant-effect prediction model)
organization: Harvard Medical School

evidence.tested: popEVE was tested on documented variants and case studies, and applied to about 30,000 undiagnosed patients, leading to a diagnosis in about one-third; 123 novel gene candidates were identified, and 25 were independently confirmed by other labs.
evidence.unknown: The press article says popEVE will need further verification for safety and accuracy before wide clinical adoption, and gives no accuracy metrics; it is not yet in routine clinical use.
evidence.ai_role: A deep generative model extending EVE with a protein language model, producing a calibrated disease-likelihood score for each variant.

title: GPT-5 helps solve a 40-year-old problem about Nesterov's accelerated gradient
summary: Ernest Ryu (UCLA) proved why Nesterov's accelerated gradient method, introduced in 1983, remains stable despite the extra momentum that makes it faster. GPT-5's turning point was a rewrite of the equations: not correct as given, but with a structure Ryu then developed and proved himself, over about twelve hours across three days and after a dozen approaches. OpenAI's account says the model created no new mathematical tools and often produced plausible arguments that failed verification.
ai_technology: GPT-5
organization: OpenAI; and University of California, Los Angeles

evidence.tested: Not reported
evidence.unknown: OpenAI states GPT-5 often produced plausible but flawed arguments; its restructuring suggestion was not correct as written. The proof was developed and written by Ryu. Whether peer review will confirm it is not reported.
evidence.ai_role: Per OpenAI, GPT-5 suggested approaches and restructured equations; Ryu checked each idea and wrote the final proof. About twelve hours over three days and nearly a dozen approaches. GPT-5 is not a co-author.

title: Early experiments in accelerating science with GPT-5
summary: A collection of case studies with universities and national labs in mathematics, physics, biology, computer science, astronomy, and materials. Examples: it helped complete a proof of an Erdős problem with Sawhney and Sellke, reconstructed the SL(2,R) symmetry of the Kerr wave equation, and proposed an immunology mechanism later confirmed by Unutmaz's lab. Reported by OpenAI; experts supervised the work.
ai_technology: GPT-5 and GPT-5 Pro
organization: OpenAI

evidence.tested: The OpenAI page lists case studies, for example a mannose rescue experiment in T cells whose results matched GPT-5 predictions, and Erdos Problem 848, where authors turned a GPT-5 density estimate into a full proof.
evidence.unknown: OpenAI says the cases are curated illustrations, not a systematic sample. GPT-5 can invent citations, mechanisms or proofs, and expert oversight is essential. One case reproduced an earlier published proof without citing it.
evidence.ai_role: GPT-5 suggested ideas, mechanisms, literature links and experiments; scientists set questions, verified results and ran lab work. OpenAI says the model is not autonomous.

title: Kosmos: an AI scientist for autonomous discovery
summary: Each run reads about 1,500 papers and executes 42,000 lines of analysis code; outside scientists judged 79.4% of its conclusions accurate. Of seven discoveries, three reproduce results already obtained by humans and four are new. Limitations include spurious correlations, a cost of about $200 per run, and a six-month work gain estimated by beta users.
ai_technology: Kosmos (agents with a structured world model)
organization: Edison Scientific

evidence.tested: Independent scientists judged 79.4% of Kosmos's conclusions accurate; three discoveries reproduced findings from preprints or unpublished manuscripts that Kosmos did not access at runtime; the four new discoveries are wet-lab validation in progress, with one checked in an independent scRNA-seq dataset.
evidence.unknown: The authors state that Kosmos chases statistically significant but irrelevant findings, that about one in five statements is not accurate, and that the human time-saving estimates are intrinsically suspect.
evidence.ai_role: An AI scientist runs about 12-hour cycles of data analysis and literature search (about 1,500 papers and 42,000 lines of code per run), linked by a structured world model, and generates traceable reports; humans set the objectives.

title: AlphaEvolve on 67 math problems with Terence Tao
summary: Tested on 67 problems in analysis, combinatorics, geometry, and number theory, AlphaEvolve matched the best known solutions in most cases and improved them in several; in some cases it generalized finite instances into formulas valid for every input. Preprint not yet peer reviewed; source checked was only the team's article.
ai_technology: AlphaEvolve
organization: Google DeepMind; Terence Tao, and Javier Gomez-Serrano

evidence.tested: The system was run on 67 problems in analysis, combinatorics, geometry and number theory and compared with the best known solutions. It rediscovered the best known solutions in most cases and improved several.
evidence.unknown: The abstract and page state no explicit limitations, and no verification details or failure cases are given.
evidence.ai_role: An LLM-guided evolutionary coding agent proposed, tested and refined algorithmic constructions, sometimes combined with Deep Think and AlphaProof.

title: DeepSomatic: a neural network for somatic variants in tumors
summary: For insertions and deletions, it reaches 90% with Illumina data versus 80% for the best other tool, and over 80% with PacBio versus under 50%. In eight pediatric leukemia samples, it recovered known variants and flagged ten new ones that have not been independently validated. The tool and CASTLE dataset are open.
ai_technology: DeepSomatic (convolutional neural network)
organization: Google Research

evidence.tested: DeepSomatic was benchmarked against SomaticSniper, MuTect2, Strelka2 and ClairS on the CASTLE cell-line dataset with held-out chromosomes and genomes, across Illumina, PacBio and other platforms.
evidence.unknown: The benchmark uses research cell lines rather than patient tumors, the glioblastoma result rests on one sample, and the 10 new leukemia variants are not stated to be validated.
evidence.ai_role: A convolutional neural network applied to sequencing data converted to images separated germline, somatic and error signals to call tumor variants.

title: C2S-Scale: a model-generated cancer hypothesis confirmed in cells
summary: The 27-billion-parameter single-cell model, built on Gemma with Yale, predicted that silmitasertib would increase antigen presentation only in an immune-positive context. In human neuroendocrine cell models with low-dose interferon, the increase was about 50%. Validation is in cells only; the authors call this ‘a first step.’
ai_technology: C2S-Scale 27B (Gemma)
organization: Google DeepMind; and Yale

evidence.tested: The model's prediction that silmitasertib boosts antigen presentation with low-dose interferon was tested experimentally in human neuroendocrine cell models not seen in training, with a roughly 50% synergistic increase reported.
evidence.unknown: The article calls this an early first step, validation is in cell models only, and clinical use is not shown.
evidence.ai_role: The 27B single-cell language model C2S-Scale ran a dual-context virtual screen of over 4,000 drugs and generated the hypothesis.

title: Enterololin: AI helps clarify an antibiotic and its mechanism
summary: An AI screen of over 10,000 molecules identified enterololin, and DiffDock predicted its binding to LolCDE within minutes, confirmed by resistant E. coli mutants, RNA-seq, and CRISPR. The mechanism was clarified in about six months versus 18–24 with traditional methods. In mice, in Crohn's-like inflammation models, healing was faster than with vancomycin. Early stage; no human testing.
ai_technology: Machine-learning screening and DiffDock
organization: MIT

evidence.tested: Enterololin was tested in mouse Crohn's-like inflammation models against vancomycin, with resistant mutant sequencing, RNA-seq and CRISPR knockdown used to clarify its mechanism.
evidence.unknown: The source states it is early-stage development, no human data are reported, and clinical trials are not yet started.
evidence.ai_role: DiffDock predicted binding of enterololin to the LolCDE complex within minutes, guiding lab experiments on the mechanism.

title: New families of unstable singularities in fluid equations
summary: Physics-informed neural networks trained to near machine precision revealed a new family of unstable singularities (blow-ups) in three fluid-dynamics equations, with a clear pattern between blow-up speed and instability order for the incompressible porous-medium and Boussinesq equations. Work with Brown, NYU, and Stanford: a step toward computer-assisted proofs, not a proof; the Navier–Stokes problem remains open.
ai_technology: Physics-informed neural networks
organization: Google DeepMind; Brown University, NYU, and Stanford

evidence.tested: Physics-informed neural networks trained to near machine precision found unstable singularities, and the accuracy was assessed numerically against the governing equations.
evidence.unknown: The source states the initial conditions must be tuned with extreme precision, the scaling formula is empirical, Navier-Stokes remains open, and supplementary information is not yet available.
evidence.ai_role: Neural networks trained on the equation residuals, with a high-precision optimizer, located new families of unstable singularities, with humans supplying the mathematical insight.

title: First bacteriophage genomes designed by a genome language model
summary: The Arc Institute group used Evo to design genomes resembling that of phage ΦX174: of 285 designs, 16 yielded functional phages (67–392 mutations from the closest natural one; 13 had never-seen mutations). They infect only two E. coli strains; a cocktail overcame resistance in three evolved strains. bioRxiv preprint; peer review is unconfirmed.
ai_technology: Evo (genome language model)
