The weights are freely available to academic and nonprofit researchers. The press release gives no experimental figures, and performance claims come from the company.
ai_technology: Chroma (generative model)
organization: Generate:Biomedicines

evidence.tested: The Nature paper reports experimental characterization of 310 designed proteins and crystal structures of two designs matching the predicted structures (backbone RMSD about 1.0 Å); the press release itself describes no experiments and states no limitations.
evidence.unknown: The paper abstract states no limitations; the press release gives no experimental figures and its performance claims come from the company.
evidence.ai_role: A generative model samples protein structures and sequences and can be conditioned on specified properties or functions.

title: GraphCast: global 10-day weather forecasts
summary: It outperforms ECMWF’s HRES system on over 90% of 1,380 variables and test forecast lead times, and produces a 10-day forecast in under a minute on a single TPU. Comparison is limited to deterministic HRES; training uses ERA5 data.
ai_technology: GraphCast (graph neural network)
organization: Google DeepMind

evidence.tested: 10-day forecasts of hundreds of variables at 0.25° in under a minute; outperforms the most accurate operational deterministic systems on 90% of 1,380 verification targets; supports better tropical-cyclone, atmospheric-river and extreme-temperature prediction.
evidence.unknown: Comparison with ensemble systems is not described in the abstract.
evidence.ai_role: A machine-learning model trained directly on reanalysis data.

title: MetNet-3: short-range neural forecasts in Google products
summary: The model forecasts precipitation, temperature, wind and dew point up to 24 hours ahead at 1–4 km resolution, learning from about 1,000 stations, and outperforms HRRR and ENS in several regions. It operates in Google Search and the app in the United States and 27 European countries, with precipitation forecasts up to 12 hours. Preprint, no numerical values in the text and one case study.
ai_technology: MetNet-3
organization: Google Research; and Google DeepMind

evidence.tested: MetNet-3 was benchmarked against HRRR and ENS over the contiguous US for forecasts up to 24 hours, scored with CRPS; a single January 2019 case study is also shown.
evidence.unknown: The post has no limitations section; it notes operational coverage limited to the contiguous US and parts of Europe, hyperlocal wind results depend on test-station input, and the case study is a single example.
evidence.ai_role: A neural model forecasts precipitation, temperature, wind and dew point up to 24 hours ahead, learning from about 1,000 stations.

title: Meta AI: near-real-time image decoding from brain activity
summary: A three-part system (image encoder, brain encoder, decoder) reconstructs viewed images from magnetoencephalography signals at each time point, with signals better aligned to DINOv2 than the other models compared. Images remain imperfect; fMRI decodes better; the page gives no numerical metrics; preprint.
ai_technology: Magnetoencephalography decoder
organization: Meta AI

evidence.tested: MEG recordings from healthy volunteers viewing images were decoded at each time point; several pretrained image models were compared (signals aligned best with DINOv2), and MEG decoding was compared with fMRI. Participant and image counts not stated on the blog.
evidence.unknown: Generated images are imperfect: high-level features are often kept but low-level features are often wrong. MEG decoding is less precise than fMRI decoding.
evidence.ai_role: AI models built the image representations and generated the output images; volunteers supplied the brain recordings.

title: Vesuvius Challenge: first letters read from an unopened Herculaneum scroll
summary: For the first time, a complete word (‘porphyras’, purple) was read from inside a never-opened carbonized scroll; a model trained on crack patterns yielded 13 letters independently and unanimously annotated by papyrologists. The letters are faint and lack context; other readings are not ruled out.
ai_technology: Machine-learning models for ink detection
organization: Vesuvius Challenge

evidence.tested: A model trained on crack patterns produced 13 letters, which papyrologists independently annotated with varying confidence; the page links only to code and no paper.
evidence.unknown: The letters are faint and lack context, word boundaries are unclear, and the page states other readings are not ruled out and the papyrological team was still investigating.
evidence.ai_role: Machine-learning models trained on ink crackle patterns (and a second model with pseudo-labeling) read letters from the scroll.

title: EVEscape: predicting viral variants before they emerge
summary: Starting from January 2020, the tool predicted SARS-CoV-2 mutations with accuracy similar to experimental antibody-binding assays and ranked their prevalence better; it generalizes to HIV and influenza. Retrospective validation; prospective performance is not reported.
ai_technology: EVEscape
organization: Harvard Medical School; and University of Oxford

evidence.tested: EVEscape was trained only on pre-2020 sequences and compared against high-throughput experimental scans of SARS-CoV-2 variation that later emerged, a retrospective validation; prospective performance is not reported.
evidence.unknown: The abstract states no limitations; the page says testing on Lassa and Nipah is ongoing and vaccine or therapy use against future variants is a future application.
evidence.ai_role: A deep learning model of historical viral sequences, combined with biophysical and structural information, scored the escape potential of mutations.

title: AlphaMissense: cataloging missense genetic mutations
summary: It classified 89% of the 71 million possible missense variants: 32% as likely pathogenic and 57% as likely benign, with 90% precision on a database of known variants. Predictions are not intended for direct clinical use.
ai_technology: AlphaMissense
organization: Google DeepMind

evidence.tested: The model was validated on genetic and experimental benchmarks, and Genomics England cross-referenced its predictions with previously aggregated human variant pathogenicity data and found them consistent. The reported comparison uses previously collected pathogenicity and variant data; an independent data source is distinct from a new independent experimental replication.
evidence.unknown: The model does not predict structural or stability effects, the blog says predictions are not designed for direct clinical use, and the abstract describes no clinical validation.
evidence.ai_role: AlphaMissense, an AlphaFold adaptation fine-tuned on human and primate variant population frequency data, classified missense variants and released predictions for all possible human substitutions.

title: A neuroprosthesis translates attempted speech at 62 words per minute
summary: For a participant with ALS, intracortical electrodes and an AI algorithm converted attempted speech into text at 62 words per minute. With a 125,000-word vocabulary, the error rate was 23.8%, versus 9.1% for only 50 words. Proof of concept in one person, with an invasive implant and experimental device.
ai_technology: Neural network for phoneme decoding and language model
organization: Stanford Medicine; and BrainGate

evidence.tested: One participant with ALS attempted speech in real time; word error rates were measured at 50-word and 125,000-word vocabularies, with decoding at 62 words per minute.
evidence.unknown: The abstract states no limitations; the results come from one participant, the large-vocabulary error rate (23.8%) is substantial and decoding is well below conversational speed.
evidence.ai_role: An AI algorithm decoded spiking activity from intracortical microelectrode arrays into text.

title: Woman with paralysis communicates through a brain-controlled avatar
summary: For a participant with stroke-related paralysis, an electrode array on the cortex and AI algorithms translated attempted speech into text, synthetic voice and avatar movements. Text reached nearly 80 words per minute after individual training. Experimental study in one person; the system requires a physical connection to computers.
ai_technology: Neural speech decoding and AI facial animation
organization: UC San Francisco; and UC Berkeley

evidence.tested: One clinical-trial participant with paralysis attempted silent speech; decoding was measured in real time at a median of 78 words per minute with a 25% median word error rate.
evidence.unknown: The abstract does not explicitly state limitations; the single-participant study and 25% word error rate are the main caveats it implies.
evidence.ai_role: Deep-learning models decoded text from surface speech-cortex signals, synthesized personalized speech and animated a facial avatar.

title: Neanderthal and Denisovan peptides reconstructed as antibiotic candidates
summary: AI analysis of proteins from extinct hominins identified sequences that were then synthesized and tested against pathogens in culture and in mice. Some peptides showed antimicrobial activity; these are preclinical results, with no demonstration of safety or efficacy in humans.
ai_technology: AI for molecular de-extinction
organization: University of Pennsylvania

evidence.tested: Fragments were tested for antimicrobial activity in vitro, and representative fragments reduced A. baumannii infection in mouse skin abscess and thigh infection models.
evidence.unknown: The abstract does not explicitly state limitations; the findings rest on in vitro work and two mouse models rather than human trials.
evidence.ai_role: A random forest model (panCleave) predicted protease cleavage sites across proteomes to find antimicrobial fragments in modern human and extinct hominin proteins.

title: Avoiding aircraft contrails with AI forecasts
summary: In a trial with American Airlines and Breakthrough Energy, pilots flew 70 flights over six months using AI forecasts to avoid forming contrails, reducing them by 54% compared with flights without the forecasts. Flights that avoided contrails used 2% more fuel; across an airline’s flights, the impact could fall to 0.3% if only a small share need rerouting.
ai_technology: AI contrail-formation forecasts and satellite imagery
organization: Google Research; American Airlines and Breakthrough Energy

evidence.tested: Google, American Airlines and Breakthrough Energy flew 70 pilot flights over six months using AI forecasts to avoid contrail-forming altitudes; satellite imagery reported a 54% contrail reduction.
evidence.unknown: The article does not state a control group, the baseline for the 54% figure, statistical methods or peer review; fuel impact (2% more fuel, 0.3% airline-wide) is an estimate.
evidence.ai_role: AI contrail forecasts guided pilots to avoid altitudes likely to form contrails.

title: MASAI: AI-assisted mammography screening in a randomized trial
summary: In the initial analysis of 80,033 women, AI-assisted screening detected 244 cancers versus 203 with standard double reading and reduced the reading workload by 44%. A Lund update on January 30, 2026, after more than two years and about 106,000 women, reports higher sensitivity without more false positives. The comparison is in a Swedish setting; it does not demonstrate reduced mortality.
ai_technology: AI for mammogram triage and marking
organization: Lund University; and Unilabs

evidence.tested: A prospective randomized single-site trial compared AI-supported screening (about 40,003 women) with standard double reading (about 40,030 women), measuring cancers detected, false positives and radiologist workload.
evidence.unknown: The Lund article states limits: single site, no mortality outcomes, and the main analysis awaits two-year follow-up; the January 2026 update could not be verified on the page read.
evidence.ai_role: AI flagged higher-risk mammography exams for two physicians or marked suspicious findings for a single reader.

title: RFdiffusion: designing new proteins with a diffusion model
summary: A guided diffusion model generates tailored protein structures, such as proteins that bind tightly to another molecule, and outperforms previous methods across a wide range of problems. The post says only that ‘a useful fraction’ of generated designs work as intended, without figures; the software was released in March 2023.
ai_technology: RFdiffusion
organization: University of Washington Institute for Protein Design

evidence.tested: Designs were characterized experimentally (symmetric assemblies, metal-binding proteins, protein binders), and a cryo-EM structure of a designed binder was nearly identical to the design model; the abstract reports no overall success rates.
evidence.unknown: The abstract states no explicit limitations; the press post gives no success rates, sample sizes or benchmark numbers and says only that a useful fraction of designs work.
evidence.ai_role: A generative diffusion model fine-tuned from RoseTTAFold generated protein backbones for monomer, binder, oligomer, enzyme scaffold and motif designs.

title: Pangu-Weather: medium-range forecasts outperform the operational ECMWF model
summary: According to the authors, it is the first AI model to outperform ECMWF’s IFS at medium range: five-day Z500 RMSE of 296.7 versus 333.7, a global 24-hour forecast in 1.4 seconds on a GPU, and mean cyclone-track error of 120 km at three days versus 162 km. Source reviewed: Huawei Cloud blog, not the Nature paper (July 6, 2023); it underestimates extremes.
ai_technology: Pangu-Weather
organization: Huawei Cloud

evidence.tested: Trained on 39 years of global data; stronger deterministic results on reanalysis data than ECMWF's operational IFS in all tested variables; also evaluated on extreme weather and ensemble forecasts.
evidence.unknown: Comparisons are initialized with reanalysis data, as the abstract states; performance from operational analyses is not given there.
evidence.ai_role: Three-dimensional deep networks with Earth-specific priors and hierarchical temporal aggregation.

title: NowcastNet: extreme-precipitation forecasts up to three hours ahead
summary: A model combining neural networks and physical constraints forecasts precipitation up to three hours ahead; 62 meteorologists preferred it in 71% of 2,400 evaluated events. Tsinghua reports it was already deployed on the National Meteorological Center’s operational SWAN 3.0 platform. Expert preference does not measure reduced damage or guarantee accuracy for every event.
ai_technology: NowcastNet
organization: Tsinghua University / National Meteorological Center / UC Berkeley

evidence.tested: 62 forecasters from 23 meteorological stations ran retrospective and prospective checks on about 2,400 extreme-precipitation events and ranked NowcastNet first in 71% of cases against leading methods.
evidence.unknown: No limitations of NowcastNet are stated; the abstract reports no verification scores beyond expert preference, and the page says the team plans to extend the approach to other physics problems.
evidence.ai_role: A neural network combined with physics-based precipitation evolution forecasts extreme precipitation up to three hours ahead from radar data.

title: CogSim helps predict fusion ignition at the NIF
summary: Neural networks, Bayesian inference and physics simulations helped assess, before the experiment, the NIF design that produced 3.15 MJ of fusion energy from 2.05 MJ of laser energy delivered to the target on December 5, 2022. Experts designed the experiment; AI estimated its outcome and uncertainties. This is not the energy balance of the entire facility; the study was later published in Science in 2025.
ai_technology: CogSim (neural networks, transfer learning and Bayesian inference)
organization: Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory

evidence.tested: The CogSim team predicted the December 5, 2022 shot outcome before the experiment (about 50.2% chance of exceeding break-even), and the result of 3.15 MJ from 2.05 MJ matched the prediction after peer review and independent diagnostics.
evidence.unknown: The page says the approach does not guarantee success and that techniques still have much to prove; one good prediction does not validate a model, and testing on more experiments was planned for 2023.
evidence.ai_role: A generative model combining simulations, deep learning, experimental data and Bayesian statistics estimated the outcome and uncertainties of the NIF design before the shot.

title: AlphaDev: reinforcement learning discovers faster sorting routines
summary: Working at the assembly-instruction level, the system found sorting routines up to 70% faster for sequences of 3–5 elements and about 1.7% faster for sequences over 250,000 elements; they were adopted in the LLVM libc++ standard library. A hashing algorithm 30% faster was added to Abseil. The largest gains are for short sequences.
ai_technology: AlphaDev (reinforcement learning)
organization: Google DeepMind

evidence.tested: AlphaDev found sort 3 and sort 5 routines with fewer instructions than human benchmarks, matched sort 4, and had lower latency on variable sorts. Libc++ versions were up to 70% faster for five elements and about 1.7% faster above 250,000 elements.
evidence.unknown: Hashing result (30% faster) not seen in the text read. Search is at assembly level; the paper reports optimality proof only for sort 3 (17 instructions). Results cover tested CPUs: ARMv8, Intel Skylake, AMD Zen 2.
evidence.ai_role: AlphaDev, an AlphaZero-based reinforcement learning agent with a transformer encoder, built assembly programs instruction by instruction, rewarded for correctness and latency; the team translated results to C++.

title: Abaucin: a targeted antibiotic against Acinetobacter baumannii
summary: A model trained on about 7,500 compounds screened 6,680 new compounds in under two hours; of 240 tested in the laboratory, nine were antibiotics, including abaucin, which was effective against wound infections in mice. Activity is highly narrow (no effect on the other bacteria tested) and still preclinical.
ai_technology: Machine learning for compound screening
organization: MIT; and McMaster University

evidence.tested: About 7,500 molecules were screened in vitro, a neural network predicted new compounds that were tested in the laboratory (about 240 tested, nine antibiotics), and abaucin controlled an A. baumannii infection in a mouse wound model.
evidence.unknown: The abstract states no explicit limitations; the press release says activity is highly narrow (no effect on the other bacteria tested) and the compound remains preclinical.
evidence.ai_role: A neural network trained on screening results predicted structurally new compounds active against A. baumannii.

source_review.scope: Original institutional announcement checked for the specific results, AI contribution and limitations cited in the antibiotic dossier or mathematical follow-up pilot. Full-paper reanalysis, external replication and an exhaustive follow-up search were not performed.

relationships.reason: The source explicitly traces this A. baumannii screening study to the earlier halicin program. Distinct candidate and experiment; not independent confirmation of halicin.

follow_up.note: MIT identifies halicin and abaucin as earlier screening results motivating generative design of new NG1/DN1 candidates. The later study does not establish clinical efficacy of these earlier candidates.

follow_up_review.scope: Bounded check of the original announcements cited by the events recorded here, including explicit links to later program work. This is not an exhaustive literature search or ongoing monitoring commitment.

title: ExoMiner and multiplicity validate 69 new exoplanets
summary: ExoMiner V1.2 combines deep learning with information about other signals in the same star system to validate 69 planets in Kepler data. This is statistical validation of transit signals, not new direct observation; the result is distinct from the 301 planets validated in 2021.
ai_technology: ExoMiner V1.2 / multiplicity boost
organization: USRA; NASA and SETI Institute

evidence.tested: ExoMiner V1.2 with multiplicity information was applied to Kepler data and validated 69 planets, compared against baseline classifiers and prior validation work.
evidence.unknown: The arXiv page states no limitations, and the statistical validation and false-positive tests are not described on the page read.
evidence.ai_role: A deep-learning classifier (ExoMiner V1.2) combined with information about other signals in the same star system to validate transit signals.

title: Nonlocal quantum interference without entanglement of intrinsic properties
summary: An AI- and graph-theory-based prediction was confirmed in two experiments: four photons exhibit nonlocal interference without requiring entanglement of their intrinsic properties. The superposition concerns their generation locations; applications to metrology remain prospective.
ai_technology: AI and graph theory for quantum experiments
organization: Max Planck Institute for the Science of Light; Nanjing University and Hefei University

evidence.tested: Four-photon nonlocal interference without entanglement of intrinsic properties was demonstrated experimentally, and the abstract reports the interference controlled by an undetected photon.
evidence.unknown: The abstract states no limitations; the press release says applications to metrology remain prospective.
evidence.ai_role: The press release says an AI- and graph-theory-based prediction was confirmed in two experiments; the Nature Communications abstract does not describe the AI prediction.

title: First draft of the human pangenome reference
summary: A consortium of 119 scientists from 60 institutions published in Nature a pangenome combining assembled genomes from 47 people of diverse ancestries, rather than one person. Google adapted DeepVariant to identify variants and DeepConsensus to correct sequencing errors; a long-read assembler achieved over 99.999% final accuracy. This is a draft: benefits for diagnosis and treatment remain prospective.
ai_technology: DeepVariant and DeepConsensus
organization: Google Research; and Human Pangenome Reference Consortium

evidence.tested: The draft pangenome from 47 assemblies was evaluated for accuracy at structural and base-pair levels, and short-read analysis was compared with GRCh38-based workflows (34% fewer small-variant errors).
evidence.unknown: The abstract states no explicit limitations; the blog says this is a draft and benefits for diagnosis and treatment remain prospective.
evidence.ai_role: Google adapted DeepVariant to call variants and DeepConsensus to correct sequencing errors in the pangenome assembly.

title: New zirconium-indium-nickel superconductor identified with machine learning
summary: Predictive models and experts guided fabrication of candidates and identified a zirconium, indium and nickel alloy with a superconducting transition around 9 K. The press release reports a three-month discovery; this is not a room-temperature superconductor or a demonstration of industrial use.
ai_technology: MITHRIL / machine learning
organization: Johns Hopkins Applied Physics Laboratory

evidence.tested: Closed-loop ML predictions were tested experimentally: candidates were fabricated and measured, and results fed back to refine the model; a Zr-In-Ni superconductor with transition around 9 K was found in four cycles.
evidence.unknown: The arXiv page states no limitations and omits synthesis, transition temperature and model accuracy details; the press release notes training-data human bias and chemically impossible generated compositions, and cites an npj Computational Materials paper that was not read.
evidence.ai_role: Machine-learning models trained on public superconductor datasets predicted and ranked candidate compositions for fabrication.

title: LinearDesign: more stable mRNA sequences designed by an algorithm
summary: The algorithm, based on a parsing technique from natural-language processing, finds the most stable mRNA sequence for a given protein in about eleven minutes. According to Baidu’s press release, whose study appeared in Nature, sequences produced this way showed greater stability, protein expression and antibody response than comparators in animal experiments. Figures are company-reported; the Baidu release copy on EurekAlert was reviewed, not a baidu.com page.
ai_technology: LinearDesign
organization: Baidu Research

evidence.tested: LinearDesign-designed mRNA for COVID-19 and VZV was compared with wildtype and codon-optimized sequences in animal experiments, measuring half-life, expression and antibody response; the figures are company-reported and the release describes no independent replication.
evidence.unknown: The Nature abstract states no specific study limitations and the release states none; the release says benefits such as lower doses and fewer side effects are possibilities not tested.
evidence.ai_role: A parsing-based algorithm (LinearDesign) optimized mRNA structural stability and codon usage for a given protein.

title: An MRI decoder turns brain activity into text
summary: A noninvasive decoder reconstructs continuous text from fMRI that closely, and sometimes precisely, matches the original meaning in about half of trials (after dozens of hours of training with podcasts; it also works on silent videos). Published in Nature Neuroscience; it works only with cooperative participants and is not word-for-word transcription.
ai_technology: Semantic decoder from fMRI
organization: University of Texas at Austin

evidence.tested: A non-invasive fMRI decoder generated continuous text that conveyed the meaning of perceived speech, imagined speech and silent videos; the press release says it matched the original meaning in about half of trials and works only with cooperative participants.
evidence.unknown: The abstract does not report participant numbers or semantic accuracy measures and states no explicit limitations; the press release says it is not word-for-word transcription.
evidence.ai_role: A decoder trained on fMRI recordings of cortical semantic representations generated word sequences matching the meaning of brain activity.

title: Language models guide improvements to seven antibodies
summary: Two rounds of laboratory evolution, using at most 20 variants per antibody, improved the affinity of four mature antibodies by up to sevenfold and three immature ones by up to 160-fold. Biochemical and pseudovirus tests; no demonstration of therapeutic benefit in humans.
ai_technology: Protein language models
organization: Stanford University

evidence.tested: Language-model-guided variants of seven antibodies were made in two lab evolution rounds (at most 20 variants per antibody) and binding was measured by biolayer interferometry; four antibodies were also checked for thermostability, polyspecificity and pseudovirus neutralization.
evidence.unknown: The authors state that affinity gains are smaller than in vivo somatic hypermutation, the method improves existing binding rather than creating new binders, and it may work less well under other selection pressures; no therapeutic benefit in humans is shown.
evidence.ai_role: General protein language models guided affinity maturation by choosing which antibody variants to test.

title: PRIMO: a sharper image of the M87 black hole
summary: A machine-learning method trained on more than 30,000 simulated black-hole images reconstructed M87* from 2017 Event Horizon Telescope data, using the array’s full resolution: the ring is about half as wide as in the 2019 image. It fills gaps with patterns learned from simulations, without quantified uncertainty.
ai_technology: PRIMO (dictionary learning)
organization: Georgia Institute of Technology; Institute for Advanced Study and NSF NOIRLab

evidence.tested: The PRIMO reconstruction, built from over 30,000 simulated black-hole images, was checked for consistency with the 2017 EHT data and the 2019 image; no held-out tests are described.
evidence.unknown: The article states that generating the image requires assuming an appropriate form of the missing information and describes no quantified uncertainties; implications for the black hole are framed as future possibilities.
evidence.ai_role: A machine-learning method trained on simulated images filled gaps in the 2017 EHT data to reconstruct the M87* image.

title: LuxSit: de novo luciferases active in the laboratory
summary: The group designed new luciferases and identified three active enzymes among the initial designs. The 117-residue LuxSit catalyzes blue light with the DTZ substrate; its function is verified in the laboratory, while therapeutic or industrial applications remain prospective.
ai_technology: Family-wide hallucination and deep learning
organization: Institute for Protein Design

evidence.tested: Designed luciferases were tested in activity assays with synthetic luciferin substrates; the most active design had catalytic efficiency comparable to native luciferases and high substrate selectivity.
evidence.unknown: The abstract does not state how many designs were tested or how many were active, and states no explicit limitations; therapeutic or industrial applications remain untested.
evidence.ai_role: Deep learning generated idealized scaffolds with binding pockets and matching sequences used to design artificial luciferases.

title: Real-time wildfire perimeters from satellite imagery
summary: A model using geostationary imagery tracks fire perimeters with updates every 10–15 minutes and, according to the page, is more accurate than similar products and the previous model based on NOAA GOES-16/17 data; shown in Search and Maps for large fires in the United States, Mexico, much of Canada and Australia. Resolution is 2 km; clouds can hide fires; figures appear only in an image.
ai_technology: Model on geostationary satellite imagery
organization: Google Research

evidence.tested: Fire perimeters were compared with official fire scars using precision, recall and distance metrics; a comparison with an earlier GOES-16/17 model and a 2022 US test set unavailable during training are also reported.
evidence.unknown: The post states limitations: smoke and clouds hide fires, resolution is about 2 km and coarser away from nadir, and coverage is limited to large fires in the listed regions; no paper is cited.
evidence.ai_role: A model using geostationary satellite imagery tracks fire perimeters with updates every 10-15 minutes.

title: Deep learning searches for technosignatures around 820 nearby stars
summary: A deep-learning method analyzed 150 TB of Green Bank Telescope data from 820 stars, previously searched in 2017 without interesting signals, and found eight narrowband signals of interest with nonzero drift, present only in observations where the target was in view. Follow-up observations did not find them again; no claim of extraterrestrial origin.
ai_technology: Deep learning on radio data
organization: SETI Institute; Breakthrough Listen and University of Toronto

evidence.tested: The deep-learning method analyzed Green Bank Telescope data from 820 stars and flagged eight narrowband candidates; the page reports no follow-up results and no injection tests, and the abstract gives no false-positive figures.
evidence.unknown: The page states no limitations; rejecting human radio interference is named as the core challenge, and the full paper's methods, which the listing says were later published in Nature Astronomy, were not read.
evidence.ai_role: A beta-Convolutional Variational Autoencoder flagged technosignature candidates in a semi-unsupervised manner.

title: Sybil: lung-cancer risk prediction up to six years from a low-dose CT
summary: The model predicts risk from a single CT with a six-year C-index of 0.75 (NLST), 0.81 (MGH) and 0.80 (CGMH), and a one-year ROC area between 0.86 and 0.94. Retrospective validation on three independent datasets; trained only on smokers, with prospective testing and testing in nonsmokers as next steps.
ai_technology: Sybil (neural network on CT scans)
organization: MIT; Mass General Cancer Center and Chang Gung Memorial Hospital

evidence.tested: The model was trained on NLST low-dose CT scans and validated on a held-out NLST set and two independent cohorts (MGH and CGMH), with six-year C-index 0.75, 0.81 and 0.80; the abstract describes no prospective testing.
evidence.unknown: The abstract states that future study is required to understand clinical applications; the press release says prospective testing and testing in nonsmokers are next steps.
evidence.ai_role: A deep learning model predicts lung-cancer risk from a single low-dose chest CT.

title: A liver-cancer target and molecule identified with Pharma.AI
summary: Pharma.AI combined PandaOmics, Chemistry42 and an AlphaFold-predicted structure to identify a hepatocellular-carcinoma target and produce a hit molecule within 30 days of target selection, synthesizing seven compounds. A second round produced a more potent hit; an early Chemical Science study, with no clinical efficacy demonstrated.
ai_technology: Pharma.AI, PandaOmics, Chemistry42 and AlphaFold
organization: University of Toronto; Insilico Medicine and collaborators

evidence.tested: Selected compounds were synthesized and tested in biological assays: the first hit bound CDK20 (Kd about 9.2 µM) and a second AI-driven round gave a more potent compound with greater antiproliferative activity in liver cancer cells; the abstract describes no in vivo testing.
evidence.unknown: The abstract notes AlphaFold predictions have varying confidence, the first hit came from only 7 synthesized compounds, and potency values vary widely; no clinical efficacy is demonstrated.
evidence.ai_role: Pharma.AI platforms (PandaOmics, Chemistry42) used AlphaFold-predicted structures to select a liver-cancer target and generate candidate molecules.

title: ESM Metagenomic Atlas: over 600 million protein structures
summary: Meta AI published predicted structures for almost the entire MGnify90 database (over 600 million), generated in about two weeks on roughly 2,000 GPUs with a 15-billion-parameter language model, up to 60 times faster than previous methods. These are predictions, and high-confidence structures are a much smaller subset.
ai_technology: ESMFold (15-billion-parameter language model)
organization: Meta AI

evidence.tested: The preprint reports structure prediction up to 60 times faster while maintaining accuracy versus state-of-the-art methods and an atlas of 617 million structures; the blog describes no experimental checks.
evidence.unknown: The blog lists no limitations and notes some sequences fold into disordered forms; high-confidence predictions are a subset.
evidence.ai_role: Language model (15B parameters) predicted protein structures from sequence.

title: AlphaTensor: new algorithms for matrix multiplication
summary: A reinforcement-learning agent found matrix-multiplication algorithms better than known ones for many sizes (for example, 76 multiplications instead of 80 for 4×5 by 5×5). Algorithms optimized for hardware were 10–20% faster on V100 GPUs and TPU v2. The improvement over Strassen applies in a finite field.
ai_technology: AlphaTensor (based on AlphaZero)
organization: Google DeepMind

evidence.tested: Algorithms are provably correct by construction and their multiplication counts are compared with known methods; hardware-targeted algorithms were benchmarked on V100 GPU and TPU v2.
evidence.unknown: The page lists no formal limitations; it notes the search space is very large and the work is specific to matrix multiplication.
evidence.ai_role: Reinforcement-learning agent searched for tensor decompositions giving new matrix-multiplication algorithms.

title: Machine learning and synthesis clarify metastable phases of carbon
summary: An algorithm constructed metastable phase diagrams of carbon and identified structural features of n-diamond that were then verified experimentally. The group also synthesized predicted phases and compared structures under a microscope; the work concerns carbon only and does not establish useful properties of the new materials.
ai_technology: Machine learning and atomistic simulations
organization: Argonne National Laboratory

evidence.tested: Workflow found 505 candidate carbon structures; a neural network trained on 273 phases, test error 37.1 meV/atom. Diamond-anvil laser-heating experiments on graphite with electron microscopy were used to compare predicted metastable phases, including n-diamond.
evidence.unknown: The search is not guaranteed exhaustive; the paper calls cubic-diaphite a candidate structure for n-diamond. The model had higher errors at high pressure; kinetics are only partly covered. Argonne synthesis of unreported phases was not seen in the paper text read.
evidence.ai_role: A deep neural network predicted Gibbs free energy; a support vector machine drew phase boundaries; an evolutionary search proposed structures. Humans ran the experiments.

title: AlphaFold helps interpret activation of PINK1, a Parkinson’s-linked protein
summary: After experimentally determining different forms of PINK1, the WEHI group used AlphaFold to model the human protein and its dimer, obtaining structures consistent with experimental results. The predictions also helped interpret how mutations associated with early-onset Parkinson’s may affect dimerization; this does not amount to a validated therapy.
ai_technology: AlphaFold
organization: WEHI; and Google DeepMind

evidence.tested: The WEHI group compared an AlphaFold model of human PINK1 dimer with its own experimental structure work and used it to model disease mutations, which it says confirmed their suspicions.
evidence.unknown: The article describes no specific limitations of the predictions and says plenty of questions remain.
evidence.ai_role: AlphaFold modelled human PINK1 and its dimer and the effect of mutations on dimerisation.

title: ProteinMPNN: protein sequences designed in about one second
summary: A neural network generates the amino-acid sequence for a given protein shape in about one second, over 200 times faster than the best previous software, without specialist tuning. A related study shows that proteins designed with ProteinMPNN fold correctly much more often, including nanoscale rings and complex assemblies. Researchers describe it as the beginning of machine learning in protein design.
ai_technology: ProteinMPNN
organization: University of Washington Institute for Protein Design

evidence.tested: Speed is compared with prior software; a related Science study tested lab-made designs, which folded as intended more often, including nanoscale rings imaged by electron microscopy.
evidence.unknown: The article gives no quantitative success rates and notes protein data is scarce, requiring trial and error.
evidence.ai_role: Neural network generated amino-acid sequences for given protein shapes.

title: AlphaFold Database: over 200 million structures
summary: The predicted-protein-structure archive, maintained with EMBL-EBI, grew from nearly 1 million to over 200 million structures, covering practically all cataloged proteins, with free access and bulk download from Google Cloud. More than 500,000 researchers in 190 countries had already used it. These are predictions, not experimental measurements.
ai_technology: AlphaFold 2
organization: Google DeepMind; and EMBL-EBI

evidence.tested: The post gives no accuracy metrics for the new structures; it cites two Nature AlphaFold papers and uses in experiments as evidence.
evidence.unknown: The post states no explicit limitations or caveats on prediction accuracy.
evidence.ai_role: AlphaFold predicted protein structures added to the AlphaFold Database.

title: TREWS: early sepsis alerts evaluated in five hospitals
summary: A machine-learning system monitored about 590,000 patients in five hospitals, flagging sepsis risk from medical records. In the studied cohort, timely clinical confirmation of alerts was associated with lower mortality, organ failure and length of stay. Observational study: the association does not show that AI caused better outcomes.
ai_technology: TREWS (Targeted Real-time Early Warning System)
organization: Johns Hopkins University; and Bayesian Health

evidence.tested: A prospective multi-site cohort of 590,736 monitored patients (five hospitals) compared outcomes of sepsis alerts confirmed by a provider within 3 hours with outcomes otherwise, adjusting for severity.
evidence.unknown: The association is observational and does not show that the AI caused better outcomes.
evidence.ai_role: Machine-learning early warning system (TREWS) flagged sepsis risk from medical records.

title: BirdNET: citizen science through bird-song identification
summary: The app recognizes over 3,000 species from their calls, with more than 2.2 million people contributing since 2018; in four test cases, its data reproduced known patterns such as song distribution and the migration ranges of two species. Published in PLOS Biology; only four cases, with no identification-error figures.
ai_technology: BirdNET (bioacoustics)
organization: Cornell Lab of Ornithology

evidence.tested: In four test cases where conventional research had robust answers, BirdNET data replicated known patterns such as song-type distribution and migration ranges.
evidence.unknown: No identification-error rates are reported and the authors describe the validation as the first step.
evidence.ai_role: Bird-song recognition app identified species from calls and produced citizen-science observations.

title: Model of the human nuclear pore with AlphaFold2 and electron microscopy
summary: AlphaFold2 and ColabFold, combined with cryo-tomography and cryo-electron microscopy, produced a model of the human nuclear pore complex (about 30 proteins, about 1,000 copies, 120 MDa) covering over 90% of the complex, versus 46% for previous models. Flexible parts remain unresolved; a complete dynamic model is future work.
ai_technology: AlphaFold2 and ColabFold
organization: EMBL

evidence.tested: The integrative model (AlphaFold2 with cryo-ET and cryo-EM data) was validated against experimental data and covers more than 90% of the NPC core versus 46% for previous models.
evidence.unknown: Flexible peripheral parts are not modelled, no quantitative confidence scores are given, and a complete dynamic model is future work.
evidence.ai_role: AlphaFold2 and ColabFold predicted protein structures that were assembled into the nuclear pore model.

title: Machine learning suggests a more general theory of microlensing
summary: An algorithm highlighted microlensing configurations not explained by usual interpretations, leading to a theory unifying two degeneracies. The authors report a better fit to data from two dozen previous discoveries; they describe the theory as probably incomplete.
ai_technology: Machine-learning inference
organization: UC Berkeley / The Ohio State University

evidence.tested: The machine-learning-derived theory was checked against the datasets of two dozen earlier microlensing discoveries and fit them better than the earlier interpretations.
evidence.unknown: The authors say the broader theory is likely still incomplete, and the multi-planet case is not yet worked out.
evidence.ai_role: Algorithm highlighted microlensing configurations not explained by the usual interpretations.

title: FAST-PETase: an AI-engineered enzyme degrades PET waste
summary: A machine-learning model suggested PETase mutations, then tested on 51 post-consumer containers, fibers and fabrics. FAST-PETase degrades PET below 50 °C, in some cases down to monomers within 24 hours; production at scale and environmental use still needed development.
ai_technology: MutCompute / 3D convolutional network
organization: University of Texas at Austin

evidence.tested: FAST-PETase was tested on 51 post-consumer containers, fibers and fabrics, degrading PET below 50 °C, in some cases to monomers within 24 hours.
evidence.unknown: Scale-up, field use at polluted sites and cost are not demonstrated, and the work covers only PET.
evidence.ai_role: Machine-learning model suggested enzyme mutations.

title: Murmurations: unexpected oscillations in elliptic-curve data
summary: Classification experiments and analysis of elliptic-curve data show oscillations in the mean of Frobenius traces that vary with rank. A numerical observation, not proof of a general law; the 2022 preprint was later published in Experimental Mathematics in 2024.
ai_technology: Logistic regression and PCA
organization: Yang-Hui He; Kyu-Hwan Lee, Thomas Oliver and Alexey Pozdnyakov

evidence.tested: Classification experiments and analysis of elliptic-curve data show oscillations in the average Frobenius trace that vary with rank.
evidence.unknown: Not reported in the arXiv abstract read.
evidence.ai_role: Machine-learning classification experiments were used to classify elliptic curves by rank.

title: Ithaca: restoring and dating ancient Greek inscriptions
summary: A neural network reconstructs missing text in damaged Greek inscriptions, identifies their provenance and dates them: 62% accuracy in restoration, 71% in location, and dating within 30 years of reference ranges. With Ithaca, historians improved from 25% to 72% correct restorations. It is intended to assist historians.
ai_technology: Ithaca (deep neural network)
organization: Google DeepMind

evidence.tested: Restoration (62%), location (71%) and dating were checked on held-out dated inscriptions, and a historian study rose from 25% to 72% correct restorations with the tool.
evidence.unknown: Accuracy is far from perfect, dating is a range within about 30 years, and the model was trained only on Greek inscriptions.
evidence.ai_role: Neural network restored missing text, identified provenance and dated Greek inscriptions.

title: FourCastNet: high-resolution global forecasts with neural networks
summary: The preprint presents global forecasts at 0.25° resolution and a one-week forecast in under two seconds. Comparison with IFS is favorable at short lead times for large-scale variables and some finer-scale variables; this does not mean general superiority or operational use.
ai_technology: Adaptive Fourier Neural Operators
organization: Jaideep Pathak; and collaborators

evidence.tested: Forecasts at 0.25 degrees are compared with ECMWF IFS, matching it at short lead times for large-scale variables and outperforming it for some fine-scale variables such as precipitation.
evidence.unknown: Not reported in the arXiv abstract read.
evidence.ai_role: Adaptive Fourier neural operator produced global weather forecasts.

title: Tokamak plasma control with reinforcement learning
summary: A single neural network controls the magnetic coils of Lausanne’s TCV tokamak and forms plasmas in different configurations (snowflake, ITER-like shape, double droplet). Trained mainly in simulation and then tested on the real machine. Stated limitations: plasma lasts about three seconds and the machine changes from day to day.
ai_technology: Deep reinforcement learning
organization: Google DeepMind; and EPFL Swiss Plasma Center

evidence.tested: On the TCV tokamak the controller produced and held elongated, conventional, negative-triangularity and snowflake configurations, with accurate tracking of location, current and shape, and sustained two separate 'droplet' plasmas.
evidence.unknown: Transfer to larger or reactor-scale devices is not reported in the abstract.
evidence.ai_role: A deep reinforcement-learning architecture learned to command the full set of control coils from high-level objectives.

title: DINGO: gravitational-wave parameters in seconds
summary: The neural network estimates the mass, spin, position, inclination and distance of binary black holes in seconds rather than hours or months, with about ten days of training, and was tested on eight events from LIGO and Virgo’s O1 and O2 runs. Published in Physical Review Letters; extension to neutron stars is only promising; source reviewed was a Max Planck doctoral-program page.
ai_technology: DINGO (Bayesian inference with neural networks)
organization: Max Planck Institute for Intelligent Systems; and Max Planck Institute for Gravitational Physics

evidence.tested: Parameter estimates for eight LIGO-Virgo events agree closely with standard inference codes, with inference times cut from days to about 20 seconds.
evidence.unknown: The article says extension to neutron stars and complex signals is promising but not demonstrated.
evidence.ai_role: Neural network acted as a surrogate for Bayesian posterior distributions for gravitational-wave parameters.

title: DM21: a neural network as a density-functional theory functional
summary: A neural network represents the functional used in DFT and addresses two longstanding errors of traditional functionals: excessive electron delocalization and spin-symmetry breaking during bond breaking. Published in Science with open code; the post gives no benchmark figures and DFT remains an approximation.
ai_technology: DM21 (neural network for the exchange-correlation functional)
organization: Google DeepMind

evidence.tested: DM21 is compared with traditional functionals on benchmarks for main-group atoms and molecules and on bond-breaking and charge-localisation examples.
evidence.unknown: The page gives no numerical benchmark figures and says DFT remains an approximation.
evidence.ai_role: Neural network represents the exchange-correlation functional in density functional theory.

title: AI-guided pure mathematics: knots and representation theory
summary: With mathematicians Williamson (Sydney) and Lackenby and Juhász (Oxford), supervised-learning techniques revealed patterns leading to an unexpected link between a knot’s algebraic signature and its geometry (the ‘natural slope’), and to a new algorithm for the combinatorial invariance conjecture. The conjectures and proofs are the mathematicians’; the algorithm was checked on over 3 million examples, not proved in general.
ai_technology: Supervised learning and attribution techniques
organization: Google DeepMind

evidence.tested: Conjectures and proofs were established by mathematicians, and the new algorithm was computationally verified on over 3 million examples.
evidence.unknown: Certain patterns still elude ML, and the representation-theory structure appears only at 100s or 1000s of vertices.
evidence.ai_role: Supervised learning revealed patterns that led to the knot and representation-theory results and a new algorithm.

title: A neural network “hallucinates” new protein structures
summary: The network predicted about 2,000 new sequences as foldable; over 100 were produced in the lab, and for three, nuclear magnetic resonance and X-ray crystallography confirmed the predicted shapes. Only three proteins were characterized in detail; using the method to create useful functions (drugs, enzymes) is a future goal.
ai_technology: Neural network for structure prediction (hallucination)
organization: University of Washington Institute for Protein Design

evidence.tested: 129 hallucinated sequences were synthesised, 27 gave monodisperse proteins, and three structures determined by X-ray crystallography or NMR matched the hallucinated models.
evidence.unknown: Only three proteins were characterised in detail, and using the method for useful functions is a future goal.
evidence.ai_role: Neural network hallucinated new protein sequences predicted to fold.

title: ExoMiner: 301 new planets validated in Kepler data
summary: The ExoMiner neural network, run on the Pleiades supercomputer, validated 301 planets from the remaining Kepler candidates, adding to the 4,569 already validated; none is Earth-like or in the habitable zone. “Validated” is statistical, not confirmed; NASA’s 2026 count gives 370 for the same work, an unexplained discrepancy.
ai_technology: ExoMiner (deep neural network)
organization: NASA Ames Research Center; and NASA JPL

evidence.tested: ExoMiner was evaluated on a test set (recall 0.936 at 99% precision in the arXiv abstract) and used to validate 301 new planets.
evidence.unknown: Validation is statistical rather than confirmation, the article gives no false-positive rates, and none of the planets is Earth-like.
evidence.ai_role: Deep learning classifier vetted transit signals from Kepler.

title: Enformer: gene expression predicted from DNA sequence
summary: A Transformer-based model predicts gene expression from 200,000 base pairs of input DNA, over five times more than earlier methods, and is much more accurate at predicting variant effects. Enhancer attribution scores are comparable to methods using experimental data. The post gives no numerical gain and acknowledges that linking enhancers to the genes they regulate remains an open problem.
ai_technology: Enformer (Transformer)
organization: Google DeepMind

evidence.tested: Enformer is compared with prior models on variant-effect prediction and enhancer contribution scores against methods using experimental data, with a rs11644125 case study.
evidence.unknown: Linking enhancers to the genes they regulate is described as a major unsolved problem, and many disease variants are spuriously correlated.
evidence.ai_role: Transformer model predicted gene expression from 200,000 base pairs of DNA.

title: Short-term rainfall prediction with a generative model
summary: Developed with the UK Met Office, the model forecasts precipitation up to two hours ahead; over 50 expert meteorologists chose it as their first choice in 89% of cases compared with the most widely used methods. The authors cite long-range accuracy and rare, intense events as limitations.
ai_technology: Deep generative radar model (DGMR)
organization: Google DeepMind; and Met Office

evidence.tested: Over 50 Met Office meteorologists chose the model first in 89% of cases, and it was compared with PySTEPS and UNet on UK and US radar data.
evidence.unknown: No method is without limitations; long-range accuracy and rare intense events need improvement.
evidence.ai_role: Generative model forecast precipitation up to two hours ahead.

title: Climate TRACE: first independent database of global emissions
summary: Using machine learning on data from over 300 satellites and 11,100 sensors (over 59 trillion bytes), emissions from oil and gas in major countries were estimated at about twice UNFCCC reports (about 1 billion tonnes more), while rice emissions in India were nearly three times the official 2016 inventory. No peer review; the page gives both September 14 and September 16, 2021.
ai_technology: Machine learning on satellite and sensor data
organization: Climate TRACE

evidence.tested: The page gives no methodology for checking the estimates; it says more than 50 outside organisations reviewed methodology and validated findings, without describing results.
evidence.unknown: The page notes granularity is still developing and that estimates are hedged and constantly evolving; no peer review is mentioned.
evidence.ai_role: Machine learning on satellite and sensor data estimated global emissions.

title: IceNet: seasonal forecasts of Arctic sea ice
summary: The model outperforms ECMWF’s SEAS5 dynamical system in seasonal forecasts of summer sea ice, especially for extreme events, and is over 2,000 times faster (under ten seconds on a GPU). SEAS5 is better at a one-month lead, and the September comparison covers nine years; published in Nature Communications.
ai_technology: IceNet (probabilistic deep learning)
organization: British Antarctic Survey; Alan Turing Institute, and others

evidence.tested: IceNet is compared with the SEAS5 dynamical model in seasonal summer sea-ice forecasts, especially extreme events.
evidence.unknown: Not reported in the abstract read.
evidence.ai_role: Probabilistic deep-learning model forecast the next six months of sea-ice concentration.

title: INS018_073: AI identifies a preclinical candidate for renal fibrosis
summary: Insilico Medicine named INS018_073 a preclinical candidate after in vitro tests and testing in a mouse model of renal fibrosis. The company reports improvements in pathology, biomarkers, and histologically observed fibrosis. The candidate was proposed for IND-enabling studies; these are company-reported preclinical results, not clinical evidence or independent confirmation.
ai_technology: Pharma.AI / Chemistry42
organization: Insilico Medicine

evidence.tested: Company-reported in vitro potency (nanomolar) and a mouse unilateral ureteral obstruction model with histology, plus a 14-day mouse safety study.
evidence.unknown: No effect sizes, doses or biomarkers are named, and no independent confirmation or peer review is stated.
evidence.ai_role: AI-driven target and compound identification (PandaOmics) produced the candidate.

title: AlphaFold Protein Structure Database: first 350,000 models
summary: Predicted structures for the human proteome (about 20,000 proteins) and 20 other organisms were published, over 350,000 models in total, hosted free by EMBL-EBI. DeepMind announced an expansion to over 100 million structures. These are predictions that complement experimental methods. Note: the page header says July 22, 2022, but the text calls CASP14 “last December” and the 2022 post refers to it as a 2021 release; date corrected to 2021.
ai_technology: AlphaFold 2
organization: Google DeepMind; and EMBL-EBI

evidence.tested: Predictions cover 98.5% of human proteins; 58% of residues have a confident prediction and 36% very high confidence. Case studies illustrate possible hypotheses.
evidence.unknown: The structures are predictions; the abstract does not report experimental confirmation of new structures.
evidence.ai_role: AlphaFold 2 applied at proteome scale, with confidence metrics built on the model.

title: ProGen generates artificial proteins with enzyme activity
summary: A protein language model generated synthetic lysozymes: two of the five characterized in cells degraded bacterial cell walls with activity comparable to egg-white lysozyme. Laboratory tests and crystallography support the result, but do not demonstrate clinical applications. The preprint dates to July 18, 2021; the Nature Biotechnology publication and UCSF announcement are from January 2023.
ai_technology: ProGen
organization: UCSF / Salesforce Research

evidence.tested: Five model-generated lysozyme families were experimentally characterised, with activity and catalytic efficiency compared with natural lysozymes, and crystal structures reported.
evidence.unknown: Not reported in the abstract read.
evidence.ai_role: Protein language model trained on over 280 million sequences generated artificial lysozymes.

title: RoseTTAFold: accessible prediction of protein structures
summary: A three-track neural network (sequence, residue interactions, and 3D structure) computes a structure in about ten minutes on a single gaming computer. Baker’s group predicted hundreds of new structures, including little-known proteins in the human genome. The web server received over 4,500 requests in the previous month. The page does not state limitations.
ai_technology: RoseTTAFold
organization: University of Washington Institute for Protein Design

evidence.tested: The page describes the tool's speed and hundreds of new structures but does not describe how predictions were checked.
evidence.unknown: Not reported.
evidence.ai_role: Three-track neural network predicted protein structures.

title: A neuroprosthesis restores words for a man with paralysis
summary: Neural networks decoded the attempted speech of a man with stroke-related paralysis, displaying words and sentences on a screen. With a 50-word vocabulary, the system reached up to 18 words per minute and a median accuracy of 75%. Proof of principle in one person, using an implant on the brain surface and a limited vocabulary.
ai_technology: Neural networks for speech and language model
organization: UC San Francisco

evidence.tested: Decoding was tested in one participant over 48 sessions using a 50-word vocabulary, reaching up to 18 words per minute and a median accuracy of 75%.
evidence.unknown: It is a proof of principle in one person with a limited vocabulary, per the press release.
evidence.ai_role: Deep-learning algorithms decoded attempted words from cortical activity.

title: H01: reconstruction of one cubic millimeter of human cerebral cortex
summary: A sample of about 1 mm³ of human cortex was imaged at 4 nm across about 5,300 sections and automatically reconstructed: 1.4 petabytes, tens of thousands of neurons, 130 million annotated synapses, and 104 manually corrected cells. The sample is about one-millionth of a brain; reconstruction is imperfect and initial findings are preliminary.
ai_technology: Automated segmentation of electron microscopy images
organization: Google Research; and Harvard (Lichtman Lab)

evidence.tested: The automated reconstruction was checked by manual proofreading of about 104 cells; the abstract says connections were validated.
evidence.unknown: Automated reconstruction is imperfect, the sample is about one-millionth of a brain, and findings are preliminary.
evidence.ai_role: Automated machine-learning pipeline reconstructed neurons and synapses from electron microscopy images.

title: EAGLE: AI electrocardiograms to detect reduced heart function
summary: A randomized study across 120 primary-care groups at 45 sites evaluated neural-network alerts on electrocardiograms from 22,641 adults. The intervention produced five additional diagnoses of low ejection fraction per thousand patients, without a global increase in echocardiography use. The result concerns identification of dysfunction, not improved clinical outcomes.
ai_technology: Convolutional neural network for electrocardiograms
organization: Mayo Clinic

evidence.tested: A cluster-randomised trial across 120 primary-care teams (22,641 adults) compared AI-ECG alerts with usual care on new low-EF diagnoses within 90 days.
evidence.unknown: Not reported in the abstract read; the trial measured diagnosis rather than clinical outcomes.
evidence.ai_role: Neural network analysed electrocardiograms and alerted clinicians to possible low ejection fraction.

title: Combinatorial constructions and counterexamples with neural networks
summary: The deep cross-entropy method (reinforcement learning) finds constructions and counterexamples to open conjectures in extremal combinatorics and graph theory, including a Brualdi–Cao question about permanents. The counterexamples are verifiable; source checked was only the arXiv paper, with no institutional announcement.
ai_technology: Deep cross-entropy (reinforcement learning)
organization: Adam Zsolt Wagner

evidence.tested: The deep cross-entropy method found explicit constructions and counterexamples, verifiable by checking, including a refutation of a Brualdi and Cao question.
evidence.unknown: Not reported in the arXiv abstract read.
evidence.ai_role: Reinforcement learning (deep cross-entropy method) searched for constructions and counterexamples.

title: Two scribes in the Great Isaiah Scroll: new evidence from handwriting
summary: Independent analyses of character shapes distinguish two groups across the scroll’s 54 columns, consistent with two scribes alternating around the manuscript’s midpoint. This is statistical evidence from one artifact; the writers’ identities are unknown, and other explanations for the differences are not entirely ruled out.
ai_technology: Pattern recognition and Kohonen maps
organization: University of Groningen

evidence.tested: Independent analyses of character shapes across 54 columns separated two groups, treated as statistical evidence from one artifact.
evidence.unknown: Not reported in the abstract read.
evidence.ai_role: Pattern recognition and AI techniques analysed handwriting features to identify writers.

title: IBM designs two new antimicrobial peptides with generative models
summary: Over 48 days, 20 candidates were designed, synthesized, and tested; two showed activity against several pathogens, including multidrug-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae. In vitro and mouse tests only, with no demonstration of safety or efficacy in humans.
ai_technology: Generative autoencoder and CLaSS
organization: IBM Research

evidence.tested: 20 generative-model candidates were synthesised and tested; two were active against several pathogens, with in vitro and mouse tests.
evidence.unknown: No demonstration of safety or efficacy in humans, and no human trials are mentioned.
evidence.ai_role: Generative models designed candidate antimicrobial peptides.

title: trRosetta releases over 6,300 predicted protein-family structures
summary: Over 6,300 protein structures predicted with deep learning are available in Pfam to explore families without a known structure. These are computational models with estimated quality, not newly experimentally determined structures; this result is distinct from RoseTTAFold and the AlphaFold Database.
ai_technology: trRosetta
organization: Institute for Protein Design / EMBL-EBI

evidence.tested: Pfam models are scored with lDDT (0.6 or higher considered reasonable); the article describes no independent validation.
evidence.unknown: The article does not state limitations and says more structures are to follow.
evidence.ai_role: Deep-learning trRosetta predicted structures for protein families.

title: Mirai: future breast cancer risk from mammograms
summary: Mirai, trained on over 200,000 exams, was evaluated on hospital data from the United States, Sweden, and Taiwan. In a comparison of high-risk groups at Massachusetts General Hospital, it identified nearly twice as many future diagnoses as Tyrer-Cuzick; it does not demonstrate reduced mortality.
ai_technology: Deep learning on mammograms
organization: MIT

evidence.tested: Mirai was validated on held-out test sets from MGH, Karolinska and Chang Gung, and identified nearly twice as many future diagnoses as Tyrer-Cuzick in high-risk groups.
evidence.unknown: It does not use prior imaging and is still being validated in more diverse populations, and it does not show reduced mortality.
evidence.ai_role: Deep learning predicted future breast cancer risk from mammograms.

title: Sequential X-rays to predict COVID-19 deterioration
summary: Models trained in part on 26,838 X-rays from 4,914 patients predict deterioration up to 96 hours ahead, outperforming specialists in some retrospective comparisons. This research is for hospital resource planning, not a clinical product or evidence of better patient outcomes.
ai_technology: MoCo and Transformer
organization: Meta AI / NYU Langone Health

evidence.tested: Models trained on chest X-rays are compared with specialists in some retrospective comparisons for predicting deterioration.
evidence.unknown: Not reported in the arXiv abstract read; the research is for resource planning, not a clinical product.
evidence.ai_role: Self-supervised learning (MoCo) predicted COVID-19 deterioration from sequential chest X-rays.

title: Language models identify viral regions less prone to immune escape
summary: Analysis of influenza, HIV, and coronavirus sequences identifies regions of surface proteins less likely to mutate to escape immune responses, including the S2 subunit of spike. These are computational leads for studying possible vaccine targets, not validated vaccines.
ai_technology: Protein-sequence language model
organization: MIT

evidence.tested: Language models trained on about 60,000 HIV, 45,000 influenza and 4,000 coronavirus sequences were checked against earlier findings on influenza and HIV; the SARS-CoV-2 analysis is described as not yet peer-reviewed.
evidence.unknown: Flagged SARS-CoV-2 sequences still need investigation, and it is unknown how fast SARS-CoV-2 mutates, so how long current vaccines stay effective is unclear.
evidence.ai_role: Adapted language-model methods to viral protein sequences to predict surface regions more or less likely to enable immune escape, as candidate vaccine targets.

title: 1,210 gravitational-lens candidates in the DESI Legacy Surveys
summary: Applied to DR8 data from the DESI Legacy Imaging Surveys, machine learning found 1,210 strong gravitational-lens candidates. The DESI collaboration says this is about twice the number of lenses known at the time; these are candidates, not objects individually confirmed in every case.
ai_technology: Residual neural network
organization: NSF NOIRLab; University of San Francisco, and Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory

evidence.tested: Candidates were selected by applying trained networks to survey images and visually inspecting the top-ranked ones; the sources read describe no spectroscopic confirmation or held-out test.
evidence.unknown: Not reported
evidence.ai_role: Deep residual neural networks trained on known lenses and non-lenses found 1,210 strong-lens candidates in DESI Legacy Imaging Survey DR8 data.

title: AlphaFold wins CASP14 for protein folding
summary: AlphaFold achieved a median GDT score of 92.4 across the target set (about 1.6 Å mean error) and 87.0 on the hardest targets, which organizers judged a solution to the problem of single-protein structures. DeepMind notes that protein complexes and interactions with other molecules remain open challenges.
ai_technology: AlphaFold 2
organization: Google DeepMind

evidence.tested: Blind assessment at CASP14 on recently determined protein structures: median GDT of 92.4 across targets and 87.0 on the hardest free-modelling targets, judged by the organizers as a solution to single-protein structure prediction.
evidence.unknown: Protein complexes, interactions with DNA, RNA or small molecules, and full side-chain placement remain open; not every predicted structure will be perfect.
evidence.ai_role: Attention-based neural network using evolutionary sequence alignments and residue-pair representations to predict 3D protein structure from sequence.

title: CAMEO discovers GST467, a phase-change material with double the optical contrast
summary: CAMEO, using Bayesian active learning and closed-loop X-ray measurements, identified the Ge4Sb6Te7 alloy in 19 experimental cycles (about 10 hours), selected from 177 compositions. GST467 showed twice the optical contrast of GST225 and was demonstrated in a phase-change memory device; the result concerns this library and application, not a commercial memory.
ai_technology: CAMEO, closed-loop Bayesian active learning
organization: NIST; University of Maryland, University of Washington, SLAC

evidence.tested: CAMEO ran a closed loop over 177 candidate compositions in 19 experimental cycles; GST467 was measured by X-ray diffraction, showed twice the optical contrast of the reference alloy, and was demonstrated in a phase-change memory device.
evidence.unknown: Long-term performance and larger-scale behavior are not discussed; the tenfold time reduction is an estimate, not a measured result.
evidence.ai_role: Closed-loop Bayesian active learning chose which compositions to measure next and ran the X-ray measurements.

title: A model analyzes coughs to detect COVID-19 infections
summary: A model trained on volunteer recordings recognized 98.5% of coughs associated with confirmed infections in the test reported by MIT. This is an early result on data collected online, with health status also self-reported; it is not a diagnosis or prospective clinical validation.
ai_technology: Neural networks for audio
organization: MIT

evidence.tested: Model trained on 4,256 subjects and tested on 1,064 held-out subjects from web-collected cough recordings, with results validated against official COVID-19 test outcomes; sensitivity 98.5% and specificity 94.2% overall, but 83.2% specificity in asymptomatic subjects.
evidence.unknown: Not a diagnosis for symptomatic people and does not separate Covid from flu or asthma; status was self-reported; false-positive results for healthy participants not reported; app would need approval and a larger, more diverse dataset.
evidence.ai_role: Neural networks trained on cough biomarkers (vocal cords, sentiment in speech, lung performance) combined with a muscular-degradation estimate to flag Covid-positive coughs.

title: FermiNet: quantum physics of molecules from first principles
summary: FermiNet approximates molecular ground-state electron wavefunctions from first principles. Against the coupled-cluster reference, it recovered 99.8% of the correlation energy beyond a single Slater determinant for the smallest molecules and at least 97% for bicyclobutane (30 electrons). It also modeled stretched nitrogen and hydrogen chains. These are computational results from the original work announced on 19 October 2020. The source page was updated on 22 August 2024 with a separate excited-state study; that later study's carbon-dimer error is not a 2020 result.
ai_technology: FermiNet
organization: Google DeepMind

evidence.tested: Energies compared with coupled-cluster and variational Monte Carlo reference calculations: 99.8% of the correlation energy beyond a single determinant recovered for the smallest molecules and at least 97% for bicyclobutane.
evidence.unknown: The coupled-cluster baseline scales poorly, so results apply to medium-sized molecules; the Monte Carlo method is approximate; excited-state results are within about 0.1 eV of the most demanding calculations rather than matching them.
evidence.ai_role: Neural network wavefunction, antisymmetric in its inputs, trained by minimizing energy with Monte Carlo sampling using only nuclear positions.

title: Over 1.8 billion trees mapped in Africa’s drylands
summary: Analysis of high-resolution images located and measured the crowns of over 1.8 billion trees across 1.3 million km² of West Africa. Validation used manual annotations and field data; the study counts trees but does not yet measure their stored carbon.
ai_technology: Convolutional neural network
organization: NASA

evidence.tested: Tree detections checked against manually annotated data and field data from the region; the abstract itself does not describe the validation method.
evidence.unknown: The study counts trees but does not yet measure stored carbon; the method can mistake stones for trees and gets harder with more detail.
evidence.ai_role: Deep learning (fully convolutional network trained on about 90,000 hand-marked trees) on submetre satellite imagery mapped the crowns of over 1.8 billion trees.

title: Chematica: computational synthesis planning for natural products
summary: The system plans multistep syntheses of complex natural products, with routes in a Turing-test study largely indistinguishable from human routes; three computer-designed syntheses were carried out in the lab: dauricine, tacamonidine, and lamellodysidine A. Based on over 100,000 rules plus AI, it is not modern generative AI.
ai_technology: Chematica / Allchemy
organization: Polish Academy of Sciences; Northwestern University, IBS Center for Soft and Living Matter, and UNIST

evidence.tested: In a Turing-like test, synthesis experts largely could not distinguish the program's routes from human ones; three computer-designed natural-product syntheses were carried out in the lab.
evidence.unknown: How often its routes fail across other targets is not reported in the abstract.
evidence.ai_role: The planning program combines chemistry knowledge, data-based AI routines and causal relationships to plan several steps ahead.

title: A mobile robotic chemist
summary: A mobile robot ran 688 experiments in eight days in a ten-variable space, guided by a batch Bayesian algorithm, to search for photocatalysts that produce hydrogen from water; the best mixtures were six times more active than the initial formulations. This optimizes a formulation, not a new structure; only the abstract was reviewed.
ai_technology: Batch Bayesian optimization and mobile robot
organization: University of Liverpool

evidence.tested: 688 autonomous experiments over eight days in a ten-variable space; the best photocatalyst mixtures were about six times more active than the initial formulations.
evidence.unknown: The abstract lists no limitations of this study; it notes that atomistic simulations cannot yet capture multi-scale complexity and that robots are hard to adopt widely across diverse samples and instruments.
evidence.ai_role: A batch Bayesian algorithm chose which experiments the mobile robot ran next, automating the researcher rather than the instruments.

title: AI and clinical data to identify COVID-19 from CT scans
summary: In a test on 279 patients, a system combining CT scans and clinical information reached 84% sensitivity, compared with 75% for radiologists in the reported comparison. Retrospective study on data collected in China, without evidence of effectiveness in prospective clinical use.
ai_technology: Multimodal deep learning
organization: Mount Sinai

evidence.tested: Trained on 626 of 905 patients and tested on the remaining 279 against radiologists: sensitivity 84% versus 75%, AUC 0.92, and 68% of RT-PCR-positive cases with normal CT correctly identified.
evidence.unknown: Intended for use when CT scans and clinical history are both available; CT alone may have limited negative predictive value; prospective clinical use not evaluated; specificity not reported.
evidence.ai_role: Combined chest CT findings with clinical symptoms, exposure history and lab results to identify COVID-19-positive patients.

title: An AI system predicts progression of macular degeneration
summary: The system analyzes OCT scans to predict whether the less affected eye of patients with macular degeneration will develop the wet form, outperforming specialists in the comparison described. The announcement gives no numerical metrics; preventive clinical studies were still to be planned.
ai_technology: Deep learning on OCT images
organization: Moorfields Eye Hospital

evidence.tested: Retrospective prediction of whether the second eye converts to wet AMD within 6 months: 80% sensitivity at 55% specificity, and better than five of six experts in the comparison described.
evidence.unknown: Preventive use needs prospective trials that were only being considered; 56% of individual eyes were false positives at the high-sensitivity setting; dataset size and generalizability not stated.
evidence.ai_role: Models built on 3D OCT scans and automatically generated tissue maps to predict conversion to wet AMD.

title: Cu–Al electrocatalysts for CO2 found with active learning
summary: DFT and active machine learning identified Cu–Al catalysts that reduce CO2 to ethylene with over 80% Faradaic efficiency at 400 mA/cm² (about 66% for pure copper) and 55% half-cell energy efficiency at 150 mA/cm². Synthesized and tested in the lab; the abstract does not state how many candidates were screened.
ai_technology: Active machine learning and DFT
organization: University of Toronto

evidence.tested: Cu-Al catalysts synthesized and tested in the lab: over 80% Faradaic efficiency for ethylene at 400 mA/cm2 versus about 66% for copper, and 55% half-cell energy efficiency at 150 mA/cm2; in situ X-ray absorption examined the copper environment.
evidence.unknown: The abstract does not state how many candidates were screened or list explicit limitations; full text not read.
evidence.ai_role: DFT calculations combined with active machine learning identified the Cu-Al catalysts.

title: LCLS magnet tuning with machine learning
