evidence.tested: SAA1, FERMT3, ILK and TLN1 were elevated in active-stage AS and returned toward control levels in stable-stage patients; ELISA in a separate cohort (27 active, 28 stable, 24 controls) reproduced these patterns.
evidence.unknown: This is an observational, cross-sectional plasma-biomarker study; it does not establish causal integrin-pathway activity, prognosis over time, treatment response, or clinical utility. The independent ELISA cohort had 79 participants and was drawn from the same clinical setting. The combined AUC 0.932 applies to active AS versus healthy controls; discrimination against other inflammatory diseases was not demonstrated. SAA1 has been previously reported as an AS-associated marker; the AI-supported novelty is the combined panel and the integrin-related proteins, not discovery of SAA1 itself.
evidence.ai_role: Random-forest classification accuracy/Gini importance and OPLS-DA variable-importance scores were combined with proteomic fold-change and significance terms to rank candidate proteins. The team then measured the four prioritized proteins by ELISA in an independent cohort.

title: Machine-learning-guided electrochemical screening isolates five new reaction products
summary: A machine-learning-guided, chemist-in-the-loop screen predicted electrochemical reactivity for 38,865 potential partners with 1,4-dicyanobenzene (DCB). Automated tests of 20 prioritized, previously untested partners yielded DCB conversion in 16; five produced an isolable major product judged of synthetic or mechanistic interest. The reported examples include a silyl-enol-ether coupling and electrochemical benzylic arylation of benzyltrimethylsilane with DCB, plus three mechanistically unexpected products.
ai_technology: Machine-learning-guided reaction-competency classifier using a DFT-informed molecular representation
organization: Massachusetts Institute of Technology; collaborating institutions

evidence.tested: Automated tests of 20 prioritized, previously untested partners yielded DCB conversion in 16; five produced an isolable major product judged of synthetic or mechanistic interest.
evidence.unknown: This is an early reaction-discovery demonstration under one fixed DCB electrolysis system, not a general reaction predictor or optimized synthetic platform. Seven of the 16 DCB-converting selected reactions gave complex mixtures without an appreciable single isolated product; five yielded isolable major products, reported at low yields and without method optimization. DCB conversion alone does not establish a product identity, and the three mechanistically ambiguous outcomes require further study.
evidence.ai_role: The model screened a 38,865-member virtual set for reaction competency and, with chemist selection, prioritized 20 new partners for automated electrolysis. The experiments measured DCB conversion, then product analysis isolated and characterized five major products from the selected set.

title: Machine-learning-guided photoredox design experimentally enables three transformations
summary: A workflow combining a variational-autoencoder latent space of 11,069 literature photoredox reactions with random-forest catalyst/reagent recommendations was used to propose three transformations. Experiments synthesized a previously inaccessible substituted dihydroquinolinone 43 using fac-Ir(ppy)3, a related oxidative cross-coupling product 46 in 64% yield, and heterocycle product 49 in 74% yield. The paper presents these as experimentally validated transformations identified through model-assisted precedent retrieval and condition selection.
ai_technology: Variational autoencoder for reaction-space navigation and random-forest multilabel catalyst/reagent recommendation
organization: Wuhan University; HOURS Inc.; collaborating institutions

evidence.tested: Experiments synthesized a previously inaccessible substituted dihydroquinolinone 43 using fac-Ir(ppy)3, a related oxidative cross-coupling product 46 in 64% yield, and heterocycle product 49 in 74% yield.
evidence.unknown: The work is a human-guided photoredox design workflow, not autonomous synthesis. The three examples were selected by researchers and use a literature-trained model; the paper establishes feasibility for these tested transformations, not general transfer or broad yield improvement. Reported 64% and 74% yields apply only to the specific demonstrated products; further optimization and substrate-scope work are needed.
evidence.ai_role: The VAE organized 11,069 literature-derived reactions to retrieve traceable precedents; random-forest models recommended catalyst and reagent classes for proposed reactant-product pairs. Chemists used the model-suggested conditions to test three transformations, including two modifications beyond the reported precedent and one previously undocumented photoredox synthesis, then measured isolated product yields.

title: Cross-tissue machine learning prioritizes a 13-gene rheumatoid-arthritis activity score
summary: A machine-learning feature-selection pipeline integrated public whole-blood (1,885 samples) and synovial-tissue (284 samples) transcriptomic datasets and selected a 13-gene rheumatoid-arthritis score. Across five independent transcriptomic datasets, the score tracked DAS28 disease activity, distinguished rheumatoid arthritis from osteoarthritis, separated polyarticular juvenile idiopathic arthritis from healthy controls, and was associated with treatment effects. In an independent immunoblot cohort, two of six tested proteins, TNFAIP6/TSG-6 and HSP90AB1/HSP90, were confirmed.
ai_technology: Cross-tissue machine-learning feature-selection pipeline for transcriptomic data
organization: University of California, San Francisco; Oregon Health & Science University

evidence.tested: In an independent immunoblot cohort, two of six tested proteins, TNFAIP6/TSG-6 and HSP90AB1/HSP90, were confirmed.
evidence.unknown: The transcriptomic inputs were previously published datasets and the reported clinical associations are observational; the study does not establish a deployable diagnostic test or causal disease mechanism. The independent protein follow-up confirmed two of six proteins tested, not the entire 13-gene panel, and validation in larger prospective cohorts is needed. Treatment-effect association should not be interpreted as prospective prediction of individual response.
evidence.ai_role: The pipeline selected a compact 13-gene signature from public blood and synovial expression datasets; the study evaluated its association with disease activity and diagnostic distinctions across five independent transcriptomic datasets, then tested six selected proteins by immunoblot in a separate patient cohort.

title: Random-forest metabolite profiling reduces false-positive newborn screens for four inherited disorders
summary: A 121-analyte LC–MS/MS panel combined established markers, untargeted-metabolomics features and chromatographically resolved isobars with random-forest classification of California newborn-screen dried blood spots. In 883 archived infant samples, the study reports that the second-tier approach maintained 100% sensitivity while reducing false positives by 83% for glutaric acidemia type I, 84% for methylmalonic acidemia, 100% for ornithine transcarbamylase deficiency and 51% for very-long-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase deficiency. Several long-chain acylcarnitine and hydroxy-acylcarnitine isobar features contributed to classification, although their chemical identities were unresolved.
ai_technology: Random Forest classifier trained on targeted LC–MS/MS metabolite profiles
organization: Stanford Health Care; Yale University; California Department of Public Health

evidence.tested: In 883 archived infant samples, the study reports that the second-tier approach maintained 100% sensitivity while reducing false positives by 83% for glutaric acidemia type I, 84% for methylmalonic acidemia, 100% for ornithine transcarbamylase deficiency and 51% for very-long-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase deficiency.
evidence.unknown: This was a proof-of-principle second-tier simulation on residual archived California newborn-screen specimens, not a prospective implementation study. The validation sample was not a fully independent external set, and archived-sample degradation and processing batch effects limited biomarker discovery; some discriminating isobar identities and biological significance remain unknown. The reported sensitivity and false-positive reductions are cohort-specific and do not establish improved health outcomes or routine clinical utility.
evidence.ai_role: The classifier modeled multianalyte profiles from true-positive and false-positive screen-positive samples to distinguish the groups for four inherited metabolic disorders. Feature-importance analysis showed that complex profiles, including unresolved long-chain acylcarnitine/hydroxy-acylcarnitine isobars, contributed to classification; the model's second-tier performance was assessed against known case status.

title: 3D-HiChAT predicts embryonic enhancer hubs validated by CRISPR interference
summary: A random-forest model integrating ATAC-seq, H3K27ac ChIP-seq and HiChIP data predicted enhancer effects across mouse trophoblast stem cells, embryonic stem cells and extraembryonic endoderm cells. CRISPRi tests supported a shared Enh14 hub regulating both Tfcp2l1 and Gli2 in embryonic stem cells, and an Enh4 hub linked to seven genes in extraembryonic endoderm; four of those seven showed expression reductions as predicted. Across 40 tested enhancer-promoter pairs, experiments yielded 12 true positives and 13 true negatives, with overall prediction accuracy 0.71.
ai_technology: 3D-HiChAT, an optimized Random Forest model combining chromatin accessibility, H3K27ac and 3D HiChIP connectivity features
organization: Weill Cornell Medicine; New York Genome Center; collaborating institutions

evidence.tested: CRISPRi tests supported a shared Enh14 hub regulating both Tfcp2l1 and Gli2 in embryonic stem cells, and an Enh4 hub linked to seven genes in extraembryonic endoderm; four of those seven showed expression reductions as predicted.
evidence.unknown: The experiments were performed in mouse-derived cell lines, not intact embryos or human cells. Only selected predictions were tested; the 40-pair validation had 12 true positives, 13 true negatives and an overall reported accuracy of 0.71, leaving discordant/uncertain pairs. The Enh14 and Enh4 results support specific cell-type-dependent regulatory hubs but do not establish the full genome-wide predicted map as experimentally validated or prove developmental phenotypes in vivo.
evidence.ai_role: The model used 1D and 3D chromatin features to rank genome-wide enhancer-promoter pairs by predicted expression impact after in-silico enhancer perturbation. Researchers selected predictions for CRISPRi validation and measured target-gene expression by RT-qPCR; the paper reports specific validated multi-gene enhancer hubs and positive/negative prediction rates across 40 pairs.

title: CellOracle-guided zebrafish perturbations identify axial-mesoderm effects of noto and lhx1a loss
summary: The CellOracle machine-learning workflow used single-cell gene-regulatory networks to prioritize transcription factors for perturbation in zebrafish development. CRISPR/Cas9 tests confirmed a model-predicted, previously unreported increase in prechordal-plate differentiation after loss of noto, alongside the known loss of notochord. Model-prioritized lhx1a loss also inhibited axial-mesoderm differentiation: single-cell RNA-seq found expansion of early notochord cells and reductions in later notochord and prechordal-plate populations; orthogonal RNA assays supported reduced notochord/prechordal markers.
ai_technology: CellOracle, a machine-learning gene-regulatory-network model with in-silico transcription-factor perturbation
organization: Washington University in St. Louis; collaborating institutions

evidence.tested: CRISPR/Cas9 tests confirmed a model-predicted, previously unreported increase in prechordal-plate differentiation after loss of noto, alongside the known loss of notochord.
evidence.unknown: Evidence is from zebrafish crispants during embryonic development, not stable mutants or mammalian/human systems; the authors report no gross morphological change despite transcriptomic/cell-population effects. The CellOracle model depends on inferred networks and makes cell-state-shift predictions, not direct causal proof of all inferred edges. A later unreviewed 2024 preprint raises implementation and benchmarking concerns, particularly about its use of ATAC-seq for distal regulatory interactions and comparisons with other GRN tools; this record relies only on the specific perturbation predictions tested experimentally and does not adopt the paper's broader benchmarking claims.
evidence.ai_role: The model built context-specific networks from single-cell data, simulated transcription-factor loss, and prioritized noto and lhx1a for experimental follow-up. Researchers used CRISPR/Cas9 crispants, single-cell RNA-seq and marker assays to test the predicted zebrafish cell-fate effects; the prechordal-plate increase after noto loss was reported as previously unrecognized.

title: AcRanker-guided discovery of AcrIIA20 and AcrIIA21 anti-CRISPR proteins
summary: AcRanker, an XGBoost ranking model using amino-acid sequence features, ranked proteins from prophage regions in self-targeting Streptococcus genomes. Experimental testing identified two previously unknown type II-A anti-CRISPRs: AcrIIA20 (ML1), which strongly inhibited Streptococcus iniae Cas9 and weakly inhibited S. pyogenes Cas9, and AcrIIA21 (ML8), which inhibited S. pyogenes, S. aureus and S. iniae Cas9 with lower potency.
ai_technology: AcRanker, an XGBoost pairwise ranking model trained on amino-acid composition and grouped di- and tri-mer features
organization: University of California, Berkeley; Monash University; University of Melbourne

evidence.tested: Experimental testing identified two previously unknown type II-A anti-CRISPRs: AcrIIA20 (ML1), which strongly inhibited Streptococcus iniae Cas9 and weakly inhibited S. pyogenes Cas9, and AcrIIA21 (ML8), which inhibited S. pyogenes, S. aureus and S. iniae Cas9 with lower potency.
evidence.unknown: The authors selected 10 candidates for follow-up, successfully purified nine and reported three validated candidates across their experiments, including ML3/AcrIIA12, which had also been identified separately as an LmoCas9 inhibitor during the study. AcrIIA20 and AcrIIA21 were roughly tenfold less potent against SpyCas9 than the established AcrIIA4 control; tested potency and host range are assay-specific. The 2025 Evo paper reports distinct generated proteins EvoAcr1–5 and separate assays; shared anti-CRISPR function does not make these identical discoveries.
evidence.ai_role: The model ranked candidate proteins from predicted prophage regions for anti-CRISPR likelihood; the researchers selected candidates from those rankings and biochemically tested them. It directly prioritized the proteins later named AcrIIA20 and AcrIIA21, whose Cas9 inhibition was measured in vitro.

title: AI-prioritized CRISPR screen identifies ALOX5 and OXTR as regulators of keratinocyte IL17RA in psoriasis
summary: A genome-wide CRISPR knockout screen in primary human epidermal keratinocytes, combined with VirtualCRISPR language-model prioritization, identified ALOX5 and OXTR as previously underappreciated cell-intrinsic regulators of surface IL17RA. Targeted knockout in keratinocytes from two adult donors reduced IL17RA and inflammatory cytokine secretion. Topical inhibition of ALOX5 or OXTR also reduced disease signs in an imiquimod mouse model of psoriasiform dermatitis.
ai_technology: VirtualCRISPR, a functional-genomics language-model framework trained on BioGRID-ORCS screens
organization: Biohub; Northwestern University; University of Chicago

evidence.tested: A genome-wide CRISPR knockout screen in primary human epidermal keratinocytes, combined with VirtualCRISPR language-model prioritization, identified ALOX5 and OXTR as previously underappreciated cell-intrinsic regulators of surface IL17RA.
evidence.unknown: The genetic validation used primary cells from two donors, while therapeutic effects were tested in an imiquimod-induced mouse model, not patients. The screen provided the initial unbiased hits; the AI supplied an orthogonal novelty-prioritization layer and did not itself measure biological effects. The paper reports a provisional patent application covering methods and findings. No clinical efficacy, safety or topical treatment benefit in humans is established.
evidence.ai_role: After the unbiased genome-wide CRISPR screen, VirtualCRISPR scored whether perturbing each gene in primary adult keratinocytes would alter IL17RA expression. The authors combined screen enrichment with the model’s lower prior probability for noncanonical hits to prioritize high-novelty regulators; targeted CRISPR knockout and pharmacologic mouse experiments tested the resulting biology.

title: CellOracle-guided pancreatic islet differentiation experiments reveal STAT1 and ZEB1 lineage roles
summary: A digital model built from 400,603 cells across 61 single-cell datasets used CellOracle gene-regulatory-network inference and in-silico transcription-factor perturbations to nominate regulators of stem-cell-derived human islet differentiation. CRISPRi experiments supported a previously unreported role for STAT1 in exocrine specification: transient STAT1 knockdown reduced exocrine markers, and JAK–STAT inhibition preserved beta-cell markers and improved glucose-stimulated insulin secretion. CRISPRi also supported a stage-dependent role for ZEB1, whose early knockdown impaired endocrine specification and later knockdown reduced off-target serotonergic cells while increasing beta-cell proportion. The date is the first preprint posting; this entry summarizes the later version reviewed in the research record, which reports the specific STAT1 and ZEB1 experiments.
ai_technology: CellOracle v0.12.0 within a digital model integrating single-cell transcriptomic and chromatin-accessibility data
organization: Washington University School of Medicine; University of Miami

evidence.tested: CRISPRi experiments supported a previously unreported role for STAT1 in exocrine specification: transient STAT1 knockdown reduced exocrine markers, and JAK–STAT inhibition preserved beta-cell markers and improved glucose-stimulated insulin secretion.
evidence.unknown: This is a bioRxiv preprint (first posted 30 April 2026; the source lists a later version on 17 September 2026), not peer-reviewed at this source date. It integrates existing datasets and reports laboratory validation in stem-cell-derived islet cultures; it does not establish human therapeutic benefit or mature clinical transplantation outcomes. Regulatory-model predictions remain context- and stage-dependent.
evidence.ai_role: The integrated cell-state model inferred regulatory networks and performed in-silico transcription-factor knockout simulations to identify candidate lineage regulators and intervention windows. These model predictions guided subsequent CRISPRi and pharmacologic perturbations in stem-cell-derived islet differentiation cultures.

title: BacterAI experimentally maps amino-acid growth requirements of two oral Streptococcus species
summary: BacterAI autonomously designed and ran growth experiments with robotic liquid handling to learn amino-acid requirements for the oral commensals Streptococcus gordonii and S. sanguinis. It learned separate growth rules for each organism and showed that the closely related species have different amino-acid auxotrophies. For S. gordonii, its neural-network growth predictions exceeded 90% accuracy after nine days and 3,024 experiments; the article also reports transfer-learning tests in larger media.
ai_technology: BacterAI, a reinforcement-learning agent coupled to iterative neural-network growth models and automated laboratory robots
organization: University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign; University of Michigan

evidence.tested: BacterAI autonomously designed and ran growth experiments with robotic liquid handling to learn amino-acid requirements for the oral commensals Streptococcus gordonii and S. sanguinis.
evidence.unknown: The measured outcomes are in defined growth media under the tested laboratory conditions, not direct evidence about nutrient exchange or health effects in a human oral microbiome. The article establishes that the two species have different amino-acid requirements; transfer learning and high growth-prediction accuracy describe the method’s performance, not separate biological discoveries. Replicate growth assays showed high agreement, but inferred rules may not cover every environmental condition.
evidence.ai_role: The agent selected successive combinations of amino acids to test based on prior growth results, executed those tests through an automated pipeline, and distilled results into interpretable growth rules. It enabled an unbiased experimental mapping of nutrient requirements from a blank slate for both species.

title: Prospective multicenter validation of TriVerity links a 29-mRNA host response to infection type and near-term severity
summary: In the prospective SEPSIS-SHIELD study, a machine-learning blood test using isothermal amplification of 29 host-response mRNAs was evaluated in adults presenting to 22 emergency departments with suspected infection or sepsis. Among 1,222 patients with valid results, its bacterial and viral scores distinguished clinically adjudicated infection status with AUROCs of 0.83 and 0.91, respectively, and the system also produced a separate score for risk of ICU-level care within seven days. The test’s high/very-high and low/very-low interpretation bands had 92–99% sensitivities and specificities for selected infection/severity endpoints.
ai_technology: TriVerity on the Myrna instrument, using logistic-regression classifiers on expression measurements for 29 host-response mRNAs
organization: Inflammatix; Stanford University; Washington University in St. Louis; 22 emergency-department study sites

evidence.tested: In the prospective SEPSIS-SHIELD study, a machine-learning blood test using isothermal amplification of 29 host-response mRNAs was evaluated in adults presenting to 22 emergency departments with suspected infection or sepsis.
evidence.unknown: This is prospective diagnostic/prognostic validation of a specific host-response test, not discovery of a causal infection mechanism and not evidence that use of the score improves patient outcomes or antibiotic decisions. Of 1,441 enrolled patients, 1,222 had valid test results; the main diagnostic analysis used 729 consensus-adjudicated patients, and 1,120 were evaluable for prognosis. Clinical adjudication is not a perfect microbiological gold standard, and the study reports lower accuracy when uncertain adjudications are included. Performance and predictive values may vary with local infection prevalence and case mix. This is distinct from the earlier VB10 10-gene signature paper (DOI 10.1016/j.ebiom.2021.103352), which used different genes, cohorts and a different diagnostic score.
evidence.ai_role: The locked machine-learning classifiers convert the amplified host-response mRNA profile into separate likelihood scores for bacterial infection, viral infection and need for critical-care interventions within seven days. The multicenter clinical study measured how those AI-generated scores performed against blinded physician adjudication and near-term clinical endpoints.

title: Deep-learning knee imaging phenotypes reveal osteoarthritis genetic and fracture associations
summary: Using knee DXA scans from the UK Biobank, a ResNet-101 model identified 1,931 more probable knee-osteoarthritis cases than health-record coding and a U-Net segmentation model estimated minimum joint-space width (mJSW). In 29,257 participants, the quantitative mJSW phenotype had substantially higher SNP heritability than the binary phenotypes and yielded 18 genome-wide-significant loci, compared with one for the image-based binary classifier and six for ICD-10 coding; only one mJSW locus was already significant in a large prior knee-OA GWAS. The AI-derived mJSW phenotype was also associated with fracture history in an epidemiological analysis, a signal not seen with the binary case labels.
ai_technology: ResNet-101 convolutional neural network for knee-OA classification and U-Net image segmentation for joint-space measurement
organization: University of Texas at Austin; Dell Medical School; Columbia University; New York Genome Center

evidence.tested: Using knee DXA scans from the UK Biobank, a ResNet-101 model identified 1,931 more probable knee-osteoarthritis cases than health-record coding and a U-Net segmentation model estimated minimum joint-space width (mJSW).
evidence.unknown: The GWAS used 29,257 quality-controlled UK Biobank participants with knee DXA images, all from the analyzed white-British ancestry subset; ancestry transferability is unestablished. DXA images were non-weight-bearing. The 18 loci are genome-wide associations for a model-derived quantitative endophenotype, not 18 proven causal OA genes; the paper notes only one also reached significance in a previous large knee-OA GWAS and many loci overlap broad anthropometric associations. The fracture result is observational and does not show that OA or joint-space narrowing causes fractures. The medRxiv preprint DOI 10.1101/2023.03.07.23286909 is an earlier version of this same study and is not counted separately.
evidence.ai_role: The neural networks converted routine knee DXA scans into two disease phenotypes: a case–control OA classifier and a quantitative minimum joint-space-width measurement. The researchers used these AI-derived phenotypes in GWAS and downstream epidemiological association analyses, increasing statistical power and revealing genetic and fracture associations that were not significant with ICD-10 case coding or the binary classifier.

title: Machine-learning-selected plasma markers distinguish Lewy body and frontotemporal dementias
summary: A six-cohort plasma proteomics study used cross-validated LASSO to select a 21-protein multiplex panel for dementia differential diagnosis. In the new DLB/FTD results, ITGAV and ITGAM were reduced in dementia with Lewy bodies and also tracked Lewy-body pathology in independent autopsy-confirmed cohorts; a panel including ITGAV, ITGAM and ERBB3 distinguished DLB from controls and Alzheimer dementia in an independent multicenter cohort. For frontotemporal dementia, NfL and B4GAT1 contributed to the panel distinguishing FTD from controls. Validation-set AUCs were 0.83 for DLB versus controls, 0.78 for DLB versus Alzheimer dementia, 0.85 for FTD versus controls and 0.77 for FTD versus Alzheimer dementia.
ai_technology: Cross-validated LASSO regression and multivariable logistic-regression models applied to Olink proximity-extension plasma proteomics
organization: University of Perugia; Amsterdam University Medical Center; CSIRO; Charles University; Sant Pau Research Institute; collaborating international dementia centers

evidence.tested: A six-cohort plasma proteomics study used cross-validated LASSO to select a 21-protein multiplex panel for dementia differential diagnosis.
evidence.unknown: These are observational plasma biomarker associations and retrospective diagnostic-validation results, not evidence that the proteins cause disease or improve patient outcomes. The work reports moderate rather than definitive discrimination, especially DLB versus Alzheimer dementia (validation AUC 0.78) and FTD versus Alzheimer dementia (0.77); external prospective utility remains unestablished. The later study reuses the bPRIDE cohorts and includes Alzheimer-disease analyses overlapping the group’s earlier 2025 bPRIDE plasma-proteomics paper; this entry is limited to the distinct DLB/FTD differential-marker and independent 21-plex validation findings. No individual biomarker is presented as a stand-alone clinical test.
evidence.ai_role: The analysis used 100-fold cross-validated LASSO feature selection to prioritize a limited set of disease-associated proteins and choose 21 markers for a custom multiplex assay. Pairwise logistic-regression models used selected markers to distinguish DLB and FTD from controls and Alzheimer dementia; the targeted panel was then measured in an independent multicenter validation cohort.

title: Deep-learning-designed enhancers drive target-tissue reporter activity in mouse embryos
summary: Researchers trained convolutional neural networks on E11.5 mouse heart, limb and midbrain chromatin-accessibility data, then fine-tuned the models using validated human and mouse enhancers and used model-guided sequence optimization to design 15 synthetic enhancers. In vivo transgenic reporter assays found all 15 reproducibly active in their intended tissue. Four of five heart designs and four of five CNS designs were exclusive to the target tissue; all five limb designs were strongly active in limb and had weaker activity in other TWIST1-expressing mesenchymal tissues.
ai_technology: Convolutional neural networks for sequence-to-accessibility and sequence-to-activity prediction, transfer learning, and Ledidi gradient-based sequence design
organization: Research Institute of Molecular Pathology (IMP), Vienna BioCenter; University of California, Irvine; Vienna BioCenter PhD Program, University of Vienna and Medical University of Vienna

evidence.tested: Researchers trained convolutional neural networks on E11.5 mouse heart, limb and midbrain chromatin-accessibility data, then fine-tuned the models using validated human and mouse enhancers and used model-guided sequence optimization to design 15 synthetic enhancers.
evidence.unknown: The functional test was a transgenic reporter assay at embryonic day 11.5, not editing or activation of an endogenous native gene locus. Fifteen selected sequences were tested (five per target), so the reported all-positive result does not estimate success across every generated candidate. Some designs had weaker off-target activity, particularly in related mesenchymal tissues. These results do not establish therapeutic efficacy or safe gene therapy.
evidence.ai_role: Models learned tissue-specific chromatin-accessibility patterns from genome-wide ATAC-seq, then transfer learning adapted them to validated enhancer activity. The trained models guided de novo enhancer sequence edits; the authors selected 15 candidates for transgenic mouse-embryo reporter testing, where each showed reproducible activity in its intended target tissue.

title: EnzGFM-Agent experimentally prioritizes activity-enhancing secreted alkaline phosphatase variants
summary: EnzGFM-Agent scored all possible single amino-acid substitutions in secreted alkaline phosphatase (SEAP) and selected top candidates from EnzGFM-1.5B and ESM2-3B for testing in transfected Chinese hamster ovary cells. Among the five variants uniquely prioritized by EnzGFM, all five had significantly higher measured activity than wild type in the reported assay; three exceeded 1.5-fold, and A46I reached 6.52-fold. This is an experimentally measured enzyme-engineering result for the tested SEAP variants.
ai_technology: EnzGFM-Agent with EnzGFM-1.5B and ESM2-3B
organization: Henan Medical University; Shanghai Jiao Tong University; Shanghai AI Laboratory

evidence.tested: EnzGFM-Agent scored all possible single amino-acid substitutions in secreted alkaline phosphatase (SEAP) and selected top candidates from EnzGFM-1.5B and ESM2-3B for testing in transfected Chinese hamster ovary cells.
evidence.unknown: The evidence is limited to single substitutions in one SEAP reporter protein tested after transfection in CHO-S cells, with three independent biological replicates; it does not establish improved activity for other enzymes, industrial process performance, or a naturally occurring enzyme function. The five EnzGFM-specific variants all differed significantly from wild type, but the study also evaluated ESM2-ranked variants and five variants shared by both models. This is a paper-specific experimental validation, not independent replication.
evidence.ai_role: The workflow scored every possible SEAP single-point substitution, ranked candidates using EnzGFM-1.5B and ESM2-3B, and selected 15 unique variants for experimental validation. The distinct EnzGFM-prioritized group comprised five variants; the paper reports significantly increased SEAP activity for all five, with A46I at 6.52-fold wild type.

title: Routine-laboratory LightGBM screening identifies monoclonal immunoglobulin positivity across independent hospitals
summary: A LightGBM classifier trained on routine clinical and laboratory data distinguished serum immunofixation-positive monoclonal immunoglobulin cases from negative cases. In an independent three-hospital cohort of 2,270 patients referred for immunofixation testing, the model achieved an AUC of 0.945, with 87.0% sensitivity and 89.6% specificity. In a subset with serum protein electrophoresis results, model sensitivity was 84.6% versus 75.3% for electrophoresis; in a separate 627-patient time-extended cohort, sensitivity was 88.2%, above each of three nonspecialist clinicians in that study.
ai_technology: LightGBM classifier selected from eight machine-learning models
organization: Xijing Hospital, Fourth Military Medical University; 3201 Hospital; Shaanxi Provincial People’s Hospital; Xi’an Medical University; Xianyang Normal University

evidence.tested: In an independent three-hospital cohort of 2,270 patients referred for immunofixation testing, the model achieved an AUC of 0.945, with 87.0% sensitivity and 89.6% specificity.
evidence.unknown: This is retrospective diagnostic validation, not evidence that screening with the model improves health outcomes or shortens diagnosis in practice. All participants had been referred for immunofixation testing at tertiary or regional hospitals; an unselected community or primary-care population was not studied. The 627-patient later cohort was time-extended but not strictly prospective. The model is an adjunct for flagging patients for confirmatory tests; immunofixation remained the reference standard, and the paper states broader population validation and clinical utility remain to be established.
evidence.ai_role: Researchers used five feature-selection algorithms to identify shared predictors and trained/evaluated eight classifiers on routine clinical and laboratory measurements. The selected LightGBM model produced patient-level MIg-positive probabilities; its diagnostic performance was measured against serum immunofixation results in independent multi-center and later-collected cohorts, including direct comparisons with serum protein electrophoresis and nonspecialist clinicians.

title: HMD-AMP mining uncovers evolutionarily remote antimicrobial peptides with validated antibacterial activity
summary: A protein-language-model pipeline, HMD-AMP, screened host and gut-microorganism genomes from nine mammalian species and nominated antimicrobial peptides, including candidates with little similarity to known AMPs. Of 91 high-confidence peptides selected for experiments, 74 showed strong antibacterial activity and 48 were evolutionarily remote from known AMPs. Four tested peptides had broad-spectrum activity at low effective concentrations and low toxicity; the most potent reported candidate showed efficacy in a mouse peritoneal E. coli infection model.
ai_technology: HMD-AMP protein-language-model pipeline
organization: Shenzhen Institutes of Advanced Technology, Chinese Academy of Sciences; Chinese University of Hong Kong; Hong Kong Polytechnic University; Broad Institute and collaborating institutions

evidence.tested: Of 91 high-confidence peptides selected for experiments, 74 showed strong antibacterial activity and 48 were evolutionarily remote from known AMPs.
evidence.unknown: These are in-vitro peptide activity results plus a single reported mouse peritoneal E. coli infection experiment; they do not establish human safety or efficacy, clinical antibiotic utility, or activity against every pathogen. Only 91 of the many predicted sequences were tested, and 74 showed strong activity under the authors’ assays. The entry is one paper-level finding; other AMP discovery records in this ledger use different candidate sequences, sources or design workflows. The model acronym overlaps an earlier 2021 HMD-AMP classifier preprint, but this 2026 paper is a separate study with mammalian metagenomic mining and experimental outcomes; they are not conflated.
evidence.ai_role: HMD-AMP used protein language-model representations and a hierarchical classifier to identify and rank candidate antimicrobial peptides from host and gut-microorganism metagenomic/genomic sequences. The researchers experimentally tested 91 high-confidence candidates; 74 showed strong antibacterial activity, including 48 evolutionarily remote sequences, and four had the reported broad-spectrum/low-toxicity profile. The strongest candidate was then evaluated in a mouse infection model.

title: AI-designed bacterial anti-defense proteins enable phage infection and plasmid retention
summary: RFdiffusion-based de novo binder design and experimental screening produced synthetic proteins that inhibited three bacterial defense systems: Thoeris and Avs1 in Bacillus subtilis assays, and DdmDE in Vibrio cholerae. Five designed proteins inhibited Thoeris and nine inhibited Avs1 in the reported screens. An engineered SBSphiJ phage carrying both anti-Thoeris and anti-Avs1 proteins replicated in B. subtilis cells expressing both defenses. In native V. cholerae O1 El Tor, two of four tested DdmDE binders improved plasmid resistance to clearance.
ai_technology: RFdiffusion de novo binder design, ProteinMPNN sequence design and AlphaFold2/3 structure-guided candidate scoring
organization: Weizmann Institute of Science; École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne (EPFL)

evidence.tested: RFdiffusion-based de novo binder design and experimental screening produced synthetic proteins that inhibited three bacterial defense systems: Thoeris and Avs1 in Bacillus subtilis assays, and DdmDE in Vibrio cholerae.
evidence.unknown: These are laboratory proof-of-concept results in three bacterial defense systems and specific strains; they do not demonstrate therapeutic phage efficacy in animals or humans. Binder success was low relative to the computationally designed candidate sets, and the authors note that a verified binder may not work against homologous defense proteins. The native V. cholerae result was tested for plasmid retention, not general transformation across clinical isolates. The earlier bioRxiv version is the same study and is not a separate record.
evidence.ai_role: RFdiffusion generated candidate binder backbones for selected target sites in the Thoeris, Avs1 and DdmDE defense proteins; ProteinMPNN designed sequences and AlphaFold-based co-folding/scoring prioritized candidates for experiments. The selected synthetic binders were tested for defense inhibition, direct interactions and ability to restore phage infection or plasmid retention. The measured anti-defense functions and engineered-phage outcomes are the paper-specific results enabled by AI-guided protein design.

title: AI-guided promoter editing raises maize ZmVTE4 expression and kernel alpha-tocopherol
summary: Basenji2-based deep-learning models and editing-plasticity analysis guided CRISPR editing of maize ZmVTE4, a gene involved in vitamin E biosynthesis. Researchers isolated a previously unobserved four-base deletion in the gene’s 5′ untranslated region; the edited allele significantly increased ZmVTE4 expression and α-tocopherol content in kernels. A separate promoter-variant assay supported the four-base deletion, rather than a co-occurring 82-base deletion, as the key change associated with increased reporter activity.
ai_technology: Basenji2-long and Basenji2-3K-NAM sequence-to-expression deep-learning models with editing-plasticity analysis
organization: Huazhong Agricultural University; Hubei Hongshan Laboratory; Yazhouwan National Laboratory; Institute of Agricultural Sciences of Xishuangbanna Prefecture; Max Planck Institute of Molecular Plant Physiology

evidence.tested: A separate promoter-variant assay supported the four-base deletion, rather than a co-occurring 82-base deletion, as the key change associated with increased reporter activity.
evidence.unknown: The demonstrated editing result concerns one ZmVTE4 allele and maize material in the reported experiments; it does not establish effects on yield, nutritional outcomes in consumers, or performance across environments and genetic backgrounds. The four-base deletion is newly engineered and was not found in the 721 accessions examined, rather than a naturally observed allele. The paper reports limitations in prediction for rice and tomato and incomplete modeling of environmental influences; claims here are restricted to the maize ZmVTE4 test.
evidence.ai_role: Deep-learning models predicted plant gene expression from regulatory DNA and used interpretability/occlusion and in-silico editing to identify promoter/5′UTR sequences likely to alter expression. The editing-plasticity predictions guided CRISPR-Cas9 targeting of ZmVTE4; the resulting four-base 5′UTR deletion was experimentally linked to increased gene expression and maize-kernel α-tocopherol. This is a measured crop-specific molecular/metabolite outcome, not merely an in-silico editing proposal.

title: Machine-learning-derived seven-protein panel distinguishes remission from active ANCA-associated vasculitis
summary: Confounder-aware machine-learning feature selection on plasma proteomics identified a seven-protein signature—AHSG, CLEC3B, COMP, F9, LRG1, MCAM and MRC1—to classify remission versus active ANCA-associated vasculitis (AAV). After targeted PRM mass-spectrometry assay development, a generalized linear model was evaluated in an independent cohort of 108 AAV patients and achieved AUC 0.94 (95% CI 0.90–0.98); combined discovery and validation performance was AUC 0.97. In the study cohorts, the panel outperformed routine CRP and ANCA titer measurements.
ai_technology: MetaDeconfoundR confounder-aware feature analysis, LASSO and Boruta feature selection, and a generalized linear model applied to targeted PRM mass-spectrometry data
organization: Max Delbrück Center for Molecular Medicine; Charité – Universitätsmedizin Berlin; Berlin Institute of Health; Charles University and General University Hospital Prague; University of Oslo

evidence.tested: After targeted PRM mass-spectrometry assay development, a generalized linear model was evaluated in an independent cohort of 108 AAV patients and achieved AUC 0.94 (95% CI 0.90–0.98); combined discovery and validation performance was AUC 0.97.
evidence.unknown: This is cross-sectional classification of disease state in patients already diagnosed with AAV, not a prospective prediction of relapse, a validated basis for stopping immunosuppression, or evidence of improved clinical outcomes. The two cohorts together included just over 200 patients with a rare disease; the authors note uncertainty from sample size and treatment heterogeneity, and the panel remains a starting point for clinical-tool development. It is an adjunct biomarker result, not proof that the seven proteins cause remission or vasculitis activity.
evidence.ai_role: Machine-learning methods accounted for clinical covariates including CRP, kidney function and ANCA-related measures, prioritized candidate plasma proteins, and reduced these to a seven-protein panel. Targeted PRM-MS quantified the selected proteins, and the GLM classified AAV remission versus active disease in an independent cohort. The measured validation performance and protein signature are the specific AI-enabled diagnostic finding.

title: CRISPR perturbation and Bayesian network inference map immune-disease regulatory cascades in primary CD4+ T cells
summary: The study used CRISPR knockouts of 84 genes in primary human CD4+ T cells and a new linear latent causal Bayes (LLCB) network-inference method to estimate 211 regulatory connections. Integrating the inferred network with immune GWAS analyses identified an interconnected module in which KMT2A was inferred upstream of JAK-STAT and IL-2 signaling regulators including IRF4, STAT5A/B and IL2RA, linking an epigenetic regulator to immune-disease-associated pathways.
ai_technology: Linear latent causal Bayes (LLCB), a Bayesian extension of linear latent causal network inference, applied to CRISPR knockout and RNA-sequencing data
organization: Gladstone-UCSF Institute of Genomic Immunology; University of California, San Francisco; Johns Hopkins University; Stanford University; University of California, Berkeley

evidence.tested: The study used CRISPR knockouts of 84 genes in primary human CD4+ T cells and a new linear latent causal Bayes (LLCB) network-inference method to estimate 211 regulatory connections.
evidence.unknown: The study perturbed 84 selected genes in primary CD4+ T cells from three donors, so this is not a complete T-cell regulatory map. LLCB “direct effects” are statistical effects adjusted for other perturbed genes and are not evidence of physical binding; effects from unperturbed genes can be attributed to modeled edges. The GWAS integration identifies pathway links, not proof that the inferred cascade causes clinical disease. A prior bioRxiv version (10.1101/2023.09.17.557749) is the same study and is not counted separately.
evidence.ai_role: LLCB inferred direct and indirect regulatory relationships from perturbation-associated expression effects across 84 targeted genes. The model-derived network and gene-program analysis, combined with immune GWAS statistics, supported the specific KMT2A-to-JAK-STAT/IL-2 regulatory finding. CRISPR perturbation supplied the experimental perturbation data; the network algorithm converted those measurements into the reported regulatory map.

title: Multicenter targeted metabolomics and machine learning identify a six-metabolite rheumatoid-arthritis diagnostic panel
summary: Across seven cohorts and five medical centers, targeted metabolomics confirmed six metabolites—imidazoleacetic acid, ergothioneine, N-acetyl-L-methionine, 2-keto-3-deoxy-D-gluconic acid, 1-methylnicotinamide and dehydroepiandrosterone sulfate—as a panel for classifying rheumatoid arthritis against healthy controls and osteoarthritis. LASSO selected the six features, and logistic regression, random forest and XGBoost models were externally evaluated in geographically distinct cohorts; reported AUCs were 0.8375–0.9280 for RA versus healthy controls and 0.7340–0.8181 for RA versus osteoarthritis in three validation cohorts.
ai_technology: LASSO feature selection and logistic regression, random forest, support vector machine and XGBoost classifiers applied to untargeted and targeted metabolomics
organization: Tongren Hospital, Shanghai Jiao Tong University School of Medicine; The First Affiliated Hospital of Fujian Medical University; Guanghua Hospital Affiliated to Shanghai University of Traditional Chinese Medicine; The First Hospital of Lanzhou University; Xinhua Hospital, Shanghai Jiao Tong University School of Medicine

evidence.tested: Across seven cohorts and five medical centers, targeted metabolomics confirmed six metabolites—imidazoleacetic acid, ergothioneine, N-acetyl-L-methionine, 2-keto-3-deoxy-D-gluconic acid, 1-methylnicotinamide and dehydroepiandrosterone sulfate—as a panel for classifying rheumatoid arthritis against healthy controls and osteoarthritis.
evidence.unknown: This is a cross-sectional case–control diagnostic study, not prospective screening or evidence of improved patient outcomes. The authors note that disease activity and treatment effects were not assessed, so prognostic and treatment-monitoring uses are not established. Performance varied across cohorts and was lower for RA-versus-OA than RA-versus-healthy-control classification; stronger platform-specific than sample-type effects were observed. Some mechanistic relevance of the six metabolites remains uncertain.
evidence.ai_role: Machine-learning feature selection narrowed targeted-validated metabolites to a six-analyte panel, and supervised classifiers combined the measurements to distinguish RA from healthy controls and osteoarthritis in multiple independent cohorts. Targeted mass spectrometry provided absolute quantification; the models produced the reported cross-cohort diagnostic discrimination.

title: Prospective Swedish cohort validates multimodal AI prostate-biopsy biomarker for recurrence and adverse pathology after prostatectomy
summary: A previously developed multimodal AI score was retrospectively applied to archived diagnostic biopsies and follow-up from a prospectively collected Swedish prostatectomy cohort. The score, derived from digitized diagnostic prostate-biopsy images plus age, PSA and clinical T-stage, was associated with post-surgical biochemical recurrence and adverse pathology. Among 143 men with evaluable data and median 8.8-year follow-up, the continuous score was associated with recurrence (subdistribution HR 2.45, 95% CI 1.77–3.38); among 88 evaluable for adverse pathology, OR was 4.85 (95% CI 2.54–10.78). Estimated 5-year recurrence was 25% in intermediate/high score versus 4% in low score.
ai_technology: Artera multimodal artificial-intelligence (MMAI) prostate biomarker combining deep-learning features from digitized biopsy histopathology with age, PSA and clinical T-stage
organization: Skåne University Hospital; Lund University; Artera Inc.; University of California, San Francisco

evidence.tested: A previously developed multimodal AI score was retrospectively applied to archived diagnostic biopsies and follow-up from a prospectively collected Swedish prostatectomy cohort.
evidence.unknown: This is retrospective external prognostic validation using specimens and follow-up from a prospectively collected cohort; it is not prospective AI-guided care, a randomized test of biomarker-guided treatment, or evidence that using the score improves outcomes. Only 143 patients had evaluable images and complete covariates, and 88 were evaluable for adverse pathology; it is a single tertiary Swedish center. The model’s earlier development setting involved men receiving radiation in North America, so this tests transport to a different population/treatment context. A 2025 conference abstract describing this cohort is an earlier presentation of the same study, not another record.
evidence.ai_role: The locked MMAI score converted diagnostic biopsy images and clinical variables into patient-level prognostic scores. The prospective Swedish cohort tested whether that model-derived score associated with the distinct post-prostatectomy outcomes biochemical recurrence and adverse pathology; associations persisted after adjustment for standard NCCN/CAPRA clinical risk measures.

title: Machine-learning-guided proteomics identifies APOC3, RAB39A and KNG1 for plaque-rupture classification in acute coronary syndrome
summary: In an acute-coronary-syndrome derivation cohort matched for plaque rupture (PR) versus intact fibrous cap (IFC), quantitative mass spectrometry measured 1,121 plasma proteins. Five machine-learning algorithms screened candidate proteins; APOC3, RAB39A and KNG1 were then significantly different between PR and IFC in an independent 85-patient cohort using ELISA. The three proteins discriminated plaque rupture better than the study’s conventional biomarkers and risk factors, suggesting a candidate biomarker panel for identifying PR among ACS patients.
ai_technology: Unbiased machine-learning feature screening of quantitative mass-spectrometry plasma proteomics using five algorithms
organization: Beijing Anzhen Hospital, Capital Medical University; Beijing Institute of Heart Lung and Blood Vessel Diseases; First Affiliated Hospital of Dalian Medical University

evidence.tested: In an acute-coronary-syndrome derivation cohort matched for plaque rupture (PR) versus intact fibrous cap (IFC), quantitative mass spectrometry measured 1,121 plasma proteins.
evidence.unknown: This was a small matched derivation cohort (110 ACS patients) and an 85-patient validation cohort, not prospective outcome prediction or a clinical-impact trial. The proteins are candidate diagnostic markers; the study does not show that using them improves management or outcomes, nor establish causal roles in plaque rupture. The publisher reports electronic publication 2024-08-06 and issue date 2024-09-15; the record uses online-first date.
evidence.ai_role: The ML algorithms selected nine candidate proteins from the proteomic measurements; the study subsequently tested candidates in an independent ACS cohort and confirmed three analytes—APOC3, RAB39A and KNG1—as significantly different in plaque-rupture versus intact-cap groups. ELISA provided the independent protein validation. The AI-enabled result is this prioritized, externally tested three-protein panel for a specific plaque phenotype.

title: Machine learning links circulating tyrosine and distinct lipid-metabolite features to diabetic kidney disease and retinopathy detection
summary: In 2,772 adults with diabetes from Singapore’s population-based SEED study, LASSO and gradient-boosting models screened 220 circulating metabolites and 19 clinical factors for prevalent diabetic kidney disease (DKD) and retinopathy (DR), then were externally assessed in 5,843 UK Biobank participants. Both outcomes shared diabetes duration, insulin use, age and tyrosine as important model features. DKD additionally selected cardiovascular disease history, antihypertensive use, lactate, citrate and the intermediate-density-lipoprotein cholesterol-ester/total-lipid ratio; DR additionally selected HbA1c, glucose, pulse pressure and alanine. External AUCs were 0.791 for DKD and 0.778 for DR, versus 0.691 and 0.760 for conventional adjusted logistic-regression comparators.
ai_technology: Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator logistic regression and gradient-boosting decision trees applied to metabolomics and clinical risk factors
organization: Singapore Eye Research Institute; Singapore National Eye Centre; National University of Singapore; Duke-NUS Medical School

evidence.tested: In 2,772 adults with diabetes from Singapore’s population-based SEED study, LASSO and gradient-boosting models screened 220 circulating metabolites and 19 clinical factors for prevalent diabetic kidney disease (DKD) and retinopathy (DR), then were externally assessed in 5,843 UK Biobank participants.
evidence.unknown: The analysis is retrospective and cross-sectional; it classifies prevalent complications and cannot establish temporal prediction or causal effects of tyrosine, lactate, citrate, alanine or lipid features. The Singapore cohort was recruited in 2004–2011 and was multiethnic Asian; about 95% had type 2 diabetes, but the study did not separate diabetes types. UK Biobank definitions and available eye-severity measures differed, and validation of moderate-or-worse DR was not feasible. Performance is modest, particularly external AUC 0.791 DKD/0.778 DR, and does not establish clinical utility.
evidence.ai_role: ML feature selection prioritized a shared set of clinical/metabolic factors and distinct DKD- and DR-associated metabolites, then built detection models externally evaluated in UK Biobank. These models outperformed traditional adjusted logistic-regression comparators in the reported internal and external validation. The scientific result is the disease-specific feature pattern and its validated detection performance, not merely an algorithm benchmark.

title: Prospective silent-trial validation of a fine-tuned pathology foundation model for EGFR mutation screening in lung adenocarcinoma
summary: A fine-tuned Prov-GigaPath ViT-g model, named EAGLE, predicted EGFR mutation status from routine H&E slides plus clinical features in lung adenocarcinoma. Across an international dataset of 8,461 slides it achieved mean AUC 0.847 internally and 0.870 in external cohorts. In a four-month prospective silent trial on 197 primary lung-adenocarcinoma samples, EAGLE achieved AUC 0.890. Simulated AI-assisted triage thresholds reduced rapid molecular EGFR tests by up to 43% while maintaining the study’s performance criteria.
ai_technology: EAGLE, a task-specific model fine-tuned from the Prov-GigaPath ViT-g pathology foundation model, combining H&E whole-slide image features with clinical variables for EGFR mutation prediction
organization: Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai; Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center; Technical University of Munich; Sahlgrenska University Hospital and University of Gothenburg; SUNY Upstate Medical University; University of Montreal Hospital Centre

evidence.tested: Across an international dataset of 8,461 slides it achieved mean AUC 0.847 internally and 0.870 in external cohorts.
evidence.unknown: The four-month prospective trial was silent: AI outputs did not guide care or replace standard testing. The 43% reduction is a simulated triage workflow at a selected score threshold, not an observed reduction in tests or evidence of improved outcomes. The cohort was 197 primary cases at one real-time deployment site, while broader retrospective/external cohorts supported generalization. EAGLE predicts presence of EGFR mutation but does not identify the mutation subtype; sequencing remains necessary before treatment. Performance was lower on metastatic samples. The paper is a distinct 2025 model iteration and validation study in the lineage of the group’s 2022 arXiv proof of concept (10.48550/arXiv.2206.10573); the prior work is cited as antecedent, not treated as a second alias or hidden as the first-ever pathology-image EGFR result.
evidence.ai_role: The AI model predicted tumor EGFR mutation status directly from routine H&E digital slides, using sequencing results as ground truth. Fine-tuning the pathology foundation model produced cross-institution validation, and real-time inference in a prospective silent trial tested generalization on newly processed clinical slides. The model score was evaluated as a screening/triage layer alongside rapid molecular testing; it did not replace genomic sequencing.

title: A six-metabolite machine-learning panel and isovalerylcarnitine findings for gastric cancer
summary: In two multicenter cohorts totaling 597 people, LASSO feature selection and five machine-learning classifiers produced a six-metabolite plasma panel for gastric-cancer diagnosis, with AUCs of 0.947–0.982 in discovery and 0.920–0.951 in validation. The panel included isovalerylcarnitine (C5), which was lower in cancer plasma and paired tumor tissue; the paper further reported a Mendelian-randomization association and cell-assay evidence linking C5 treatment to reduced gastric-cancer cell migration and invasion through calpain-associated changes in VE-cadherin and MMP2.
ai_technology: LASSO regression score feature selection with neural-network, support-vector-machine, ridge-regression, logistic-regression and naive-Bayes classifiers
organization: Zhejiang Cancer Hospital; and six collaborating clinical centers; Shanghai Jiao Tong University; Zhejiang Chinese Medical University; Wenzhou Medical University; National Cancer Center/National Clinical Research Center for Cancer, China

evidence.tested: In two multicenter cohorts totaling 597 people, LASSO feature selection and five machine-learning classifiers produced a six-metabolite plasma panel for gastric-cancer diagnosis, with AUCs of 0.947–0.982 in discovery and 0.920–0.951 in validation.
evidence.unknown: The cohorts were case-control clinical samples and do not establish population-screening performance or improved patient outcomes. The validation cohort contained 453 participants from seven centers; no prospective care-impact trial was reported. Mendelian-randomization evidence is observational genetic-instrument analysis, and cell migration/invasion experiments do not establish a treatment effect in animals or people. The 2024 IDDF abstract (DOI 10.1136/gutjnl-2024-IDDF.267) is an earlier disclosure of this same project, not a separate discovery. Source checked; independent replication not assessed.
evidence.ai_role: Machine-learning feature selection narrowed replicated plasma metabolite signals to a six-feature diagnostic panel, and the specified classifiers constructed/evaluated diagnostic models. The C5 mechanistic work was follow-up metabolomics, Mendelian-randomization, proteomic-correlation and in-vitro experimentation; the record does not imply that machine learning alone established the mechanism.

title: A seven-metabolite AI model detected renal-cell carcinoma across six validation cohorts
summary: An SVM-based screen of untargeted plasma metabolomics identified candidate renal-cell-carcinoma metabolites, which were confirmed by targeted analysis and used in the RCAID AI diagnostic model. In 1,680 participants across five hospitals, seven plasma metabolites supported AUROCs of 0.977, 0.911, 0.945 and 0.972 in internal, external, multicenter and temporal validation cohorts, respectively; validation also included late-stage and non-clear-cell RCC. The authors report six associated dysregulated pathways from multi-omic analyses.
ai_technology: Support-vector-machine metabolite selection and the Renal Cell Carcinoma Artificial Intelligence Detector (RCAID)
organization: Peking University First Hospital; and Peking University Health Science Center; Beijing Miyun Hospital; Beijing Friendship Hospital; collaborating Chinese hospitals

evidence.tested: An SVM-based screen of untargeted plasma metabolomics identified candidate renal-cell-carcinoma metabolites, which were confirmed by targeted analysis and used in the RCAID AI diagnostic model.
evidence.unknown: The study used diagnostic case-control cohorts with healthy controls, so reported discrimination does not establish population-screening performance, clinical utility, or improved outcomes. Most cases were clear-cell RCC (81%) and stage I (69%); subtype and cohort composition may affect generalizability. The abstract reports multi-omic pathway associations but does not establish causal mechanisms. Samples were collected 2019–2023; source publication date is the 2025 online-first date. Source checked; independent replication not assessed.
evidence.ai_role: The source states that an SVM was used to identify candidate metabolites from untargeted plasma profiles; targeted metabolomics confirmed selected metabolites. The resulting seven-feature AI-aided RCAID model was evaluated in six independent internal, external, multicenter, temporal, late-stage and non-clear-cell validation cohorts.

title: A gradient-boosted model detected untreated infection before antimicrobial administration
summary: The eDENTIFI gradient-boosted model estimated the probability of untreated infection during the next six hours from demographics, vital signs and laboratory results. Trained on 3,357 adult hospitalizations at two Illinois health systems and validated in 1,632 patients at a third, it achieved validation AUC 0.80 versus 0.64 for SIRS criteria. At the reported threshold it detected infection a median two hours before antimicrobial administration (47.6% sensitivity; 93.6% negative predictive value).
ai_technology: eDENTIFI, a gradient-boosted machine model using longitudinal discrete-time predictions
organization: University of Chicago Medical Center; Duke University; Emory University; Loyola University; Endeavor Health; University of Wisconsin-Madison

evidence.tested: Trained on 3,357 adult hospitalizations at two Illinois health systems and validated in 1,632 patients at a third, it achieved validation AUC 0.80 versus 0.64 for SIRS criteria.
evidence.unknown: Retrospective derivation and validation used historical hospital records from 2006–2018, and the infection reference standard was clinician chart review. The reported 10.8% absolute/46.4% relative reduction in unnecessary IV antibiotics is a counterfactual model comparison, not observed intervention evidence. The authors state prospective validation is needed; no patient benefit or implementation outcome was established.
evidence.ai_role: The model used routinely available demographics, vital signs and laboratory results to predict clinician-chart-reviewed untreated infection over the next six hours. The study tested temporal detection performance in a separate third health system; model estimates were not prospectively used to direct care.

title: Explainable neural-network analysis nominated GPC6 as a Parkinson disease dopaminergic-neuron marker
summary: An explainable machine-learning workflow applied to four post-mortem midbrain single-nucleus RNA-sequencing datasets identified cell-type-specific gene signatures that distinguished Parkinson disease from control cells across datasets (mean balanced accuracy 0.92) and nominated ten candidate genes. GPC6 emerged as a marker in dopaminergic neurons; rare GPC6 variants were enriched among Parkinson disease cases in analyses spanning three case-control cohorts.
ai_technology: Explainable neural-network classifiers with LIME feature attribution applied to single-nucleus RNA-sequencing data
organization: McGill University; Montreal Neurological Institute-Hospital

evidence.tested: GPC6 emerged as a marker in dopaminergic neurons; rare GPC6 variants were enriched among Parkinson disease cases in analyses spanning three case-control cohorts.
evidence.unknown: The expression analysis used post-mortem datasets and the rare-variant association is not a functional perturbation or proof of causality. GPC6 remains a candidate marker/association requiring further validation. The reported balanced accuracy is cell-level classifier performance, not a clinical diagnostic test. Source checked; independent replication beyond the reported cohorts was not assessed.
evidence.ai_role: The neural-network classifiers identified cell-type-specific genes important for distinguishing Parkinson disease from control nuclei across four datasets; LIME feature attribution prioritized candidate genes. The researchers then used external rare-variant case-control analyses to validate GPC6 enrichment. The model nominates markers and candidates; it does not establish that GPC6 causes Parkinson disease.

title: Machine-learning protein signatures predicted Crohn disease years before diagnosis
summary: Regularized logistic-regression and other machine-learning analyses of 178 Olink proteins identified a 29-protein preclinical Crohn disease signature. It distinguished future cases from controls with AUC 0.85 in a Swedish discovery cohort and 0.87 in an independent preclinical cohort; a separate inception cohort produced AUC 1.0. The study also reported a less predictive ulcerative-colitis signature and found that downregulated proteins related to gut-barrier integrity and macrophage function correlated with time to Crohn diagnosis.
ai_technology: Regularized logistic regression and additional machine-learning methods (L1-penalized regression, elastic net, support-vector machines and random forests) applied to Olink protein measurements
organization: Örebro University; Karolinska Institutet; Uppsala University; Linköping University; University of Gothenburg; Umeå University; Swedish population-based cohorts and BIOIBD consortium collaborators

evidence.tested: It distinguished future cases from controls with AUC 0.85 in a Swedish discovery cohort and 0.87 in an independent preclinical cohort; a separate inception cohort produced AUC 1.0.
evidence.unknown: This is a nested case-control study using biobanked samples, not prospective screening or intervention evidence. The paper reports that the Crohn signature’s AUC fell to 0.58 when preclinical twins were compared with their healthy twin siblings, suggesting inherited/shared-environment factors affect discrimination. The ulcerative-colitis validation AUC was lower (0.67). Protein associations do not establish causal mechanisms; authors call for mechanistic studies. Source checked; independent replication beyond reported cohorts was not assessed.
evidence.ai_role: Machine-learning feature selection/modeling produced preclinical Crohn and ulcerative-colitis protein signatures in the discovery cohort. The fitted signature was evaluated in an external population-based preclinical cohort, an inception cohort at diagnosis, and twin comparisons. The result is predictive association from cohort data; the paper says mechanistic studies are needed.

title: A 16-feature AI model distinguished Sjögren disease from clinically similar conditions using routine tests
summary: The retrospective multicenter SMFIF study screened routine laboratory data and used multi-algorithm feature selection, SHAP ranking and a stacked ensemble to construct a 16-feature Sjögren disease model. Across a 34,958-patient source population from three Chinese hospitals, reported AUCs were 0.923 in testing, 0.934 in internal validation and 0.964 in a 545-person external cohort. The study also compared the model with conventional autoantibody and laboratory markers and evaluated discrimination from rheumatoid arthritis, lupus, systemic sclerosis and osteoarthritis.
ai_technology: SMFIF, a stacked ensemble of five selected classifiers built from multi-algorithm feature selection and SHAP-ranked routine laboratory features
organization: Nanjing Drum Tower Hospital/Nanjing University Medical School; Suzhou Municipal Hospital/Nanjing Medical University; Huai’an First People’s Hospital/Nanjing Medical University

evidence.tested: Across a 34,958-patient source population from three Chinese hospitals, reported AUCs were 0.923 in testing, 0.934 in internal validation and 0.964 in a 545-person external cohort.
evidence.unknown: All cohorts were retrospective and drawn from three hospitals in China; the external cohort had 545 people, including 139 Sjögren cases. External calibration showed greater variability, and the authors call for prospective and multinational validation. Case groups had longer recorded symptom duration than controls and higher organ involvement, which may contribute to discrimination. The study does not show clinical impact, improved outcomes, or replacement of diagnostic criteria/clinical assessment.
evidence.ai_role: The AI pipeline screened 70 candidate features from routine laboratory tests, selected a 16-feature set using multiple feature-selection methods and SHAP ranking, and combined five base classifiers in a stacking model. The resulting score estimated Sjögren disease probability and was evaluated on a held-out test set, internal validation set and external-hospital cohort.

title: Proteomic profiling and machine learning identified an externally validated diagnostic panel and severity markers for infective endocarditis
summary: The study profiled plasma and excised vegetation samples from 238 infective-endocarditis patients and 100 controls, then used an ensemble machine-learning pipeline to select a 10-protein plasma diagnostic panel. The paper reports AUCs of 0.97 in the held-out discovery test set and 0.98 and 0.94 in two external plasma cohorts. Integrating proteomic and clinical features also produced a prognostic model for severe heart-failure status (abstract AUC 0.87). LRG1 and NDUFB4 were associated with infection severity in the cohort analyses.
ai_technology: Ensemble machine-learning diagnostic and prognostic models; the diagnostic workflow compared six algorithms and used recursive feature elimination with cross-validation to select a 10-protein panel
organization: Fudan University; Guangdong Provincial People's Hospital/Southern Medical University; Fuwai Hospital/Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences; collaborating hospitals in China

evidence.tested: The paper reports AUCs of 0.97 in the held-out discovery test set and 0.98 and 0.94 in two external plasma cohorts.
evidence.unknown: The study is an observational proteomic cohort analysis; it does not demonstrate that use of the panel improves patient outcomes or can replace current diagnostic criteria. The development comparison included 238 IE patients and 100 controls, so case-control separation may not reflect performance in an unselected real-world diagnostic population. External evaluation used two additional plasma cohorts (combined n=328); the prognostic endpoint and biomarkers are associations, not causal mechanisms. The paper's proposed NET-related therapeutic implications are hypothesis-generating and are not counted as demonstrated treatment benefit.
evidence.ai_role: Machine-learning feature-importance analysis and recursive feature elimination selected a 10-protein plasma combination for distinguishing infective endocarditis from non-endocarditis samples. The models were evaluated in a held-out discovery cohort and two external plasma cohorts. A separate model combined proteomic and clinical features to classify severe heart-failure status.

title: Blood DNA methylation machine learning signatures classified brain insulin resistance across three cohorts
summary: A machine-learning framework applied to blood DNA-methylation profiles identified 540 CpG sites that classified brain insulin resistance in adults without type 2 diabetes. In the 167-person discovery cohort, the selected methylation signature was tested in two separate replication cohorts of 33 and 24 participants, with reported classification accuracy of 83–94%. The CpGs mapped to 445 genes enriched for neuronal-development and axonogenesis annotations; 98 sites showed significant blood–brain methylation correlation.
ai_technology: Supervised machine-learning framework using blood DNA-methylation profiles; a multi-fold elastic-net approach was described in the associated institutional and conference materials
organization: Institute for Diabetes Research and Metabolic Diseases, Helmholtz Munich/University of Tübingen; German Center for Diabetes Research; German Institute of Human Nutrition Potsdam-Rehbruecke; University Hospital Ulm; University of Lübeck; University of Potsdam

evidence.tested: In the 167-person discovery cohort, the selected methylation signature was tested in two separate replication cohorts of 33 and 24 participants, with reported classification accuracy of 83–94%.
evidence.unknown: This is a biomarker-classification study, not a prospective clinical screening or intervention study. The discovery cohort had 167 participants and the replication cohorts were small (n=33 and n=24); replication accuracy is reported as 83–94%, and larger independent cohorts are needed to establish transportability. Blood–brain methylation correlations at 98 sites support a proxy relationship but do not show that peripheral methylation causes brain insulin resistance. The authors describe potential future diagnostic use rather than demonstrated clinical utility.
evidence.ai_role: The supervised model selected a 540-CpG methylation signature from peripheral blood measurements to classify participants with and without brain insulin resistance, and the signature was assessed in two replication cohorts. The model-derived CpG set was then used for differential-methylation, gene-annotation and blood–brain correlation analyses.

title: Automated methylome analysis identified candidate blood epigenetic markers for first-episode schizophrenia
summary: An automated machine-learning workflow screened public blood-methylation datasets and selected IGF2BP1, CENPI and PSME4 as candidate schizophrenia-associated methylation markers. The researchers then measured these genes by targeted qMSP in 30 first-episode, drug-naive schizophrenia patients and 30 controls: IGF2BP1 methylation was higher and PSME4 lower in cases, while CENPI did not differ. A five-feature model combining the three genes with age and sex classified cases versus controls with AUC 0.755 (95% CI 0.636–0.862).
ai_technology: JADBio AutoML platform, comparing classifiers including support-vector machines, random forests, ridge logistic regression and decision trees with feature selection and cross-validation
organization: Democritus University of Thrace; Aristotle University of Thessaloniki; University of Crete; Hellenic Mediterranean University; Foundation for Research and Technology – Hellas

evidence.tested: The researchers then measured these genes by targeted qMSP in 30 first-episode, drug-naive schizophrenia patients and 30 controls: IGF2BP1 methylation was higher and PSME4 lower in cases, while CENPI did not differ.
evidence.unknown: The patient validation was a small case-control pilot (30 first-episode cases and 30 healthy controls); its AUC of 0.755 is modest and has a wide confidence interval. CENPI methylation did not differ in the clinical samples, so it should not be presented as independently validated. The study does not establish diagnostic performance in clinical differential-diagnosis populations, prospective utility or causality, and the authors describe the signature as potentially useful for future diagnostics rather than clinically established.
evidence.ai_role: AutoML selected gene-methylation features from genome-wide public schizophrenia methylome datasets and built predictive signatures. The authors then measured the selected markers using qMSP in a separate 30-case/30-control first-episode drug-naive cohort and trained a second model on methylation plus demographic variables.

title: PICNIC machine learning predictions revealed previously poorly characterized human proteins in cellular condensates
summary: The PICNIC gradient-boosting model ranked proteins for membership in biomolecular condensates using sequence-pattern and AlphaFold2-derived structural features. To test its predictions, researchers expressed 24 poorly characterized human proteins in U2OS cells: 21 formed mesoscale fluorescent foci, and 18 met the paper’s high-confidence condensate threshold. The experiments mapped examples to cytoplasmic bodies, nuclear bodies, nucleoli or P-bodies; for example, TYW5 and RAD51AP1 showed distinct localization patterns. Across the tested set, the authors found condensate localization was not limited to highly disordered proteins.
ai_technology: PICNIC, a gradient-boosting machine-learning classifier using protein sequence co-occurrence patterns, sequence complexity/disorder features and AlphaFold2-derived structural features
organization: Max Planck Institute of Molecular Cell Biology and Genetics; Center for Systems Biology Dresden; TU Dresden Cluster of Excellence Physics of Life

evidence.tested: To test its predictions, researchers expressed 24 poorly characterized human proteins in U2OS cells: 21 formed mesoscale fluorescent foci, and 18 met the paper’s high-confidence condensate threshold.
evidence.unknown: The experimental test used fluorescently tagged proteins expressed in U2OS cells, so observed localization may depend on expression level, tag, cell type or condition. The study did not establish each protein’s endogenous localization or biological function; the authors explicitly state that condensate localization alone makes no functional claim. Three of 24 proteins did not form detectable mesoscale foci, and three additional results were low-confidence under the paper’s size threshold.
