title: Active learning identifies a high-performing four-metal perovskite oxygen-evolution catalyst
summary: A graph-based machine-learning model and closed-loop active-learning experiments identified a four-metal perovskite oxide with an intrinsic oxygen-evolution overpotential of 391 mV at 10 mA cm⁻²oxide, among the lowest reported for four-metal perovskite oxides. The study also reports recovery of several experimentally observed composition trends. This is an electrocatalyst material result; the abstract does not establish commercial electrolyzer performance.
ai_technology: Graph-based machine-learning model with active learning and closed-loop experimentation
organization: Institute for Basic Science; Seoul National University; Allchemy, Inc.; Polish Academy of Sciences; Ulsan National Institute of Science and Technology

evidence.tested: A graph-based machine-learning model and closed-loop active-learning experiments identified a four-metal perovskite oxide with an intrinsic oxygen-evolution overpotential of 391 mV at 10 mA cm⁻²oxide, among the lowest reported for four-metal perovskite oxides.
evidence.unknown: The 391 mV figure is the reported intrinsic overpotential at 10 mA cm⁻²oxide and is compared by the authors with four-metal perovskite oxides. This is a material-level electrocatalysis measurement, not a commercial device result. The reported finding is one selected composition from a model-guided campaign; the abstract does not provide a full uncertainty interval.
evidence.ai_role: The model incorporated structural-characterization data and guided iterative material selection in a closed-loop experimental workflow. The authors state that it identified the composition with the reported 391 mV intrinsic overpotential; laboratory electrochemical measurements established the catalyst outcome.

title: Machine-learning screening reveals enhanced formate selectivity of Cu–Ga for CO₂ electroreduction
summary: A machine-learning high-throughput screen of 465 binary metallic catalysts predicted previously unreported Cu–Ga selectivity for formate production in CO₂ electroreduction. Electrochemical tests of electrodeposited Cu–Ga measured a maximum formate Faradaic efficiency of about 38.4% at −1.05 V_RHE, roughly four times that on bare Cu under the reported conditions. This is a catalyst selectivity result for the tested electrode and electrolyte, not evidence of industrial-scale performance.
ai_technology: DSTAR active-motif machine-learning models with a CO₂-reduction selectivity map
organization: Sogang University; Shanghai Jiao Tong University

evidence.tested: A machine-learning high-throughput screen of 465 binary metallic catalysts predicted previously unreported Cu–Ga selectivity for formate production in CO₂ electroreduction.
evidence.unknown: The reported ~38.4% Faradaic efficiency is for the tested electrodeposited Cu–Ga electrode at −1.05 V_RHE in the authors’ cell and electrolyte, and the comparison is to bare Cu under those conditions. The paper discusses other predicted alloy outcomes too; this entry counts the single Cu–Ga study/result once. No device-scale or long-duration performance is established.
evidence.ai_role: The authors combined ML binding-energy predictions with a reaction-selectivity map to screen 465 binary metallic combinations and prioritize Cu–Ga and Cu–Pd behavior for follow-up. Experimental Cu–Ga measurements validated the previously unreported formate-selectivity prediction; the AI-enabled screening supplied the non-obvious target and selectivity hypothesis.

title: Single-station CNN analysis adds 273 visually confirmed earthquakes to the L’Aquila near-fault catalog
summary: A two-stage 1D CNN pipeline applied to continuous three-component seismic waveforms from one L’Aquila station identified 273 previously uncataloged local earthquake events during a one-month 2009 foreshock period. The study reports that 84% were assigned magnitude below 1 and that all 273 new detections were visually confirmed; the expanded catalog contained roughly three times as many new detections as the pre-existing catalog had events for that period.
ai_technology: Two-stage one-dimensional convolutional neural network (CNN) pipeline
organization: Université Grenoble Alpes; CNRS

evidence.tested: A two-stage 1D CNN pipeline applied to continuous three-component seismic waveforms from one L’Aquila station identified 273 previously uncataloged local earthquake events during a one-month 2009 foreshock period.
evidence.unknown: The analysis covers one month in February 2009 from one station. The authors report 273 new local detections and six nonlocal events among 369 windows classified as local; all 273 new detections were visually confirmed. The pipeline does not provide exact event locations, and transfer to other regions was not established. Magnitudes are coarse classes, not precise estimates.
evidence.ai_role: The detector CNN scanned continuous raw three-component waveform windows for earthquake signals; a second CNN classified distance and magnitude, enabling the researchers to find and characterize uncataloged events from a single station. The CNN pipeline generated the new event detections; authors then visually checked them.

title: Deep learning identifies MYT1L as a regulator that restricts glioblastoma plasticity
summary: scDORI inferred enhancer-linked regulatory networks from single-cell multiome data and prioritized regulators for perturbation. MYT1L overexpression restricted alternative cell states and reduced tumor growth and invasion in mice; loss of MYT1L restored malignant features. This is preclinical evidence, not an established treatment. The result was public in a May 13, 2025 preprint; the peer-reviewed paper appeared November 4, 2026.
ai_technology: scDORI; deep learning for enhancer-linked gene-regulatory network inference
organization: German Cancer Research Center (DKFZ); European Molecular Biology Laboratory (EMBL); Wellcome Sanger Institute

evidence.tested: Patient-derived cell perturbations and mouse xenograft experiments tested inferred regulators.
evidence.unknown: Clinical benefit and independent follow-up replication were not established by this review.
evidence.ai_role: Deep network inference nominated regulatory programs and MYT1L for experimental testing.

title: DeltaCata guides methyltransferase engineering with improved catalytic efficiency in vitro
summary: The accepted-paper abstract reports that DeltaCata, a geometric graph neural network predicting mutation effects on enzyme kinetics, guided engineering of methyltransferase sGmOMT2. The authors report up to a sevenfold improvement in catalytic efficiency for in vitro icaritin synthesis. This experimental application goes beyond the model benchmarks; industrial-scale performance is not demonstrated by the reviewed abstract.
ai_technology: DeltaCata; Siamese geometric graph neural network
organization: Sun Yat-sen University; National Supercomputing Center in Shenzhen

evidence.tested: The abstract reports experimental enzyme engineering and an in vitro catalytic-efficiency improvement.
evidence.unknown: Full experimental methods, industrial performance and independent replication were not assessed.
evidence.ai_role: The model predicts mutation-induced kinetic changes to prioritize enzyme variants.

title: Machine learning guides discovery of selective submicromolar CK2 inhibitors
summary: The accepted-paper abstract reports that docking, CDK-liability filtering, machine learning and error prediction guided more selective CK2 inhibitor leads. The authors report submicromolar hits and a 90% pipeline hit rate; kinase-assay figures support biochemical inhibition. These are discovery-stage compounds, with no demonstrated clinical benefit. The hit rate describes the authors' selected pipeline, not a general drug-discovery success rate.
ai_technology: Machine learning; prediction-error modeling; molecular docking
organization: University of Helsinki; Chemotargets; University of Girona; University of Turku; Åbo Akademi University

evidence.tested: Kinase-assay figures report CK2 inhibition by selected hit compounds.
evidence.unknown: Full study methods, independent reproduction and clinical outcomes were not assessed.
evidence.ai_role: ML and error prediction prioritized compounds after docking and off-target filtering.

title: Machine learning reveals incomplete concordance between DNASE1L3 genotype and cfDNA phenotype
summary: Classifiers and UMAP analyzed 129,676 prenatal-test cfDNA samples, with genotype checks in 169 selected samples. The authors report fragmentomic profiles resembling DNASE1L3 R206C homozygotes in some non-homozygotes, while some confirmed homozygotes initially lacked the profile and acquired it in later pregnancies. This extends an already-known genotype association with phenotype discordance and within-person variation; it does not establish the mechanism or clinical utility.
ai_technology: Supervised classifiers; UMAP
organization: Amsterdam UMC

evidence.tested: Existing-cohort analysis with selected ddPCR genotype validation and a small longitudinal subset.
evidence.unknown: The validation cohort was enriched for discordance; general-population accuracy and causal interpretation remain unresolved.
evidence.ai_role: Classifiers and low-dimensional embeddings identified fragmentomic subgroups and discordant cases.

title: Machine-learned potentials resolve a disorder trade-off in lithium cathode transport
summary: Using actively fine-tuned machine-learning interatomic potentials with experimental validation, the authors report that cation disorder improves lithium-path connectivity but broadens site energies, suppressing diffusion in disordered-rocksalt cathodes. They develop an energy-adjusted percolation descriptor and a Li–Mn–Ti–O design map. This is a composition-specific transport result; the review does not assign individual capacity figures to modeled or measured material states.
ai_technology: Actively fine-tuned machine-learning interatomic potentials
organization: Tsinghua University; University of Chinese Academy of Sciences; Binzhou Institute of Technology

evidence.tested: Publisher abstract describes atomistic analysis combined with experimental validation within the discovery study.
evidence.unknown: Review scope was the publisher abstract and metadata; full experimental details and capacity attribution were not assessed. Article-in-press text may change.
evidence.ai_role: Learned atomistic potentials enabled analysis of lithium connectivity and site-energy distributions.

title: GenDIReCT recovers the M87* ring from archival telescope data
summary: GenDIReCT used diffusion-based reconstruction conditioned on calibration-independent closure invariants to analyze EHT observations from 2017, 2018 and 2021. The authors recover ring morphology and estimate a diameter of 42.2 ± 1.5 microarcseconds; geometric modeling gives 42.3 ± 1.1. This is a new analysis of existing observations, overlapping the target and some data of the cataloged 2023 PRIMO reconstruction. It is not a new observation or the first black-hole-shadow discovery.
ai_technology: GenDIReCT latent diffusion
organization: CSIRO; The University of Western Australia

evidence.tested: Archival observational reconstruction, synthetic validation and geometric modeling; lower-quality epochs give less distinct morphology.
evidence.unknown: Sparse interferometric coverage and reconstruction assumptions remain limitations; physical mass estimates require separate scaling assumptions.
evidence.ai_role: Latent diffusion reconstructed images from closure invariants.

title: ProVADA steers a protein generator to adapt proteins to non-native biological contexts
summary: ProVADA steered a pretrained protein generator to produce active, drug-inhibitable cytosolic renin and deimmunized two murine antibody fragments while retaining antigen recognition. ESCAPE-seq measured reduced HLA-I peptide binding, and redesigned FMC63 variants retained CAR-T-cell killing. This summary is limited to the abstract of the October 18, 2026 version 2 preprint; the initial preprint dates to July 17, 2025.
ai_technology: ProVADA (Mixture-Adaptation Directed Annealing sampler steering a pretrained protein generator)
organization: Stanford University

evidence.tested: Renin activity/inhibitor response, antibody antigen recognition and HLA-I peptide binding, and FMC63 CAR-T-cell killing, as reported in the version 2 abstract.
evidence.unknown: Only the abstract, PMC version header and original-server corresponding-institution metadata were assessed; full author-affiliation list and full paper were not reviewed. Preserve ID.
evidence.ai_role: A pretrained protein generator, steered by ProVADA's annealing sampler toward externally defined properties while preserving functional constraints.

title: Machine learning identifies SIK1 as an epilepsy driver validated in rat models
summary: Machine-learning screening of LKB1-pathway genes in GEO data prioritized SIK1. In a PTZ-induced rat epilepsy model, SIK1 knockdown delayed seizures and shortened their duration, whereas overexpression worsened severity. The paper abstract also reports that restoring downstream NR4A2 counteracted SIK1-related effects in rescue and neuronal experiments. These are preclinical findings, not evidence of treatment efficacy in people. This summary is limited to the abstract and publication metadata.
ai_technology: Machine learning screening of LKB1 pathway genes on GEO dataset GSE143272
organization: The First People's Hospital of Qinzhou; The First Affiliated Hospital of Guangxi Medical University

evidence.tested: Gene prioritization from GEO data followed by rat SIK1 perturbations, NR4A2 rescue and neuronal electrophysiology.
evidence.unknown: Source checking does not establish independent confirmation. Review date: 2026-11-15.
evidence.ai_role: Machine learning screened LKB1 pathway genes and ranked SIK1 as the top epilepsy risk gene for experimental follow-up.

title: Deep learning ECG model separates Takotsubo syndrome from anterior STEMI, with a randomized reader study
summary: A preprint reports external validation of an ECG-image ensemble for Takotsubo syndrome versus anterior STEMI in 95 participants: accuracy 0.914 and AUC 0.970. Among 70 readers, estimated diagnostic correctness rose from 0.632 unaided to 0.864 with AI. Only the fourth phase randomized assistance conditions; AI-assisted reader accuracy remained below model accuracy. This summary is limited to the abstract and version 3 preprint dated November 8, 2026; the first version was posted October 19.
ai_technology: Self-supervised deep learning ensemble with Grad-CAM explanations
organization: North Medical Center Hiroshima City Asa Citizens Hospital

evidence.tested: ECG-image external validation and a separate four-phase reader experiment; the fourth phase randomized assistance conditions.
evidence.unknown: Review limited to abstract and original-server version/corresponding-institution metadata; full paper and historical v1/v2 contents not assessed. DATE/ID MONTH CONFLICT: publication becomes 2026-11-08 while stable ID retains 2026-10.
evidence.ai_role: Ensemble classified 12-lead ECG images; its predictions and Grad-CAM maps were shown to readers.

title: Foundation model and generative AI yield 3CL protease inhibitors confirmed at sub-micromolar IC50
summary: An AI-assisted 3CL-protease inhibitor study selected 249 molecules from about five million generated candidates and evaluated 18 using free-energy perturbation. Five molecules were experimentally tested; all five inhibited the target below 1 micromolar IC50, and one inhibited more strongly than its lead. MMELON activity predictions had Pearson R=0.72 in a blind test. This summary is limited to the abstract and November 13, 2026 publication metadata; it does not establish antiviral efficacy in people.
ai_technology: MMELON biomedical foundation model with generative molecular models
organization: IBM Research; Cleveland Clinic; Cleveland Clinic Lerner College of Medicine of Case Western Reserve University

evidence.tested: Five synthesized molecules tested for 3CL-protease inhibition after computational candidate generation and filtering.
evidence.unknown: Source checking does not establish independent confirmation. Review date: 2026-11-15.
evidence.ai_role: Generative models produced candidate molecules; the MMELON foundation model predicted activity and supported downselection.

title: AI-designed brain-penetrant HER2 inhibitor IAM1363 shows durable responses in Phase 1/1b
summary: Iambic reported updated results from an open-label Phase 1/1b study of its AI-designed HER2 inhibitor IAM1363. At the August 31, 2026 cutoff, 122 participants had received treatment across four study parts; the company reported antitumor and intracranial responses and that more than half of participants treated at 960 mg remained on treatment. This summary is limited to the company release of October 26, describing an October 23 conference poster. These uncontrolled early results do not establish comparative efficacy.
ai_technology: Iambic molecular superintelligence platform
organization: Iambic Therapeutics

evidence.tested: Company-reported safety and preliminary response outcomes from an ongoing open-label Phase 1/1b trial.
evidence.unknown: Source checking does not establish independent confirmation. Review date: 2026-11-15.
evidence.ai_role: The molecule was 'designed using Iambic's molecular superintelligence platform' and progressed to clinic in about two years, as stated by the company.

title: LLM-based virtual screening identifies two NIR-II fluorophores tested in vitro and in vivo
summary: Researchers trained a large-language-model framework to predict fluorophore emission wavelengths and used virtual screening to prioritize NIR-II imaging molecules. Two candidates were experimentally characterized and showed favorable imaging performance in vitro and in vivo, according to the abstract. The abstract supplies no quantitative imaging effect sizes. This summary is limited to the abstract and October 15, 2026 publication metadata; the candidates are imaging probes.
ai_technology: Large language model for structure-property prediction, with virtual screening
organization: Shanghai Institute of Materia Medica, Chinese Academy of Sciences; University of Chinese Academy of Sciences; Tianjin University of Traditional Chinese Medicine; Tsinghua Shenzhen International Graduate School; Shandong Laboratory of Yantai Drug Discovery, Bohai Rim Advanced Research Institute For Drug Discovery

evidence.tested: Two computationally prioritized fluorescent candidates characterized for imaging in vitro and in vivo.
evidence.unknown: Source checking does not establish independent confirmation. Review date: 2026-11-15.
evidence.ai_role: A large language model predicted emission wavelengths and guided virtual screening to choose candidates.

title: WenHai-E2E: end-to-end machine learning for global eddy-resolving ocean forecasts
summary: The November 13, 2026 paper introduces WenHai-E2E, which generates global eddy-resolving ocean forecasts directly from observations and reports better forecast accuracy than a numerical system. The abstract and publication metadata reviewed here identify no separate oceanographic discovery or specific field result beyond forecast performance. Full text was not assessed.
ai_technology: WenHai-E2E (end-to-end deep learning ocean forecast model)
organization: Laoshan Laboratory; Ocean University of China; Shandong University; Qingdao Guoshi Technology Group

evidence.tested: Forecast accuracy against a numerical ocean forecasting system, without a separate discovery in the reviewed abstract.
evidence.unknown: Complete Methods and Results were not reviewed. Observation periods, evaluation timing, forecast comparisons, eddy-event interpretation and stated limitations were not assessed beyond the abstract. The reviewed material does not resolve whether the event example establishes a scientific result beyond forecast-performance validation; no absence of such a result is inferred.
evidence.ai_role: Machine learning model produces the full eddy-resolving global ocean forecast from observations, replacing numerical initial conditions.

source_review.scope: Indexed primary PubMed abstract and bibliographic metadata; the PMC full-text route served browser verification. Complete primary Methods, Results and supplement were not reviewed.

title: Healthy neural priors improve BCI decoding in patients with motor-cortex gliomas
summary: PACT used healthy neural priors to decode hand gestures from recordings of patients with gliomas. In the reported comparison, decoding accuracy improved by more than 10%, and alignment with reference motor representations increased from r=0.66 to r=0.94. The study collected intraoperative ECoG from eight participants, four with motor-cortex gliomas and four with other gliomas. This proof of concept addresses a specific clinical population; offline decoding does not establish benefit from a deployed BCI. Review covered the abstract, affiliations and selected results.
ai_technology: Pathology-Aware Consensus Training (PACT), a neural decoder trained with biophysical constraints
organization: West China Hospital of Sichuan University; Sichuan University; KU Leuven; Imperial College London

evidence.tested: Offline gesture decoding on intraoperative recordings; selected results describe eight glioma participants.
evidence.unknown: Source checking does not establish independent confirmation. Review date: 2026-11-15.
evidence.ai_role: PACT is the decoding model; it uses healthy neural recordings as priors and learns to suppress pathological noise and reweight spatial attention.

title: A low-rank subspace of LLM representations carries most of their brain alignment
summary: A Dartmouth preprint studied which language-model features predict human neural responses during naturalistic listening. Across three intracranial/fMRI datasets and six model conditions, reduced-rank regression recovered full linear encoding performance with about 1–3% of embedding dimensions. These directions differed from the embeddings’ principal variance axes and transferred across held-out participants, less strongly across datasets. This summary is limited to the abstract and affiliation/date metadata of the October 29, 2026 preprint. It concerns measured brain–model alignment, not proof that brains use the same representations.
ai_technology: Autoregressive and masked language models with ridge reduced-rank regression
organization: Dartmouth College

evidence.tested: Linear encoding of observed intracranial/fMRI responses, reduced-rank analysis and transfer across held-out participants.
evidence.unknown: Source checking does not establish independent confirmation. Review date: 2026-11-15.
evidence.ai_role: LLM representations are the predictors of neural activity; reduced-rank regression identifies the brain-predictive subspace.

title: Wearable-based health age models for cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic risk profiling and coaching
summary: Google Research reported a wearable-based health-age model associated with subsequent hypertension, cardiovascular disease and type 2 diabetes in the All of Us cohort (22,748 participants). A companion world model simulated 12-week trajectories. In 490 blinded paired reviews, coaches preferred simulation-grounded plans in 71.4% of evaluations; physicians rated 97.6% of physiological claims accurate. This summary is limited to the November 11, 2026 institutional blog. The authors state all evaluations were offline and retrospective; clinical effectiveness and durable habit change require prospective trials.
ai_technology: Coachable health-age model, SensorWM action-conditioned world model, feasibility-constrained optimizer with a language model agent, multimodal CKM deviation model
organization: Google Research

evidence.tested: Retrospective clinical-risk modeling and blinded expert comparison of simulated coaching plans.
evidence.unknown: Source checking does not establish independent confirmation. Review date: 2026-11-15.
evidence.ai_role: Built the health-age metric and multimodal CKM model from wearable and clinical markers, forecast physiological responses to habit changes with a world model, and filtered and converted simulated habit plans into coaching text with a language model agent.

title: Bolero predicts cell-state-specific gene regulation from DNA across species
summary: Bolero predicted cell-specific responses to AP-1 activity and transferred a human-trained response model to mouse and macaque neuronal enhancers, according to Arc Institute. Its announcement also describes a computational AP-1/cofactor spacing hypothesis; these virtual edits do not establish biological causality. This summary is limited to the October 20, 2026 institutional announcement, which identifies a collaboration with Harvard Medical School and describes a 10.8-million-cell atlas. The linked paper is a preprint; full-paper methods and experimental independence were not assessed.
ai_technology: Bolero (cell-state-conditioned sequence-to-function Transformer)
organization: Arc Institute; Harvard Medical School

evidence.tested: Human-trained AP-1 response predictions compared with mouse/macaque neuronal enhancers; virtual regulatory perturbations.
evidence.unknown: Source checking does not establish independent confirmation. Review date: 2026-11-15.
evidence.ai_role: Bolero, a Transformer conditioned on cell-state embeddings, predicts cell-state-specific gene regulation directly from DNA and estimates responses in unprofiled cell states.

title: IRIS model reconstructs signaling histories of single cells
summary: IRIS inferred signaling histories from gene activity after training on human stem-cell perturbations. The researchers used it to identify a signaling intervention predicted to encourage lung development and report experimental confirmation in mouse embryos. This summary is limited to MIT/Whitehead’s October 15, 2026 announcement, which explicitly dates the Nature Methods paper to September 8. The release supplies no quantitative accuracy metrics; proposed organoid and therapeutic uses are future applications.
ai_technology: IRIS (neural network with transfer learning)
organization: MIT; Whitehead Institute for Biomedical Research

evidence.tested: Inferred cell signaling histories and a lung-development prediction checked in mouse embryos, according to the institutional release.
evidence.unknown: Source checking does not establish independent confirmation. Review date: 2026-11-15.
evidence.ai_role: IRIS learns consistent pathway fingerprints in gene activity across cell types, reconstructs signaling histories, and generated the lung-development prediction that was tested in mouse embryos.

title: Human-in-the-loop AI copilot improves topology-optimized structure design
summary: A U-Net trained on synthetic preference labels recommended regions for human edits in topology-optimization demonstrations. An L-bracket example had about 39% higher simulated linear buckling load. This validates a design workflow; physical fabrication or load testing was not established by the reviewed material.
ai_technology: Human-in-the-loop AI copilot with topology optimization (machine-learning region-flagging model)
organization: MIT; Georgia Institute of Technology

evidence.tested: Computational topology-optimization workflow demonstrations; no separate structural finding established in reviewed scope.
evidence.unknown: The reviewed demonstrations are computational; they do not establish physical load-test performance or in-service structural outcomes. Compliance and timing comparisons differ between the article text, table and abstract and were not reconciled in this review. The training preferences were synthetic, and users modified the recommended regions.
evidence.ai_role: A machine-learning model quickly identifies design regions a human would likely want to change, within a topology optimization workflow.

source_review.scope: Primary journal PDF Results, Methods, Table 1 and Discussion; indexed publisher publication metadata. Reviewed results concern computational topology-optimization demonstrations and simulated linear buckling.

title: Depth-aware machine learning for 3D reconstruction of fibrous porous electrodes from FIB-SEM tomography
summary: The October 25, 2026 paper applies depth-aware machine learning to copper-coated polymer-fiber mats and compares reconstructions with independent physical measurements. The abstract supports improved morphology agreement, but identifies no separate electrode-property or materials discovery beyond validating reconstruction quality. This source check is limited to the abstract, electronic publication date and affiliations; the full paper was not assessed.
ai_technology: Depth-aware machine learning: monocular depth estimation plus unsupervised clustering
organization: Empa, Swiss Federal Laboratories for Materials Science and Technology; EPFL; ETH Zürich; European Synchrotron Radiation Facility

evidence.tested: Reconstruction agreement with porometry, pycnometry and X-ray tomography for one fiber-mat material system.
evidence.unknown: The complete Results and supplement were not reviewed. Exact reconstruction metrics, volume/sample details and full validation caveats were not assessed. The reviewed passages describe reconstruction agreement for Cu-coated PVDF-HFP fiber mats; any material-specific finding beyond method validation and any electrochemical-performance outcome remain unassessed.
evidence.ai_role: Monocular depth estimation model, trained on macroscale images, plus unsupervised clustering to separate in-plane from subsurface material in FIB-SEM slices.

source_review.scope: Indexed primary Wiley abstract, Introduction and pycnometry Methods passage, plus indexed primary PubMed abstract and publication metadata. Complete article Results and supporting information were not reviewed.

title: AI-enhanced electrocardiography for detection and prediction of dilated cardiomyopathy
summary: In the journal abstract, an AI-ECG model trained on more than 330,000 ECG–echocardiogram pairs detected the dilated-cardiomyopathy phenotype (AUROC 0.87–0.97) and predicted later disease (C-index 0.80–0.87). In familial cohorts, five-year negative predictive values were 95.5% in Antwerp and 91.5% in Maastricht; positive predictive values were 42.4% and 39.4%. These are diagnostic and risk-prediction findings, not demonstrated clinical benefit.
ai_technology: Explainable deep learning model applied to electrocardiography
organization: Imperial College London; University of Antwerp and Antwerp University Hospital; Maastricht University Medical Center; Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center; Zhongshan Hospital of Fudan University

evidence.tested: Validated in UK Biobank, Zhongshan Hospital and Antwerp cohorts, and in two familial cohorts (Antwerp n=166, Maastricht n=177), compared with traditional ECG features and echocardiographic traits.
evidence.unknown: Review limited to the indexed abstract and publication metadata; full-paper methods and additional limitations were not assessed.
evidence.ai_role: Deep learning model trained to detect and predict the echocardiographic DCM phenotype from ECG; explainable AI-ECG outperformed traditional ECG parameters.

title: CochleaNet: deep learning analysis of cochlear connectomics and gene therapy
summary: The journal abstract describes CochleaNet, a deep-learning framework for cleared-cochlea light-sheet images, covering hair cells, spiral ganglion neurons, synapses, tonotopy and gene expression. Trained on mouse data, it was applied to gerbil and lower-resolution mouse and marmoset data. The authors say they analyzed neuron types and validated gene-therapy products but the abstract does not identify the biological or therapy-comparison findings. The date represents the 2026-10-23 journal version; an earlier preprint appeared on 2025-11-17.
ai_technology: CochleaNet: deep learning framework for volumetric image segmentation and analysis
organization: University Medical Center Göttingen; University of Göttingen

evidence.tested: Manual-analysis and prior-segmentation comparisons; applications to neuron types, gene-therapy products, gerbil cochleae and lower-resolution mouse and marmoset imaging. The abstract does not state the specific biological outcomes.
evidence.unknown: The journal abstract reports neuron-type analyses and gene-therapy-product validation without stating their specific biological or product-comparison outcomes. Complete Methods and Results, sample sizes and the distinction between tool validation and biological or therapeutic validation were not assessed. This omission does not establish that the paper contains no qualifying finding.
evidence.ai_role: Deep learning framework that reconstructs the cochlea and segments hair cells, neurons and synapses, and quantifies tonotopy and gene expression.

source_review.scope: Indexed primary Molecular Therapy journal abstract and metadata, and the author-institution page reproducing the 2025 preprint abstract. Complete primary Methods and Results were not accessed; journal and preprint evidence were kept version-specific.

title: A language-model approach to species distribution reveals alternative stable states
summary: In the journal abstract, a language-model-inspired generative model trained on about 27,000 reef-fish surveys produced alternative coral-associated and macroalgal-associated community configurations under identical environmental conditions. It also inferred core, bridging and satellite species positions and improved occurrence and biomass predictions over XGBoost and MLP baselines. The configurations are model-derived and consistent with previously described ecological regimes; independent field confirmation is not established by the abstract.
ai_technology: Language-model-inspired generative model for ecological communities
organization: Université de Montpellier; CNRS; Ifremer; IRD; Inria; University of Tasmania

evidence.tested: Fitted on about 27,000 reef fish surveys; predictive skill compared with XGBoost and MLP baselines; multistability interpreted against described ecological regimes.
evidence.unknown: Review limited to the indexed abstract and publication metadata; full-paper methods and additional limitations were not assessed.
evidence.ai_role: Generative language-model-style model that predicts each species and its biomass conditional on previously assembled species, used to generate community configurations.

title: Machine-learning mining uncovers hidden MXenes, including 11 new rare-earth MXenes
summary: The journal abstract reports that machine-learning-assisted database mining identified 33 previously synthesized but unrecognized MXene candidates. Guided by that search, the researchers synthesized seven multilayer MXenes and realized 11 previously unexplored rare-earth-based MXenes. Experiments and modeling suggested semiconducting behavior and diverse magnetic states. Review is limited to the abstract and publication/affiliation metadata.
ai_technology: Machine-learning-assisted database mining for MXene candidates
organization: Linköping University

evidence.tested: Seven multilayer MXenes were synthesized and 11 rare-earth MXenes realized; experiments and modeling assess electronic and magnetic behavior.
evidence.unknown: Review limited to the indexed abstract and publication metadata; full-paper methods and additional limitations were not assessed.
evidence.ai_role: Machine learning performed database mining to screen candidate MXene compositions.

title: PREVIA: LLM ensemble predicts PTSD risk from emergency department trauma narratives
summary: In the journal abstract, PREVIA used trauma narratives from 145 patients at two New York City trauma centers to predict PTSD assessed one month later. Reported AUROC was 78.49% ± 5.75%, with precision 46.76% ± 8.66%. On 30 randomly selected patients, its performance was comparable to one PTSD-specialist emergency clinician. The authors describe these as initial findings requiring larger independent-cohort validation; prospective collection does not establish prospective evaluation of a locked model.
ai_technology: PREVIA clinically informed large language model ensemble
organization: New York University Grossman School of Medicine

evidence.tested: One-month PTSD prediction in 145 trauma patients; comparison with a specialist emergency clinician on 30 selected patients.
evidence.unknown: Abstract and metadata review only. Authors explicitly call for larger independent-cohort validation; full methods and timing of model selection relative to outcomes were not assessed.
evidence.ai_role: LLM ensemble extracts early post-traumatic stress symptoms, risk and protective factors from narratives and produces the risk forecast.

title: The Virtual Biotech: a multi-agent AI framework for drug development decisions
summary: The Virtual Biotech journal abstract reports a human-guided multi-agent analysis of 55,984 trials. Drugs targeting cell-type-specific genes were associated with a 48% greater likelihood of reaching market and 32% fewer adverse events. The system also proposed a lung-cancer strategy and inferred possible reasons for a terminated ulcerative-colitis trial. These are retrospective associations and hypotheses, not demonstrated treatment benefits. The date represents the 2026-10-22 journal version; the linked preprint, including the same reported association, first appeared on 2026-02-23.
ai_technology: Virtual Biotech multi-agent AI framework (more than 37,000 agents)
organization: Stanford University

evidence.tested: Retrospective trial-outcome/target-feature analysis across 55,984 trials, plus computational therapeutic and trial-failure hypotheses.
evidence.unknown: Review limited to the indexed abstract and publication metadata; full-paper methods and additional limitations were not assessed.
evidence.ai_role: More than 37,000 AI agents annotated trial outcomes and integrated multimodal evidence to propose and analyze therapeutic decisions.

title: Deep learning finds an ECG biomarker for sudden cardiac death
summary: The Nature paper, published online on 2026-06-24, reports a deep-learning ECG biomarker evaluated retrospectively in Swedish data and external US and Taiwanese datasets. Its high-risk group comprised 2.2% of the sample and had a 7.0% annual sudden-cardiac-death rate, versus 4.6% for reduced LVEF; 86.1% were not flagged by LVEF. Among high-risk patients with defibrillators, sudden cardiac death was 54.4% lower than model-expected, an observational association subject to confounding and not proof of benefit.
ai_technology: Deep learning ECG model with a generative ECG waveform model for visualization
organization: University of California, Berkeley; University of Chicago; Massachusetts Institute of Technology; Halmstad University; Region Halland; University of Gothenburg; Sahlgrenska University Hospital

evidence.tested: Existing Swedish ECG/death-certificate data, a held-out lockbox created before analysis, external US ventricular-arrhythmia and Taiwanese arrhythmic-arrest evaluations; observational defibrillator associations.
evidence.unknown: Main paper reviewed; supplementary attachments not read. The authors explicitly identify residual confounding and the need for randomized testing of defibrillator benefit in model-high-risk patients.
evidence.ai_role: Deep learning model discovered the predictive ECG waveform pattern; generative model used to visualize it.

title: Deep learning controls electrical stimulation patterns in human visual cortex
summary: The Neuron abstract reports a deep-learning framework trained on trial-resolved recordings from a bidirectional human visual-cortex implant. A learned inverse network and gradient-based optimizer shaped stimulation-evoked population activity, achieved targets at lower currents and elicited more consistent perception than conventional methods. This is an experimental neural-control result, not evidence of restored functional sight. The paper was first published online on 2026-08-07; review here is limited to its abstract and metadata.
ai_technology: Deep learning inverse network and gradient-based optimizer for neural stimulation
organization: University of Zurich; ETH Zurich; University of California, Santa Barbara; Miguel Hernández University

evidence.tested: Within-study human visual-cortex stimulation experiments comparing two learned control approaches with conventional methods; lower currents and more consistent reported percepts.
evidence.unknown: Complete abstract and metadata reviewed. Participant count, implant duration, long-term performance and functional-vision outcomes were not assessed; full-text XML retrieval returned HTTP 500.
evidence.ai_role: Deep learning model trained on trial-resolved neural recordings to synthesize and optimize stimulation patterns.

title: Machine learning guided design of strong transcriptional activation domains
summary: The preprint abstract reports computational generation of 500,000 candidate transcriptional activation domains and selection of 18,750 high-scoring sequences for yeast experiments using sequence-to-function models including three neural networks. More than 90% of 16,770 well-measured sequences functioned as activation domains. Some designed sequences retained activity in fungi, plants and human cells. Model agreement motivated the MADRIGAL consensus predictor. Review is limited to the abstract and original-server metadata.
ai_technology: Neural-network sequence-to-function models (three networks); consensus predictor MADRIGAL
organization: University of California, Berkeley

evidence.tested: 18,750 selected sequences were tested experimentally in yeast; over 90% of 16,770 well-measured sequences functioned as activation domains, and some retained function in fungi, plants and human cells.
evidence.unknown: Review limited to the indexed abstract and publication metadata; full-paper methods and additional limitations were not assessed.
evidence.ai_role: Neural networks scored sequences generated from known activation-domain-like sequences; high-scoring sequences were selected for experimental validation and the consensus model MADRIGAL was developed.

title: Cross-state representation learning enables prospective discovery of dynamic protein allosteric sites
summary: The preprint abstract reports that AllositeUltra recovered allosteric sites among its top three predictions in 65.2% of apo structures and 70.6% of substrate-bound structures. More importantly, application to MAGI2 identified a previously unrecognized interdomain pocket, tested by small-molecule screening and X-ray crystallography. This within-study experimental finding qualifies separately from the benchmark. Review is limited to the abstract and original-server metadata.
ai_technology: AllositeUltra (structure-aware protein language model combined with physical dynamics; residue-guided candidate supplementation)
organization: Shanghai Jiao Tong University

evidence.tested: The predicted MAGI2 interdomain pocket was validated experimentally through small-molecule screening and X-ray crystallography; benchmark recovery was measured on apo and substrate-bound structures.
evidence.unknown: Review limited to the indexed abstract and publication metadata; full-paper methods and additional limitations were not assessed.
evidence.ai_role: A deep-learning model predicted allosteric sites on apo and substrate-bound structures and was applied prospectively to MAGI2 and proteome-wide.

title: Generative design of de novo AAV vectors with unique serological profiles
summary: The preprint abstract reports a variational autoencoder trained on natural AAV sequences to generate capsids. More than 255 designs were synthesized and tested in vitro. Seven transduced human cells at over 50% efficiency; four of those avoided neutralization by every AAV-reactive human serum sample tested, at the reported NT50 threshold below 1:50. This establishes in-vitro capsid properties, not in-vivo delivery or clinical efficacy. Review is limited to the abstract and original-server metadata.
ai_technology: Variational autoencoder (generative model of AAV capsid sequences)
organization: University of Toronto

evidence.tested: More than 255 AI-generated capsid designs were synthesized and tested in vitro; seven transduced human cells above 50% efficiency and four avoided neutralizing antibodies in all reactive human sera.
evidence.unknown: Review limited to the indexed abstract and publication metadata; full-paper methods and additional limitations were not assessed.
evidence.ai_role: A variational autoencoder learned AAV sequence constraints from natural sequences and generated functional capsid proteins de novo, with a second design campaign exploring uncertain regions.

title: Antibody design across observed and forecasted antigenic evolution
summary: The Germinal Multi preprint abstract reports antibodies designed against several antigen variants at once. Experimental screens of tens of designs per campaign found binders to resistance-associated EGFR variants and neutralizers of historical SARS-CoV-2 variants, including variants withheld from design. Redesign of BD55-1205 restored neutralization of a forecast-guided engineered escape variant while retaining parental-variant activity. The escape result concerns an engineered variant, not a demonstrated future circulating strain. Review is limited to the abstract and original-server metadata.
ai_technology: Germinal Multi (computational antibody design framework); evolutionary forecasting model
organization: Stanford University

evidence.tested: Tens of designs per campaign were screened experimentally; designs bound EGFR variants and neutralized SARS-CoV-2 variants, including variants withheld from the design process.
evidence.unknown: Review limited to the indexed abstract and publication metadata; full-paper methods and additional limitations were not assessed.
evidence.ai_role: Germinal Multi computationally optimized one antibody paratope against multiple antigen variants, and an evolutionary forecasting model guided construction of an escape variant and antibody redesign.

title: APOLLAI, a multimodal AI system, versus EMS personnel for prehospital detection of stroke-related deficits
summary: The medRxiv abstract reports APOLLAI evaluation on video/audio recordings from 295 suspected-stroke patients at Nîmes University Hospital, against seven-neurologist consensus labels for five NIHSS items. Global sensitivity was 78.5% versus 59.4% for EMS personnel, specificity 87.0% versus 85.9%, and AUC 0.882. These are diagnostic comparisons on recorded patient data; the authors call for prospective validation in real EMS conditions.
ai_technology: APOLLAI (computer vision, audio deep learning and SVM fusion classifier)
organization: AI-Stroke; Nîmes University Hospital

evidence.tested: Recorded cases from 295 suspected-stroke patients; AI and EMS assessments compared with consensus labels for five neurological tasks.
evidence.unknown: Complete abstract and original-server metadata reviewed; full methods, model-selection timing and external EMS generalizability were not assessed. Authors explicitly call for real-world prospective validation.
evidence.ai_role: A multimodal machine-learning system detected stroke-related neurological deficits from video and audio recordings and was compared with clinicians' assessments.

title: AI agent maps proton-gated water loss in perrhenate-catalysed deoxydehydration
summary: The paper reports a computational mechanism for perrhenate-catalysed deoxydehydration: proton-assisted water loss enables ring closure and alcohol reduction. Under human-defined hypotheses, a Claude Code agent located transition states, which the authors validated. Coupled-cluster-anchored microkinetic modeling predicted a rate increase of about eight orders of magnitude over the best proton-free pathway. At matched conversion conditions, modeled barriers were consistent with the 31.5–34.0 kcal/mol window inferred from previously reported experimental turnover; this was not a new wet-lab demonstration.
ai_technology: Claude Code LLM agent for human-directed reaction-network and transition-state search, combined with electronic-structure calculations and microkinetic modeling
organization: KU Leuven

evidence.tested: Agent-located transition states verified by the authors; computed energetics, reaction-network and microkinetic consistency checks; comparisons to existing turnover-derived barrier estimates.
evidence.unknown: Main paper reviewed; supplementary files were not read. The mechanism and rate changes are predictions compared with prior experimental kinetics, not a new experimental confirmation.
evidence.ai_role: Claude Code carried out calculation/search/triage workflows for author-specified mechanistic hypotheses; authors validated the located stationary points.

title: ORI engineers active lysozymes, heat-tolerant chitinases and dual-activity enzymes
summary: Tencent researchers used ontology-conditioned generation and experimental feedback to engineer enzymes. In the reported assays, lysozyme TX-RL15 exceeded the earlier TX-L6 design by 66-fold and hen egg-white lysozyme by over two orders of magnitude. Chitinase TX-SC2 retained activity after incubation at 85 °C; selected proteins combined lysozyme and chitinase activity. These are bounded biochemical results. The date represents initial journal publication; the version of record followed on May 7, 2026.
ai_technology: ORI; protein generation model (PGM); unified sequence model (USM)
organization: Tencent AI for Life Sciences Lab

evidence.tested: Expression, enzyme-activity and heat-treatment assays on selected generated proteins.
evidence.unknown: Separate supplements and independent replication not assessed. Assay-specific advantages do not establish industrial or clinical outcomes.
evidence.ai_role: Ontology-conditioned generation and reinforcement learning from experimental feedback.

title: ERTransformer-generated TCR candidates activate T cells in defined receptor contexts
summary: ERTransformer generated epitope-conditioned TCR β-chain CDR3 candidates. Flow-cytometry experiments found selected artificial TCRs induced activation comparable to or greater than natural controls in defined TCR/pMHC contexts. This represents the September 2026 journal report; an ERTransformer precursor was posted October 20, 2023. The earlier report does not establish that these journal wet-lab results were already public.
ai_technology: ERTransformer; EpitopeBERT; ReceptorBERT
organization: Tencent AI for Life Sciences Lab; City University of Hong Kong; The University of Hong Kong; Xijing Hospital of Digestive Diseases; Harvard Medical School, Harvard University; Monash University

evidence.tested: Selected generated candidates tested for T-cell activation by flow cytometry.
evidence.unknown: Full experimental methods and supplements not assessed: publisher rendering exposed abstract and metadata. General specificity, safety and clinical outcomes are not established by this review.

title: HuDiff humanizes antibodies and nanobodies while retaining measured binding
summary: HuDiff generated humanized variants of a murine SARS-CoV-2 RBD antibody and two alpaca nanobodies. Bio-layer interferometry measured 0.15 nM affinity for the best humanized antibody versus 0.12 nM for its parent; a humanized nanobody measured 2.52 nM versus 5.47 nM. The journal abstract also reports viral neutralization. The October 2025 journal date follows an October 25, 2024 precursor describing one antibody and one nanobody.
ai_technology: HuDiff-Ab; HuDiff-Nb
organization: School of Basic Medical Sciences, Lanzhou University; Tencent AI Lab; Fudan University; Peking University

evidence.tested: Newly humanized molecules underwent binding assays; journal abstract reports neutralization.
evidence.unknown: Main journal methods are subscription content and were not assessed. Humanness scores do not establish reduced human immunogenicity or clinical safety.
evidence.ai_role: Adaptive autoregressive diffusion generates humanized framework sequences from CDR inputs.

title: tFold designs binding antibodies against four defined antigens
summary: Tencent researchers generated antibodies against influenza hemagglutinin, PD-1, PD-L1 and SARS-CoV-2 RBD, followed by phage-display screening and SPR characterization. Anti-SC2RBD-H330 showed neutralization IC50 of 0.42 nM. Screening remained extensive, and some confident epitope predictions failed competition tests. The date represents initial journal publication, preceding the January 19, 2026 version of record; a tFold precursor was posted February 8, 2024.
ai_technology: tFold System; tFold-Ab; tFold-Ag; AlphaFold-Multimer
organization: Tencent AI for Life Sciences Lab

evidence.tested: Binding and competition assays on generated antibodies; RBD-antibody neutralization.
evidence.unknown: Separate supplements and independent replication not assessed. First-public dates of individual journal experiments were not established by precursor version comparison.
evidence.ai_role: Generates CDR sequences and predicts complexes for structure-guided filtering.

title: AI-assisted macaque cortex atlas reveals regional cell-type organization
summary: AI-assisted segmentation and Spatial-ID annotation helped map 264 transcriptome-defined cell types across the macaque cortex. Regional cell-type composition tracked cortical hierarchy, and cross-species comparisons identified primate-specific types enriched in layer 4. This is the July 12, 2023 journal version; the atlas is observational, uses male monkeys, and has limited transcript capture per spatial cell.
ai_technology: AI-assisted cell segmentation; Spatial-ID (deep neural network and graph convolutional network)
organization: Chinese Academy of Sciences; BGI-Research; Tencent AI Lab

evidence.tested: New macaque tissue measurements and spatial maps were compared across sections and biological replicates; this supports a bounded anatomical result, not causal brain function.
evidence.unknown: Not assessed: independent replication and exhaustive supplementary material. The paper identifies limited transcript sensitivity and absence of female subjects.
evidence.ai_role: Image segmentation identifies cells; Spatial-ID trains a DNN on nucleus profiles and a GCN incorporating spatial neighborhoods to assign spatial cell labels.

title: AI-assisted cerebellar atlases reveal primate-specific cellular organization
summary: Deep-learning segmentation and spatial annotation supported cerebellar atlases of macaques, marmosets and mice, revealing primate-specific cell subtypes and regional gene-expression differences. Transcriptomic gradients corresponded with awake functional-connectivity patterns. This represents the September 27, 2024 journal version; an institutional announcement gives September 26, and the observed associations do not establish causal functions.
ai_technology: Deep-learning cell segmentation; STAGATE; DestVI
organization: BGI-Research; Chinese Academy of Sciences; Erasmus MC; Tencent AI Lab

evidence.tested: New spatial tissue measurements, biological replicates and comparisons with awake fMRI supported the reported anatomical associations within this study.
evidence.unknown: Not assessed: exhaustive supplements, earlier-preprint chronology and independent confirmation. Functional mechanisms are not established by spatial correlations.
evidence.ai_role: Deep-learning models segment cells; STAGATE clusters spatial domains and DestVI assigns cell-type probabilities.

title: AI-assisted macaque claustrum atlas links cell types with projection zones
summary: Learned segmentation and Spatial-ID annotation helped connect macaque claustral cell-type distributions with four projection zones identified through tracer experiments. Different glutamatergic compositions preferentially connected to different brain regions. This is the April 3, 2025 journal version, preceded by a related 2024 conference abstract; comparisons reuse published macaque-cortex data, and the findings do not establish a causal account of consciousness.
ai_technology: Mask R-CNN; Spatial-ID; nnUNet
organization: Chinese Academy of Sciences; Stem Cell and Brain Research Institute, Inserm; BGI-Research; Tencent AI for Life Sciences Lab

evidence.tested: Spatial transcriptomics and retrograde tracing directly supported the cell-type/projection-zone relationship within the discovery study.
evidence.unknown: Not assessed: independent replication, complete supplements and exact first posting day of the earlier conference abstract.
evidence.ai_role: Mask R-CNN segments cells; Spatial-ID trains DNN and GCN models for spatial labels; expert-corrected nnUNet segments claustral boundaries.

title: Spatial-DC maps a candidate fibroblast–cancer signaling interaction in pancreatic tumors
summary: Spatial-DC reconstructed cell-type-resolved spatial proteomes and suggested COL8A1–ITGA2 communication between cancer-associated fibroblasts and pancreatic cancer cells. Multiplexed immunohistochemistry supported the spatial predictions; human protein co-expression was associated with survival. The pairing was already known: the result concerns its inferred spatial deployment, not a new receptor pair or established causal mechanism. This record uses the May 27, 2026 journal version; the result already appeared in the December 20, 2024 preprint.
ai_technology: Spatial-DC; graph-enhanced transfer learning
organization: Southern University of Science and Technology; Tencent AI for Life Sciences Laboratory

evidence.tested: Retrospective spatial proteomic reconstruction and human survival association. Same-study multiplexed immunohistochemistry supports spatial distributions and co-expression, not causal COL8A1–ITGA2 communication.
evidence.unknown: No causal signaling perturbation, therapeutic benefit or independent replication is established in the reviewed material. Current review read indexed publisher introduction and NLM abstract/metadata; full journal methods were inaccessible. Earlier primary preprint XML was read in the project audit on November 16, 2026; revised journal quantitative details were not assessed.
evidence.ai_role: Graph-enhanced transfer learning deconvolved mixed spots and reconstructed cell-type-resolved protein profiles used to infer spatial interactions.

title: AI-assisted hippocampal atlas maps Alzheimer-associated cellular changes around amyloid plaques
summary: In a six-donor postmortem hippocampal study, neural cell segmentation and Spatial-ID annotation helped map Alzheimer-associated cell distributions and gene-expression changes. Immunofluorescence supported the inferred accumulation patterns of microglia and astrocytes around amyloid-beta plaques. These are observational associations, not causal effects or clinical benefit. This record describes the December 7, 2023 preprint; the later Neuron paper was published online March 31, 2025 with an expanded cohort, whose counts and final methods are not pooled here.
ai_technology: StereoCell/ESPANet cell segmentation; Spatial-ID deep neural network and graph convolutional network
organization: Zhejiang University; BGI Research; Tencent AI Lab; University of Chinese Academy of Sciences

evidence.tested: Spatial transcriptomics and single-nucleus sequencing in three AD and three control donor brains; immunofluorescence checked the plaque-associated glial distribution pattern within the same study.
evidence.unknown: Postmortem observational results do not establish disease causation. No independent replication was assessed. Preprint methods retain an unfinished training-epoch placeholder. The reviewed claims and AI architectures refer to the primary preprint, not authenticated final journal methods; candidate blood biomarkers and diagnostic efficacy are outside this record's represented claim.
evidence.ai_role: Trained neural segmentation delineated cells; Spatial-ID used a DNN and GCN to assign spatial cell types, enabling plaque-associated cell-distribution analysis.

title: GPT-6 Astra assists a gauge-invariant lattice chiral-fermion measure construction
summary: Nathaniel Craig proposes a smooth, exponentially local, gauge-invariant fermion measure on admissible four-dimensional lattices, with restrictions covering the Standard Model gauge groups. GPT-6 Astra helped develop the refinement construction and led the detailed proof. The supplementary report states that Lean kernel replay accepted the encoded measure-existence result and supporting inputs under their recorded assumptions. This is a candidate finite-lattice definition; reflection positivity, practical simulation and an interacting continuum theory remain outside the established claim. The October 6, 2026 preprint preceded the November 15 institutional announcement.
ai_technology: GPT-6 Astra; Lean 4 formalization
organization: University of California, Santa Barbara; OpenAI

evidence.tested: Source-reported Lean kernel replay checked the concrete companion measure-existence theorem, its analytic/geometric inputs and Standard Model restrictions under encoded definitions and assumptions. Same-study mathematical and two-dimensional computational checks are also reported.
evidence.unknown: Review checked the preprint verification/conclusion sections and formal-verification supplement, not an independently executed Lean build. Formal-to-source correspondence was reviewed by AI agents. A separate frozen-reference comparator failed on generated proof names; the report distinguishes this from successful kernel replay. Kernel correctness is relative to the encoded claim and axioms; it does not establish reflection positivity, a physical continuum limit, independent scientific confirmation or practical usefulness.
evidence.ai_role: Craig supplied the refinement strategy; Astra developed key construction steps, led proof development and carried out proposed verification work.

title: Robotic learning identifies nine polyoxometalate-based frameworks
summary: A robot and an XGBoost classifier guided crystallization experiments that produced nine reported polyoxometalate-scaffolding metal-organic frameworks. Researchers defined the chemistry and performed structural and electrochemical characterization. The measured electron-transfer behavior does not establish practical energy-storage deployment.

organization: University of Glasgow

evidence.tested: Nine frameworks were synthesized with reported repeatability.
evidence.unknown: Independent replication, exhaustive structural prior art and device performance were not assessed.
evidence.ai_role: XGBoost with uncertainty-feedback retraining supported the stated study; experimental and interpretive work remained with researchers.

This is an experimental processing result, rather than discovery of a new chemical composition or demonstrated deployed-device efficiency. The result was public in the July 2024 preprint before the journal version.

summary: Gaussian-process models and chemist decisions guided synthesis and testing of organic photocatalysts for a specified cross-coupling reaction. title: Machine-guided microscopy characterizes an atypical ataxia presentation
summary: Unsupervised image analysis detected cellular patterns not apparent by inspection in an investigation of one family with an atypical ataxia presentation. Additional cell experiments found altered ataxin-7 behavior and mitochondrial bioenergetic deficits. The proposed combined role of ATXN7 and TOP1MT variants remains a hypothesis: unaffected parents carried individual variants, and fly models did not reproduce the patient phenotype.

evidence.tested: The authors report experimental validation of the x=0.01 and 0.02 Sn compositions against predefined dielectric-stability targets and room-temperature permittivity above 3300.
evidence.unknown: The parent family and substitution were known; the stated criteria do not establish full device certification or deployment. Direct publisher page was inaccessible, so evidence is limited to PubMed metadata and abstract in this check.
evidence.ai_role: Multimodal literature mining curated prior measurements and a deep neural-network ensemble screened candidate dielectric compositions and guided refinement.

title: Multi-omics models guide experimental validation of flowering-time genes
summary: Researchers trained models on genomic, transcriptomic and methylomic data for Arabidopsis traits and used feature interpretation to select flowering-time gene candidates. The preprint reports nine experimentally validated genes inferred to contribute to flowering time, tested using mutant phenotypes. Random-forest and ridge-regression models were used, so do not assign every gene to the random forest alone. Count one study, not nine discoveries. This draft follows the primary 2023 preprint version; the journal paper appeared in 2024.
ai_technology: Random-forest models; ridge regression; multi-omics integration
organization: DOE Great Lakes Bioenergy Research Center, Michigan State University; Chinese Academy of Agricultural Sciences

source_review.scope: Primary bioRxiv v1 full text, posted-date line, abstract, methods and author affiliations.

evidence.tested: The preprint reports experimental validation of nine flowering-time gene candidates using single- and/or double-mutant phenotypes.
evidence.unknown: Individual candidate-selection routes are not all attributed to one model; the result is from a preprint version and does not establish independent replication.
evidence.ai_role: Random-forest and ridge-regression models used multi-omics data to predict plant traits and identify features associated with flowering-time predictions.

title: Deep learning helps experimentally map a ribozyme neutral network
summary: After earlier experimental evolutionary rounds, the authors trained a deep classifier to guide the final in-silico generation and experimentally tested candidates. They measured all 2^16 intermediates between two active RNA ligase ribozymes separated by 16 mutations and report an extensive network of neutral paths. The result applies to this ribozyme and assay, not all RNA evolution. The paper also notes possible model overfitting and the restricted classifier’s accuracy.
ai_technology: Deep-learning classifier; evolutionary algorithm
organization: Okinawa Institute of Science and Technology Graduate University

source_review.scope: Primary Nature Communications indexed full text, abstract, main text, publication metadata and author affiliation.

evidence.tested: The study reports experimental activity measurements for all 2^16 connecting sequence variants and a screen of more than 120,000 ribozyme sequences.
evidence.unknown: The neutral network is bounded to one RNA ligase ribozyme and assay; generality across other landscapes is not established, and the paper notes potential classifier overfitting.
evidence.ai_role: A deep-learning classifier trained on prior experimental generations guided in-silico selection, mutation and recombination in the final generation.

title: Machine learning guides fatty acyl-ACP reductase engineering
summary: A machine-learning-guided iterative design–test–learn workflow engineered fatty acyl-ACP reductase variants for microbial fatty alcohol production. Across ten rounds, the study reports over twice the production of the starting natural sequences under tested conditions; the top sequence also had enhanced catalytic rate on palmitoyl-ACP. These are laboratory results, not industrial-scale production. The journal article date is used here; the earlier preprint’s exact posting and result-version differences were not checked.
ai_technology: Machine-learning-guided protein engineering; Gaussian-process optimization
organization: University of Wisconsin-Madison

source_review.scope: Primary Nature Communications indexed full text, abstract, article date, author affiliations; preprint chronology not fully checked.

evidence.tested: The paper reports ten design–test–learn rounds, in-vivo microbial fatty-alcohol production and catalytic-rate characterization on palmitoyl-ACP.
evidence.unknown: Results are under the study’s microbial test conditions and do not establish industrial production; exact preprint-version results remain unchecked.
evidence.ai_role: Machine-learning models iteratively selected reductase sequences for experimental testing and subsequent model updates.

title: Machine learning guides engineering of fluorescent calcium indicators
summary: An ensemble of three regression models trained on experimentally derived GCaMP mutation libraries screened 1,423 uncharacterized variants. The study reports eGCaMP and eGCaMP+ with faster kinetics and larger fluorescence responses than previously published fast variants, and eGCaMP2+ with greater dynamic range than the tested sixth-, seventh- and eighth-generation indicators. The preprint reports cell and neuron assays. These are laboratory sensor results, not human or clinical validation. This is one study; the journal article is a later version.
ai_technology: Ensemble of three regression models
organization: University of Washington
