Variants with four to five substitutions showed in-vitro and cellular binding comparable to conventionally recombined variants with 13–15 substitutions; the paper also reports blockade assays and therapeutic activity in a mouse tumor model. These are preclinical antibody-engineering results, not evidence of human efficacy. The preprint reports patent applications related to the subject matter.
ai_technology: Deep-learning model trained on deep-mutational-scanning sequence–binding data
organization: Université Paris-Saclay; CEA; INRAE; CNRS; Inserm; Institut Agro Rennes

source_review.scope: Primary bioRxiv v1 indexed full-text/abstract, author-affiliation metadata and official API metadata; direct page open returned 403.

evidence.tested: The preprint reports in-vitro and cellular binding properties of selected variants, PD-1/PD-L1 competition/blockade assays, epitope mapping and mouse tumor-model assessment. The 4–5 substitution variants are compared with highly mutated variants requiring 13–15 substitutions.
evidence.unknown: Mouse-model activity is preclinical and does not establish human therapeutic efficacy. The preprint reports patent applications relevant to the work; no freedom-to-operate or patent-priority conclusion is made.
evidence.ai_role: A deep-learning model trained on DMS-derived sequence-binding data selected minimal mutation combinations for experimental antibody characterization.

title: Machine-learning pipeline identifies antimicrobial hexapeptides
summary: A sequential machine-learning pipeline screened virtual libraries of 6–9-residue peptides and identified three leading antimicrobial hexapeptides. The paper reports activity against multidrug-resistant clinical isolates and therapeutic effects in a mouse bacterial-pneumonia model. These are laboratory and animal results, not clinical efficacy.
ai_technology: Sequential machine-learning pipeline for peptide selection, classification, ranking and activity regression
organization: Zhejiang University

source_review.scope: Primary Nature indexed article text and PubMed abstract/metadata/affiliation record for the ML hexapeptide screening study, its January 2023 publication date and reported mouse pneumonia assays.

evidence.tested: The authors report a sequential machine-learning pipeline over virtual 6–9 amino-acid sequence space; the leading three identified hexapeptides were tested against clinical multidrug-resistant isolates and in a mouse bacterial-pneumonia model.
evidence.unknown: The mouse model and reported comparison with penicillin do not establish human efficacy. The PubMed primary metadata gives journal online date 2023-01-12; no earlier pre-2020 version is identified in the reviewed primary material.
evidence.ai_role: Sequential learned modules selected, classified, ranked and regressed peptide candidates from the virtual sequence library; the reported three lead hexapeptides are outputs of that workflow.

title: ECNet-guided selection of higher-order TEM-1 variants
summary: ECNet integrated evolutionary context with learned sequence representations to prioritize previously untested higher-order TEM-1 variants. The authors constructed and measured 37 selected variants under ampicillin selection, using relative resistance as an enzyme-fitness proxy. The assays do not imply clinical treatment outcomes, and the reported group of 37 should not be read as showing that every variant improved.
ai_technology: ECNet evolutionary-context-integrated deep-learning framework
organization: University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign

source_review.scope: Primary Nature indexed article and author-hosted full text; official bioRxiv API checked and identified the previously associated preprint DOI as a different paper.

evidence.tested: Thirty-seven previously untested higher-order TEM-1 variants selected with ECNet were constructed and experimentally measured under ampicillin selection against wild-type and study controls. The study uses relative resistance as an enzyme-fitness proxy.
evidence.unknown: The bounded entry does not imply that all 37 variants improved equally, does not establish clinical outcomes, and makes no claim of independent sequence novelty beyond the authors’ screened literature.
evidence.ai_role: ECNet integrated evolutionary context and a learned representation to prioritize higher-order TEM-1 variants for experimental construction and ampicillin-selection measurements.

title: CoSaNN designs and tests an induced-fit carbohydrate kinase
summary: CoSaNN combined neural structure prediction, learned sequence optimization and solubility ranking to design variants of an induced-fit ROK carbohydrate kinase. The authors measured expression, thermal stability and activity in vitro. The paper reports measurable expression for 189 of 348 designs in one table, while the strategy-level counts do not sum to that total; no success-rate claim is made here.
ai_technology: CoSaNN: AlphaFold2-based conformation modeling, ProteinMPNN sequence design and SolvIT graph neural network ranking
organization: Enzymit Ltd.

source_review.scope: Primary PMC full text and PNAS DOI record for CoSaNN-guided glucokinase design, Enzymit affiliations, experimental activity results and the discrepancy in reported design totals.

evidence.tested: The authors applied CoSaNN to redesign the Arthrobacter polyphosphate glucokinase ROK kinase and performed expression, thermal-stability and enzyme-activity assays on designed variants. The primary Results table reports 189 designs with detectable soluble expression among 348 listed designs; its strategy counts (119+95+94 plus 40 in another strategy; rows in the prose/table are internally inconsistent) do not reconcile cleanly, so the record does not use a single total as a success-rate denominator.
evidence.unknown: The study tests a company-designed enzyme set in vitro; it does not establish industrial deployment. The primary paper’s count inconsistency remains explicitly disclosed.
evidence.ai_role: CoSaNN uses deep-learning structure prediction (AlphaFold2), sequence optimization with ProteinMPNN and a learned solubility classifier (SolvIT) to rank enzyme designs for experimental characterization.

title: Active learning selected oxidative methane coupling catalysts
summary: The authors combined automatic feature engineering with active learning and high-throughput experiments for oxidative coupling of methane. Of 36 selected catalysts, 30 reached combined ethane and ethylene yields of at least 15% in the reported tests. This is a small-data, reaction-specific catalyst screening outcome; the paper also tests feature engineering on other catalysis datasets. A ChemRxiv version predates the journal publication, and this record does not claim journal-version priority.
ai_technology: Automatic feature engineering with active learning
organization: Japan Advanced Institute of Science and Technology; Hokkaido University

source_review.scope: Full published article text in German National Library repository and publisher-indexed primary metadata/abstract; earlier ChemRxiv version noted but not compared.

evidence.tested: The article reports 36 selected oxidative coupling of methane catalysts experimentally assessed; 30 achieved combined ethane and ethylene yields of at least 15% under the reported test conditions.
evidence.unknown: The paper also appeared as an earlier ChemRxiv version; this check did not establish whether every quantitative detail appeared in that version. The result is limited to the reported catalyst set and reaction conditions.
evidence.ai_role: Automatic feature engineering extracted catalyst descriptors, and active learning selected catalysts for high-throughput experimental testing.

title: Adaptive learning selected an additive for a magnesium-air battery
summary: An iterative machine-learning adaptive-design workflow selected 2,3-dihydroxynaphthalene for a lab-made (Mg-0.2Ca)-air battery. The authors report a cell voltage of 1.82 V and 3.37 kWh kg⁻¹ specific energy calculated from total Mg-anode mass loss, not whole-cell or pack mass. The publisher abstract reports 83% anodic utilization, while the full article reports 85% at a stated 0.5 mA cm⁻² condition; this discrepancy is not resolved here and the utilization figure is omitted. The authors also state that the surrogate model overestimated performance predictions for this additive.
ai_technology: Iterative adaptive design with SOAP descriptors and a KPCovR surrogate model
organization: Institute of Surface Science, Helmholtz-Zentrum Hereon; Hebei University of Technology; Kiel University

source_review.scope: Primary Elsevier indexed abstract and full publisher PDF text hosted by ResearchGate; primary Hereon repository metadata cross-check. Specific energy basis and internal utilization-efficiency discrepancy reviewed.

evidence.tested: The authors report a lab-made (Mg-0.2Ca)-air battery with the model-selected 2,3-dihydroxynaphthalene additive at 1.82 V. Reported specific energy is 3.37 kWh kg−1 calculated from total Mg-anode mass loss. No whole-cell or pack-mass specific energy is claimed.
evidence.unknown: Publisher abstract reports 83% anodic utilization; full article text gives 85% at a stated 0.5 mA cm−2 condition. The difference is unresolved, so no utilization percentage is asserted. The authors report that the surrogate model overestimated predictions for this additive.
evidence.ai_role: A SOAP-descriptor/KPCovR model in iterative adaptive experimental design contributed to selecting 2,3-dihydroxynaphthalene for electrochemical validation.

title: Machine learning guides a proposed UCd3 intermetallic phase assignment
summary: A support-vector classifier using composition-derived elemental features predicted a Cu₃Au-type structure for UCd₃ and guided synthesis. Powder X-ray diffraction from the second of two samples showed peaks the authors fit to a UCd₃ phase with a = 4.648(2) Å; the sample also contained uranium, uranium oxide and cadmium, while the first sample differed. This is the authors’ proposed phase assignment from a multiphase powder, not phase-pure material or independent structural confirmation.
ai_technology: Support-vector machine discriminant analysis; Gaussian-process regression for feature completion
organization: The Cooper Union for the Advancement of Science and Art; Manhattan College

source_review.scope: Primary ChemRxiv v1 full text, affiliation/date metadata, methods and diffraction discussion, plus primary UCd11 literature review for prior-compound context.

evidence.tested: The authors report synthesis and powder X-ray diffraction; the proposed phase was present in the second of two samples.
evidence.unknown: Only one synthesis batch/sample (the second of two samples) showed the additional peaks assigned by the authors to UCd₃; the powder was multiphase. The checked 2022 primary review says UCd₁₁ was the only previously reported U-Cd compound, but this is not an independent confirmation of the proposed UCd₃ structure.
evidence.ai_role: SVM classification of composition-derived descriptors predicted a Cu₃Au-type structure and motivated experimental synthesis/testing.

title: Machine learning guided XylM variant improved biosensor-indicated productivity
summary: Two machine-learning-assisted directed-evolution cycles produced XylM-D140E-V144K-F243L-N244S, reported to have 15-fold higher 3-methylsalicylic acid productivity than wild-type XylM. Productivity was estimated using XylS-dependent fluorescence in a sensor strain; this is a biosensor-based productivity readout, not a purified-enzyme kinetic constant.
ai_technology: Machine-learning-assisted directed evolution using biosensor-derived activity data
organization: The University of Tokyo; National Institute of Advanced Industrial Science and Technology; AIST-Waseda University Computational Bio Big-Data Open Innovation Laboratory

source_review.scope: Primary ACS publisher indexed abstract and affiliation/article-history metadata, cross-checked against primary PubMed abstract and metadata.

evidence.tested: The publisher reports XylM-D140E-V144K-F243L-N244S with 15-fold greater 3-methylsalicylic-acid productivity than wild type after two ML-assisted directed-evolution cycles, using XylS-dependent fluorescence from a sensor strain as the measured indicator.
evidence.unknown: The signal is an indirect biosensor-based productivity proxy; the reported value is not a purified-enzyme kinetic constant.
evidence.ai_role: Machine learning used sensor-derived data to guide two rounds of directed evolution and prioritize XylM variants.

title: Machine learning guided Cu catalyst additive discovery for CO₂ reduction
summary: Across three iterative cycles of experimental testing, machine-learning analysis, prediction and redesign, the authors obtained Cu catalysts selective for CO, formic acid and C₂+ products in electrochemical CO₂ reduction. This summary follows the primary abstract and does not assign disputed sample identifiers or report cell-specific percentages.
ai_technology: Machine-learning-guided iterative additive screening and redesign
organization: Xiamen University; Northwestern Polytechnical University

source_review.scope: Primary ACS abstract, author-affiliation and article-history metadata; full text and supporting information not reviewed.

evidence.tested: The primary abstract reports three iterative cycles of experimental testing and model-guided redesign, producing Cu catalysts selective for CO, formic acid and C₂+ products. No disputed sample-level metrics are included.
evidence.unknown: Full text and supporting information were not reviewed. The exact sample-to-performance mapping and the third-party rendering’s sample-number discrepancy remain unverified.
evidence.ai_role: Machine-learning analysis of experimental additive/catalyst data guided predictions and redesign over three iterative experimental cycles.

title: MutCompute guides thermostable Bst DNA polymerase variants
summary: MutCompute predicted substitutions in Bst DNA polymerase; the authors constructed and tested variants in loop-mediated isothermal amplification assays. The Mut235 triple variant showed the highest activity among four tested triple-mutant variants and remained active at 73 °C; its reported melting temperature was 78.1 °C. The evidence is in vitro and does not establish clinical diagnostic performance. The journal article cites a bioRxiv v1 posted 2021-04-15, but that version’s full text was inaccessible in this review; this entry uses the verified journal result and does not claim when the Mut235 result first appeared.
ai_technology: MutCompute machine-learning amino-acid environment scoring
organization: The University of Texas at Austin

source_review.scope: Primary PMC full journal text for MutCompute, LAMP assays, University of Texas affiliation and measured variants; primary bioRxiv v1 endpoint was attempted but blocked, so earlier-version result details remain bounded to what the journal and cited metadata support.

evidence.tested: The authors assayed ML-predicted Bst polymerase substitutions in LAMP/LAMP-OSD reactions. Mut235 showed the highest activity among four triple-mutant variants tested, supported amplification at 73 °C, and had a measured melting temperature of 78.1 °C versus 75.5 °C for parental Bst-LF in the reported thermal-shift assay.
evidence.unknown: The article cites an earlier bioRxiv preprint dated 2021-04-15, but this check did not retrieve its full v1 text; no claim is made that every final-version assay/result was present in v1. Results are in-vitro amplification assays, not clinical diagnostic validation.
evidence.ai_role: MutCompute machine learning predicted amino-acid substitutions in Bst DNA polymerase; the authors constructed and assayed variants including Mut235.

title: AlphaZero finds improved finite extremal-graph bounds
summary: A neural network-guided AlphaZero search with a curriculum generated triangle- and 4-cycle-free graphs that improve known lower bounds for the extremal function ex(n,{C3,C4}) over finite sizes; the proceedings report AlphaZero improvements for n=64–136 and release the graph constructions. The paper also finds improvements using a separate tabu-search method, which often matches or outperforms AlphaZero. This does not solve the asymptotic Erdős conjecture. The result was present in the arXiv v1 posted 2023-11-06; the 2024 IJCAI proceedings paper is a later version.
ai_technology: AlphaZero reinforcement learning with neural Pairformer representation and curriculum
organization: Google DeepMind; Imperial College London; Yonsei University; University of Bonn; Worcester Polytechnic Institute

source_review.scope: Primary arXiv v1 full text and metadata plus IJCAI 2024 proceedings page/PDF for AlphaZero versus tabu-search graph construction results, theorem limits and author affiliations.

evidence.tested: The paper reports released graphs with improved lower bounds for ex(n,{C3,C4}) for node counts 64–134. Incremental AlphaZero (neural network-guided Monte Carlo tree search) is explicitly reported to improve bounds for sizes 64–136 in the proceedings version; incremental tabu search also improves bounds and the authors report it can match or exceed AlphaZero. This is a finite-graph construction result, not a proof of the asymptotic Erdős conjecture.
evidence.unknown: The result consists of explicit finite constructions/lower bounds; the asymptotic conjecture remains open. The work does not establish that learned search outperforms strong local search.
evidence.ai_role: AlphaZero with a neural Pairformer representation and a curriculum generated extremal graphs improving the established lower bounds for n=64–136; tabu search is a separate, non-neural method and its results are not attributed to AI.

title: Machine learning and directed evolution improved an L-Dopa-producing monooxygenase
summary: Zero-shot protein models prioritized HpaBC substitutions, which were experimentally assayed with a L-Dopa-responsive GFP biosensor. EVOLVEpro then combined experimentally validated substitutions, including directed-evolution-derived variants, and selected higher-order designs. The best reported combined variants produced up to 57–58 times the wild-type fluorescence signal under the stated assay conditions. This is a biosensor proxy for L-Dopa production, not a purified-enzyme kinetic measurement; the work also builds on prior directed-evolution mutations and does not establish clinical benefit.
ai_technology: MutCompute, ProteinMPNN, ESM protein language models and EVOLVEpro combinatorial design
organization: The University of Texas at Austin

source_review.scope: Primary bioRxiv v1 API metadata and Crossref posted-date metadata checked; primary v1 full-text indexed extract reviewed for methods, biosensor-normalized outcomes, model role and affiliation. Direct full-text page open was blocked.

evidence.tested: 329 model-predicted variants were assayed; 19 showed at least 1.25-fold biosensor signal. EVOLVEpro-selected combined variants yielded up to 57–58-fold normalized fluorescence relative to wild type under the reported assay conditions.
evidence.unknown: Fluorescence from a DopA/GFP biosensor is an indirect L-Dopa-production proxy, not a purified-enzyme catalytic constant. The work includes directed-evolution-derived mutations; G295T had prior directed-evolution support. No human therapeutic efficacy is established.
evidence.ai_role: MutCompute, ProteinMPNN and ESM prioritized single substitutions for experimental testing; EVOLVEpro combined tested mutations and iteratively selected higher-order variants, including designs incorporating directed-evolution results.

title: Progressive learning screened single-atom oxide catalysts for acidic oxygen evolution
summary: A progressive-learning workflow combining density-functional theory and machine learning screened 261 single-atom-doped metal oxides and identified nine candidates with predicted OER overpotential below 0.5 V. The publisher abstract reports experimental evaluation confirming predicted activity and durability for Mn single atoms on RuO₂ under acidic conditions. Candidate-wide values are theoretical predictions; only the specified material’s validation is summarized as experimental.
ai_technology: Progressive learning with DFT-derived adsorption-energy features and machine learning
organization: University of Puerto Rico, Río Piedras; Zhejiang University; Shandong University of Technology; Chung-Ang University

source_review.scope: Primary publisher abstract, first-publication date, and author-affiliation metadata; full article and supporting information not reviewed.

evidence.tested: The abstract reports experimental evaluation confirming predicted activity and durability for MnSA-RuO₂ under acidic conditions. The nine candidates and their <0.5 V overpotentials are theoretical screening outcomes, not nine experimental validations.
evidence.unknown: The abstract does not provide detailed experimental conditions or an independent comparison; those are not inferred.
evidence.ai_role: Progressive learning combined DFT with machine learning, using adsorption-energy predictions as auxiliary features to screen single-atom-doped oxide catalysts.

title: Machine learning enriched MthUPO variants for beta-damascone hydroxylation
summary: Researchers combined experimental activity measurements with machine learning to enrich a second MthUPO peroxygenase library for substrate-specific activity. Across 506 distinct variants screened and sequenced, 97 of 108 variants in the ML-enriched library outperformed wild type in the screening assay, compared with 14% in the initial htFuncLib library. The authors report an 11.8-fold turnover number for the best variant producing 4-hydroxy-beta-damascone, with greater than 99% regioisomeric excess. Separate 5–12-fold enrichment and recovery figures in the paper are simulation benchmarks and are not treated as experimental outcomes.
ai_technology: Machine-learning enrichment of experimental enzyme-activity data following htFuncLib design
organization: Martin Luther University Halle-Wittenberg

source_review.scope: Official bioRxiv API v1 metadata/abstract and primary indexed v1 full-text excerpts; simulation and experimental results kept separate.

evidence.tested: The preprint reports screening and sequencing 506 distinct MthUPO variants. In the ML-enriched library, 97 of 108 variants outperformed wild type in the screening assay, compared with 14% in the initial htFuncLib library. The best reported variant had an 11.8-fold turnover number for 4-hydroxy-beta-damascone with greater than 99% regioisomeric excess.
evidence.unknown: The preprint is not peer reviewed. The paper separately reports simulation-only MLEE/htFuncLib comparisons, which are excluded from the experimental result summary. Assay outcomes do not establish process-scale productivity or commercial suitability.
evidence.ai_role: Machine learning used experimental enzyme-activity measurements to enrich a library of MthUPO variants for testing, following an earlier htFuncLib design stage.

title: Machine learning screened metal oxides for acetylene semihydrogenation
summary: A neural-network model was used to predict metal-oxide catalyst performance for acetylene semi-hydrogenation. The authors report experimental validation of predictions for CuO, ZnO and V2O5, and report 99.6% conversion with 90% ethylene selectivity for CuO under the abstract-described conditions. The entry is limited to the publisher abstract; detailed model validation, candidate selection and full assay context were not reviewed.
ai_technology: Neural-network prediction of metal-oxide catalyst performance
organization: Zhejiang University of Technology

source_review.scope: Primary publisher abstract for identity, displayed date, model and reported experiment; official Zhejiang University of Technology faculty profile/publication list for named contributor affiliation. Full paper methods and supplement not reviewed.

evidence.tested: The publisher abstract says CuO, ZnO and V2O5 predictions were experimentally validated; it reports 99.6% conversion and 90% ethylene selectivity for CuO at 50–100°C.
evidence.unknown: Detailed selection chronology, model split/performance, full test conditions and results for ZnO and V2O5 were not established from the reviewed abstract. The date is the publisher-displayed date, not a claim of first public appearance.
evidence.ai_role: A neural-network model predicted catalyst performance and informed the metal-oxide candidates reported as experimentally validated.

title: Machine learning guided multi-metric optimization of photocatalytic CO2 reduction
summary: Bayesian optimization guided experiments on a five-component self-assembled photocatalytic micelle system for CO₂-to-CO reduction. The authors report that optimized conditions increased measured CO yield from 1.48 ± 0.24 to 5.72 ± 0.12 μmol h⁻¹, with improved turnover and quantum-yield metrics while maintaining CO selectivity. The article’s narrative fold-change (4.2×) is inconsistent with the displayed means (about 3.9×), so this record gives the means and omits the fold claim. The findings apply to the tested aqueous micelle system and conditions.
ai_technology: Bayesian optimization for experimental selection; random-forest models and SHAP for later analysis
organization: University of Cambridge; Politecnico di Torino; Uppsala University

source_review.scope: Primary ACS publisher metadata and University of Cambridge repository copy of the article full text checked for article identity, affiliations, date, optimization method, results and source discrepancy.

evidence.tested: The article reports CO yield means of 5.72±0.12 and 1.48±0.24 μmol h−1 for optimized vs initial conditions, along with turnover and quantum-yield metrics and maintained selectivity. The narrative states a 4.2-fold yield improvement, inconsistent with these displayed means; the record does not repeat the fold value.
evidence.unknown: This demonstrates a study-specific photocatalytic system optimization, not industrially scaled carbon conversion or independent replication. The source’s stated yield fold change conflicts with its displayed means.
evidence.ai_role: Bayesian optimization guided the experimental parameter search and selected test conditions in a five-component micelle system; random-forest models and SHAP then analyzed parameter effects.

title: Active learning identified a KNN ceramic composition with high piezoelectric response
summary: An active-learning loop combined machine-learning prediction, surrogate optimization and experimental testing to explore lead-free potassium-sodium niobate (KNN) ceramics. After three experiment and optimization iterations, the authors report identifying a composition with a measured piezoelectric coefficient d33 of approximately 353 pC/N from thousands of possible compositions. This is a laboratory material-property measurement, not validation of a finished sensor or device.
ai_technology: Support vector regression with a radial basis function kernel in an active-learning experimental-design loop
organization: Nanjing University of Aeronautics and Astronautics

source_review.scope: Primary publisher indexed full text/abstract and primary institutional repository metadata/abstract for article date, author affiliation, model workflow and experimental result.

evidence.tested: After three active-learning-guided experiment iterations, the authors report a synthesized KNN composition with measured d33 of approximately 353 pC/N.
evidence.unknown: The reported coefficient is a laboratory material-property measurement, not device-level qualification or commercial performance.
evidence.ai_role: An SVR model predicted KNN piezoelectric response and guided composition selection across three experiment-optimization iterations.

title: Machine-learning screening identified experimentally active pore-forming peptides
summary: Machine-learning models and membrane-related filters were used to prioritize natural peptide sequences for testing. The study reports seven experimentally active peptides; three showed broad-spectrum activity and pore-forming evidence in the reported membrane assays. Peptide 615 had already been disclosed in a Peking University patent published in March 2025, before the related preprint and journal article. This entry represents one study campaign and makes no first-disclosure or sequence-novelty claim. Assay results do not establish clinical safety or efficacy.
ai_technology: ProtBERT-BFD sequence embeddings with a support-vector classifier and membrane-interaction, secondary-structure and contact-map predictions
organization: Peking University; Yantai University; Institute of Physics, Chinese Academy of Sciences; University of Chinese Academy of Sciences; École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne; University of Geneva; Songshan Lake Materials Laboratory

source_review.scope: Primary PMC full text, metadata and affiliation block; published patent text for earlier public disclosure; primary preprint record identified in the frozen source review.

evidence.tested: The paper reports seven experimentally active selected peptides and pore-forming measurements for three broad-spectrum candidates.
evidence.unknown: One peptide sequence, 615, was disclosed in an earlier university patent. The article does not establish clinical safety or efficacy, and no universal mechanism is claimed.
evidence.ai_role: Machine-learning sequence and membrane-related models prioritized peptide candidates for experimental testing.

title: BroadAMP-GPT generated and experimentally tested broad-spectrum AMP_S13
summary: BroadAMP-GPT combined transformer-based peptide generation, computational screening and experimental testing. The paper reports that 57% of AI-generated candidates showed potent activity against ESKAPE pathogens. AMP_S13 showed broad-spectrum antimicrobial activity, stability under tested conditions, low cytotoxicity and hemolysis, and efficacy in Galleria mellonella and a murine MRSA wound model. These preclinical findings do not establish human safety or efficacy; the 57% abstract metric is kept distinct from the separately reported assays of 14 synthesized candidates.
ai_technology: Transformer-based peptide generation with deep-learning-guided screening
organization: Nanjing Agricultural University; Hainan University; China Pharmaceutical University

source_review.scope: Primary publisher full article/PDF, publisher publication history and NCBI/PubMed metadata/abstract; first-public preprint and sequence priority are not claimed.

evidence.tested: The paper reports a 57% potent-activity rate among AI-generated candidates and describes AMP_S13 broad-spectrum activity, stability, low cytotoxicity/hemolysis, Galleria mellonella infection testing and a murine MRSA wound-infection model. A separate cohort statement reports six of 14 synthesized candidates inhibiting both E. coli and S. aureus at MIC ≤16 μg/mL; these are distinct denominators/outcomes.
evidence.unknown: The results are laboratory and animal preclinical findings, not human efficacy or safety. The entry makes no claim that the peptide sequence was first disclosed here or is globally novel.
evidence.ai_role: BroadAMP-GPT generated peptide candidates with a transformer and applied deep-learning-guided screening before experimental validation; AMP_S13 is the named lead candidate in the reported assays.

title: OxiGraphX predicted vacancy formation energies in high-entropy perovskites
summary: OxiGraphX, a graph neural network, predicted oxygen-vacancy formation energies for three high-entropy perovskite oxides that the authors synthesized. Experimental measurements reported 29% oxygen vacancies in BSL4B, 27% in SL4B and no detected vacancies in L4B, broadly tracking the predicted and DFT-calculated formation energies. The article contains inconsistent text assigning the relative oxygen-evolution overpotentials; this entry does not make that comparison.
ai_technology: OxiGraphX graph neural network for oxygen-vacancy formation-energy prediction
organization: University of North Carolina at Greensboro; University of North Georgia; Kennesaw State University; University of Texas at Austin; Brookhaven National Laboratory

source_review.scope: Primary publisher indexed full text, PMC full text and NCBI/PubMed metadata/affiliations. Disputed OER overpotential comparison omitted.

evidence.tested: Three high-entropy perovskite oxides were synthesized; oxygen-vacancy measurements reported 29% for BSL4B, 27% for SL4B and undetected for L4B. The article compares these measurements with OxiGraphX predictions and DFT calculations.
evidence.unknown: The source text conflicts on relative oxygen-evolution overpotentials, which are not included here. These tests do not establish device-level or industrial performance.
evidence.ai_role: OxiGraphX predicted oxygen-vacancy formation energies that informed selection of perovskite compositions for synthesis and comparison with measured vacancy content.

title: Knowledge-guided graph learning designed a printable nickel superalloy
summary: A knowledge-informed graph attention model with uncertainty quantification selected the KG-AMS nickel superalloy composition and processing conditions for laser directed-energy deposition. The study reports experimental validation with defect area fractions of 0.037%–0.133% and hardness of 391–417 HV across tested parameter sets; it also reports room-temperature tensile strength of 1307 MPa and elongation of 22.2%. These measurements apply to the tested alloy and processing window, and larger builds remain untested. This entry covers KG-AMS only; the paper’s separate aluminum alloy KG-AMAA had already been reported by the same group in 2025.
ai_technology: Knowledge-informed graph attention network with uncertainty quantification (UQ-KGAT)
organization: Northeastern University

source_review.scope: Primary Nature Communications article, linked supplementary affiliation block, and indexed PMC full text checked for date, alloy/model link and tested properties; record is limited to KG-AMS to avoid duplication of KG-AMAA.

evidence.tested: The paper reports fabricated KG-AMS nickel alloy specimens with defect area fractions of 0.037%–0.133% and hardness of 391–417 HV over the reported processing parameters; it also reports room-temperature tensile strength 1307 MPa and elongation 22.2%.
evidence.unknown: Results are bounded to the specimens and processing conditions in the study; larger builds and independent replication are not established. The separate KG-AMAA aluminum alloy is not counted here because the same group reported it earlier.
evidence.ai_role: UQ-KGAT, a knowledge-informed graph attention network with uncertainty quantification, identified the KG-AMS alloy and its processing region for experimental validation.

title: Neural-network-ranked survey found candidate lenses and spectroscopically followed seven
summary: Two residual neural networks ranked multiband UNIONS galaxy images for strong-lens candidates; researchers visually graded the candidates. The paper lists 1,346 candidates and reports independent Keck/Gemini spectroscopy for seven selected high-quality systems, with background-source redshifts above 2.1. The authors report overlaps with other lens surveys. This entry represents one AI-assisted survey and its selected spectroscopic follow-up, not 1,346 confirmed lenses or seven uniquely first-discovered objects; object-level priority and complete cross-survey overlap remain unresolved.
ai_technology: Two residual neural networks trained on real lens images and applied to multiband UNIONS imaging
organization: University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa; Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory; University of San Francisco; University of California, Berkeley; Université Paris-Saclay; Laboratoire d’Astrophysique de Marseille; National Research Council Herzberg Astronomy and Astrophysics; University of Waterloo; Perimeter Institute; University of British Columbia

source_review.scope: Primary arXiv v1 full paper and history; authors’ primary candidate-catalog deposit and later dataset record for coordinates, overlaps and affiliations.

evidence.tested: The paper reports 1,346 human-reviewed lens candidates and spectroscopy of seven selected high-quality systems with background-source redshifts above 2.1.
evidence.unknown: Candidates overlap other surveys; not every candidate is spectroscopically confirmed, and full object-level priority/cross-survey matching is not claimed.
evidence.ai_role: Residual neural networks ranked imaging candidates for human inspection and selection for spectroscopic follow-up.

title: AI-guided reactor design improves a specific continuous-flow cycloaddition
summary: Reac-Discovery combines learned geometry screening with automated experimental optimization of continuous-flow catalytic reactors. The peer-reviewed article reports a Schoen_G structured reactor with space–time yield of 803 g L−1 h−1 for a specific CO₂–epichlorohydrin cycloaddition, compared with 412 in the study’s initial data set. The comparison is study-specific and restricted to the authors’ reactor conditions; it does not establish industrial scale or net carbon removal. The article was published online on 13 October 2025; an earlier preprint described the platform and reaction, so this record attributes the 803 result to the journal version.
ai_technology: Neural geometry screening and machine-learning-guided experimental optimization
organization: Universitat Jaume I

source_review.scope: Primary Nature Communications article metadata and publisher PDF front matter/result checked; result/date/affiliation source checked.

evidence.tested: The paper reports a measured Schoen_G reactor space-time yield of 803 g L−1 h−1 for CO₂–epichlorohydrin cycloaddition, compared with 412 in the study’s initial data set. The comparison is limited to the article’s experimental conditions.
evidence.unknown: This study-specific result does not establish industrial scalability, net carbon removal or independent replication. The earlier preprint describes the platform and reaction; the 803 result is assigned to the journal article version.
evidence.ai_role: Machine-learning optimization selected process parameters and topological descriptors for the reactor; the article reports the measured cycloaddition result for the optimized reactor.

title: Generative design and screening produced experimentally tested antimicrobial QACs
summary: A topology-aware generative workflow and activity predictor prioritized quaternary ammonium compounds (QACs) for synthesis and testing. Across two workflows the authors report 29 selected compounds characterized and 11 QACs designated as novel, with measured minimum inhibitory concentrations of 1–32 μM against bacterial pathogens. Earlier same-team conference disclosures had already described AI-generated QAC design and synthesis; this record covers the later paper’s bounded tested results and does not claim the first AI-generated QACs or universal chemical novelty. Activity and cytotoxicity remain assay-specific and do not establish clinical use.
ai_technology: Topology-aware QAC generative model with structure/activity prediction and filtering (Q-HERO)
organization: George Mason University; Villanova University; Emory University; Saint Joseph’s University

source_review.scope: Primary ACS indexed full article, publication history, methods/results, named affiliations and indexed supporting-information description; earlier team conference disclosures as identified in the frozen source review.

evidence.tested: The article reports synthesis and antimicrobial testing across two workflows, with 29 selected compounds characterized and 11 reported novel QACs with MIC values of 1–32 μM.
evidence.unknown: Prior same-team AI-QAC design and synthesis were described in 2022 and 2024 institutional conference abstracts. The measured activity is limited to the reported laboratory assays and does not establish clinical efficacy.
evidence.ai_role: A topology-aware generative model proposed QAC structures, and learned activity filtering helped prioritize candidates for synthesis and antimicrobial assays.

title: Machine learning selected nucleoside derivatives for hydrogel testing
summary: A machine-learning model trained on 71 previously reported nucleoside derivatives was applied to an external set, from which the authors selected 24 candidates for hydrogel testing. They report gel formation for 20 of the 24 tested molecules and characterize cation-independent hydrogel behavior for 8-aminoguanosine and 8-hydroxyguanosine. A 2023 Sichuan University patent by the same team had already disclosed the model, 12 selected candidates and 10 gelation positives, including these two derivatives. This entry represents one study/campaign and does not claim that the 2024 article was the first public disclosure or that the compounds were novel.
ai_technology: Machine-learning classifier using molecular descriptors to predict nucleoside derivative hydrogel formation
organization: Sichuan University

source_review.scope: Primary Nature article page and PubMed Central indexed full text for model selection and experimental outcomes; PubMed record for date and affiliations; published patent application text for same-team prior disclosure and overlapping candidates.

evidence.tested: The paper reports that 20 of 24 externally selected nucleoside derivatives formed hydrogels in experimental validation. It also reports cation-independent hydrogel behavior for 8-aminoguanosine and 8-hydroxyguanosine.
evidence.unknown: A 2023 patent application from the same university/team already disclosed the same model, 12 selected derivatives, 10 gelation positives, and included 8-AG and 8-OHG. Do not treat the overlapping paper and patent as independent discoveries or claim first disclosure/compound novelty. Hydrogel behavior does not establish clinical benefit.
evidence.ai_role: The ML model predicted gel-forming ability and selected nucleoside derivatives for external experimental validation.

title: Active learning found unconventional self-assembling pentapeptides
summary: An experiment-driven active-learning workflow selected pentapeptide sequences for testing of beta-sheet self-assembly. Among 268 synthesized and tested peptides, 96 formed beta-sheet assemblies, including sequences such as ILFSM, LMISI, MITIY, MISIW and WKIYI that conventional propensity rules did not predict. The result concerns measured assembly under the study conditions; it does not establish a functional material application or therapeutic effect. The outcome was already reported in the September 2024 preprint and is dated accordingly.
ai_technology: AI-driven active learning with machine-learning models that selected peptide sequences for iterative synthesis and testing
organization: Indian Institute of Technology Madras; Argonne National Laboratory; University of Illinois Chicago

source_review.scope: Primary PMC full article for active-learning workflow and measured assemblies; primary Research Square v1 manuscript for September 2024 version date and named affiliations; primary AAAS article for the peer-reviewed version and reported results.

evidence.tested: The v1 reports synthesis/testing of 268 pentapeptides and 96 beta-sheet-forming assemblies, including several unconventional sequences.
evidence.unknown: Assembly findings are bounded to the reported experimental conditions; no application-level performance, therapeutic efficacy or independent replication is established. The specific result was present in the preprint before journal publication.
evidence.ai_role: AI-driven active learning prioritized sequences for iterative synthesis and experimental characterization, focusing in part on cases where model predictions differed from conventional propensity tables.

title: Machine learning selected fractionally doped perovskites for synthesis
summary: A function-confined gradient-boosting model trained on 632 records was used to rank fractionally doped perovskite oxides for a solar thermochemical hydrogen-production application. The authors synthesized 11 selected compositions, seven of which the model classified as relevant to that application. This is a composition-discovery and synthesis result; it does not show that all seven were experimentally validated for hydrogen-production performance.
ai_technology: Function-confined gradient-boosting classifier
organization: Clemson University

source_review.scope: Primary Nature publisher record and full article author manuscript; composition synthesis separated from predicted application relevance.

evidence.tested: The authors report synthesizing 11 model-selected fractionally doped perovskite oxide compositions; seven were classified as relevant to solar thermochemical hydrogen production. The model was evaluated on 632 training records and achieved reported 95.4% accuracy; this classification metric is not a performance result for the 11 synthesized materials.
evidence.unknown: The evidence reviewed does not establish experimentally measured hydrogen-production performance for all seven materials. The entry does not claim each composition is novel outside the authors’ checked data or that model accuracy generalizes beyond the reported dataset.
evidence.ai_role: A function-confined gradient-boosting classifier ranked compositions for synthesis based on target application criteria.

title: Active learning selected antimicrobial polymer P7
summary: An automated Design-Build-Test-Learn campaign applied machine learning and high-throughput synthesis/characterization to a library of 13,728 polymer combinations. Across four active-learning rounds, the authors selected seven candidates for detailed testing. The leading polymer P7 had a reported MIC of 2 μg/mL and IC20 of 256 μg/mL, and was tested in in-vitro and animal models. These laboratory and preclinical results do not establish clinical efficacy or safety.
ai_technology: Graph Transformer model with active-learning selection
organization: Zhejiang University; Institute of Intelligent Chemical Manufacturing and iChemFoundry Platform, Zhejiang University

source_review.scope: Primary PMC indexed full text and NCBI/PubMed metadata/abstract for publication date, affiliations, model, assay outcomes and P7 result.

evidence.tested: The study reports seven top candidates from four active-learning rounds. P7 had MIC 2 μg/mL and IC20 256 μg/mL, with in-vitro characterization and animal-model testing reported by the authors.
evidence.unknown: These are laboratory and animal results, not human efficacy or safety. The entry reports the authors’ selection and assay result without a claim of global chemical novelty or clinical readiness.
evidence.ai_role: A graph-transformer prediction model and active-learning loop ranked polymer candidates for automated synthesis and antimicrobial/biocompatibility testing.

title: Machine learning guided a PET-binding module into a reusable whole-cell catalyst
summary: An HMM and supervised PET hydrolase model screened sequence candidates and prioritized the PET-binding module tCBM13-1. Experiments found greater PET adsorption and retention than the CBM2 comparator; when displayed with FAST-PETase on E. coli, the system increased PET-film depolymerization by about 43% and retained over 64% of initial activity after ten cycles. These are laboratory assays, not evidence of industrial-scale recycling.
ai_technology: Profile-HMM homology search combined with supervised PET hydrolase machine-learning model PETML
organization: Nanjing Tech University; State Key Laboratory of Materials-Oriented Chemical Engineering, Nanjing Tech University

source_review.scope: Primary publisher-indexed full text and primary NCBI/PubMed metadata/abstract, including official article date and affiliations.

evidence.tested: The authors experimentally measured tCBM13-1 adsorption and retention on PET and tested whole-cell co-display with FAST-PETase. The publisher abstract reports about 43% greater PET-film depolymerization (2793 μg/(d·cm²)) and over 64% residual activity after ten cycles.
evidence.unknown: Results are laboratory PET assays; they do not establish industrial-scale recycling, environmental deployment, or lifecycle benefit.
evidence.ai_role: A supervised PET hydrolase machine-learning model within an HMM-based sequence-mining workflow prioritized tCBM13-1 from candidate modules for experimental adsorption and whole-cell depolymerization tests.

title: Random Forest selection guided discovery of nine TRAPUM millisecond pulsars
summary: A Random Forest classifier identified Fermi-LAT sources as pulsar candidates; the team observed 79 selected sources with MeerKAT and reported nine new millisecond pulsars, eight in binaries. The paper reports that all nine candidate signals were subsequently confirmed by additional detections. The authors separately note an independent redetection of one pulsar that had already been discovered elsewhere; it is not counted among the nine new MSPs. This is the 2022 preprint version of a 2023 MNRAS paper.
ai_technology: Random Forest classification of unassociated Fermi-LAT sources
organization: Max Planck Institute for Gravitational Physics (Albert Einstein Institute); Leibniz Universität Hannover; Jodrell Bank Centre for Astrophysics, The University of Manchester; Max-Planck-Institut für Radioastronomie; South African Radio Astronomy Observatory

source_review.scope: Primary arXiv v1 full text and submission metadata; journal reference confirmed on primary arXiv record.

evidence.tested: The source reports that a Random Forest classified 4FGL unassociated sources, 79 selected sources were observed with MeerKAT, and nine new MSPs were detected and subsequently confirmed by additional detections. Eight were in binary systems.
evidence.unknown: The paper describes nine discoveries as new and distinguishes a separate previously discovered pulsar redetected independently. This review did not conduct a separate external catalog audit of every pulsar designation.
evidence.ai_role: A Random Forest classified unassociated 4FGL sources to choose pulsar candidates for the targeted MeerKAT survey in which the nine new MSPs were discovered.

title: Deep-learning prioritization of metagenomic products yielded cytotoxic compounds
summary: MetasynBGC used gene-cluster-family-guided metagenomic mining and a Chemprop graph neural network to prioritize predicted natural-product structures for synthesis. Six selected NRPS-derived compounds showed in-vitro cytotoxic activity across seven cancer cell lines, with reported IC50 values as low as 38.04 μM; compounds D and E showed cell-line-selective activity. These are in-vitro results and do not establish in-vivo efficacy or therapeutic benefit.
ai_technology: Chemprop graph neural network used to prioritize predicted biosynthetic products by antitumor activity
organization: Shandong University; Shenzhen Institutes of Advanced Technology, Chinese Academy of Sciences; Jining Medical University

source_review.scope: Primary ASM article abstract, methods and author affiliation block checked for online date, model role, synthesized compounds and measured cytotoxicity.

evidence.tested: Six synthesized NRPS-derived compounds were tested in vitro across seven cancer cell lines; the paper reports IC50 values as low as 38.04 μM and selective activity for compounds D and E.
evidence.unknown: No in-vivo efficacy or clinical therapeutic benefit is established. The reported potency is limited to the tested in-vitro cancer cell-line assays.
evidence.ai_role: A Chemprop graph neural network scored PRISM-predicted biosynthetic product structures for antitumor potential; the authors jointly used predicted scores and structural feasibility to prioritize compounds for synthesis and cytotoxicity testing.

title: Machine learning exposed a structure in terminal-singularity classification
summary: A neural-network classifier trained on eight-dimensional, Picard-rank-two toric varieties achieved 95% accuracy on a five-million-example test set and enabled rapid generation of a much larger predicted landscape of Q-Fano varieties. The authors report that the model’s classification pattern led them to formulate a new combinatorial criterion for terminal singularities, which they prove mathematically. The learned model suggested the route to the theorem; it did not supply the proof.
ai_technology: Feed-forward neural-network classifier trained on toric-variety weight matrices
organization: Imperial College London; University of Nottingham

source_review.scope: Primary arXiv v1 metadata and full text for posting date, author affiliations, learned-classifier results and connection to the stated mathematical criterion; linked NeurIPS proceedings identity checked.

evidence.tested: The authors report a 95% classification accuracy on a balanced test split of five million eight-dimensional toric-variety examples and use the model to explore a larger Q-Fano landscape. They formulate and prove a new combinatorial criterion for terminal singularities, motivated by the ML analysis.
evidence.unknown: The 95% is internal held-out classification performance, not independent external validation; the authors state the neural network does not itself perform the theorem’s divisibility-based test or proof.
evidence.ai_role: The trained neural-network classifier revealed a tractable pattern in the classification landscape and directly motivated the authors’ new combinatorial criterion; the authors separately establish its correctness by proof.

title: Neural operators reveal nonreciprocal interactions behind microfluidic nonlinear waves
summary: Interpreting a microfluidic droplet experiment movie with a Fourier neural operator and sparse regression yielded a KdV–Burgers-type continuum model containing a dispersive term absent from the prior Burgers description. The authors’ simulations attribute the nonlinear-wave propagation and stabilization to nonreciprocal hydrodynamic interactions. The work analyzes existing experimental data and does not report a new experiment or a general proof for all nonequilibrium crystals.
ai_technology: Fourier neural operator, interpretable neural-network pipeline and sparse regression
organization: University of Chicago; Old Dominion University; Université Claude Bernard Lyon 1; ENS de Lyon; CNRS

source_review.scope: Primary APS abstract and accepted manuscript for the neural-operator and sparse-regression analysis of microfluidic wave data, affiliation block, source data and publication chronology.

evidence.tested: The authors trained/interpreted a neural-operator network on a microfluidic droplet experiment movie and used sparse regression to derive a KdV–Burgers-type model. The new dispersive term improved the shock-front description relative to Burgers’ equation; a microscopic model attributes nonlinear-wave stabilization/propagation to nonreciprocal hydrodynamic interactions. The source says the model was trained on an existing experimental movie.
evidence.unknown: This is a model-derived interpretation of a specific microfluidic experiment and supporting simulations, not a new experiment or a general proof for all nonequilibrium crystals.
evidence.ai_role: A Fourier neural operator learned latent experimental dynamics from the microfluidic movie; sparse regression extracted the governing equation, and the learned term guided the interpretation of nonreciprocal hydrodynamic interactions.

title: AI-generated catalyst design led to experimentally tested polymerization catalysts
summary: A regression-transformer model fine-tuned on historical ring-opening-polymerization data generated candidate catalysts. Researchers selected synthetically accessible, modified surrogates of one model-generated catalyst for laboratory testing. One surrogate, 5c, reached 60% conversion in 32 minutes for monomer 2a and 100% conversion in 45 minutes for monomer 2d, with reported dispersities of 1.06 and 1.34, respectively. The first ChemRxiv v1 (2022-06-27) described computational generation and recovery of a literature-known catalyst. The experimental results appeared in ChemRxiv v2, posted 2023-02-13, and the 2023 peer-reviewed journal article followed on 2023-06-21. The measured tests concern modified surrogates, not the unmodified generated structure.
ai_technology: Regression Transformer generative model fine-tuned on historical polymerization data represented with Chemical Markdown Language
organization: IBM Research–Almaden; IBM Research–Zurich; ETH Zurich; Arctoris

source_review.scope: Primary ChemRxiv v1/v2 records and linked full v1 PDF for version chronology; primary PubMed Central journal full text for model-to-catalyst relationship and measured outcomes; PubMed metadata for journal publication date and affiliations.

evidence.tested: The journal reports model-derived catalyst 3g and synthetically accessible modified surrogates 5c/5d. Surrogate 5c produced 60% conversion of monomer 2a in 32 minutes (dispersity 1.06) and 100% conversion of monomer 2d in 45 minutes (dispersity 1.34).
evidence.unknown: The tested catalysts were modified surrogates rather than the unmodified model-generated 3g structure. These are laboratory ring-opening-polymerization outcomes, not process-scale or commercial performance. The earlier 2022 v1 reported model generation and literature-known catalyst recovery; the experimentally validated result is reported in v2 on 2023-02-13 and in the later journal article.
evidence.ai_role: A regression transformer generated catalyst 3g from historical polymerization data; researchers tested synthetically accessible modified surrogates 5c and 5d that preserved its endocyclic guanidine motif.

title: D2ML guided prospective ROS1 potency and selectivity optimization
summary: Assay-aware models were used to select 84 new compounds for synthesis and prospective testing in a ROS1 kinase program, with TRKB as an anti-target. The most selective prospective compound had a measured ROS1 IC50 of 14.7 nM and 233-fold selectivity over TRKB, compared with 20.3 nM and 79-fold for the most selective training-set compound. The evidence is biochemical and does not establish therapeutic efficacy or safety.
ai_technology: D2ML multi-stage deep neural networks trained across direct-to-biology assay data
organization: Kimia Therapeutics

source_review.scope: Primary arXiv v1 abstract, submission history and full text for date, affiliation, model methods and prospective assay result.

evidence.tested: The authors prospectively synthesized and assayed 84 model-selected compounds. The most selective new compound had ROS1 IC50 14.7 nM and 233-fold selectivity over TRKB; the most selective training compound had 20.3 nM ROS1 IC50 and 79-fold selectivity.
evidence.unknown: This is an in-vitro biochemical discovery result. It does not establish cellular activity, therapeutic efficacy, safety or clinical benefit. The paper compares a historical analog but makes no claim of global chemical novelty.
evidence.ai_role: Assay-aware models using data from multiple direct-to-biology screening stages selected compounds for prospective synthesis and ROS1/TRKB testing.

title: Machine-learning-guided peptide design yielded non-hemolytic anticancer candidates
summary: A recurrent neural network generated peptide sequences and classified predicted activity and hemolysis; a genetic-algorithm route also generated analogues. After sequence and physicochemical filters, researchers synthesized and tested 33 peptides. The paper reports 11 active anticancer peptides in its cell assays, four non-hemolytic under its red-cell assay. These in-vitro results do not establish cancer-cell specificity, clinical safety or therapeutic efficacy. A related 2020 modeling paper is separate from this experimental study; no claim of absolute sequence novelty is made.
ai_technology: Generative recurrent neural network, genetic algorithm, and recurrent-neural-network activity and hemolysis classifiers
organization: University of Bern

source_review.scope: Primary publisher metadata and primary PubMed abstract/affiliation block; full PMC endpoint returned a browser verification challenge in this review.

evidence.tested: The abstract reports that 33 peptides were experimentally evaluated, 11 were active in anticancer cell assays, and four of the active peptides were non-hemolytic in the reported assays.
evidence.unknown: In-vitro activity and red-cell hemolysis do not establish cancer-cell specificity, clinical safety or treatment efficacy. Detailed potency measurements and absolute sequence novelty were not reassessed in this bounded review.
evidence.ai_role: RNN and genetic-algorithm generation with RNN activity and hemolysis classifiers guided peptide selection for synthesis and testing.

title: Machine-learning screening identified three compounds with measured ULK1 inhibition
summary: A Gaussian naive-Bayes classifier using ECFP6 fingerprints ranked commercial compounds from a 13-million-compound library, followed by docking, property filtering and manual selection. Researchers purchased and assayed 25 candidates; three showed micromolar ULK1 inhibition, with reported IC50 values of 37.11 ± 4.41, 7.67 ± 2.82 and 3.15 ± 0.77 μM. The molecules were purchased rather than newly synthesized, and this entry does not claim absolute chemical novelty. The study’s comparator MRT68921 was more potent; the results do not establish cellular activity or clinical utility.
ai_technology: Gaussian naive-Bayes classifier on ECFP6 molecular fingerprints (NB-ECFP6)
organization: The First Affiliated Hospital of Wenzhou Medical University; Oujiang Laboratory; Wenzhou Medical University; Macao Polytechnic University

source_review.scope: Primary PMC full article and linked publisher-version PDF, including methods, kinase assay results, date and author affiliation block.

evidence.tested: The paper reports 25 purchased candidates tested in a biochemical ULK1 kinase assay; three had measured micromolar inhibition with IC50 values 37.11 ± 4.41, 7.67 ± 2.82 and 3.15 ± 0.77 μM.
evidence.unknown: The candidates were purchased, not synthesized. The reported assays do not establish cell activity or clinical effect; the reference MRT68921 was more potent in the paper’s comparison. Absolute structure novelty is not claimed here.
evidence.ai_role: The NB-ECFP6 model screened a large commercial compound set and prioritized candidates for downstream docking and biochemical testing.

title: Active learning improved whole-cell antibiotic screening and validation
summary: A closed-loop active-learning campaign for Borrelia burgdorferi whole-cell screening increased the experimental hit rate five-fold, from 0.2% in investigator-selected plates to 1.0% in the AL-guided campaign. The same study separately reports prospective in-silico selection of diverse compounds across bacterial species, with 11.0% experimental validation of predicted hits and 53-fold enrichment over investigator-directed screening; those validated compounds showed the intended narrow-spectrum B. burgdorferi activity. These are assay and screening results, not clinical efficacy.
ai_technology: Active learning using a directed message-passing neural network and evidential Dirichlet head
organization: Harvard Medical School; Tufts University; Tufts Lyme Disease Initiative; Texas A&M University; Broad Institute of MIT and Harvard; Tufts University School of Medicine; Stuart B. Levy Center for Integrated Management of Antimicrobial Resistance; Tufts University School of Engineering; Mass General Hospital

source_review.scope: Primary bioRxiv indexed text, PubMed metadata/abstract and PMC indexed full-text excerpt; direct bioRxiv and PMC page loads were blocked.

evidence.tested: In a closed-loop Borrelia burgdorferi campaign, active-learning-guided selection produced a 1.0% experimental screening hit rate versus 0.2% in investigator-selected plates. A separate prospective in-silico selection across bacterial species achieved 11.0% experimental validation of predicted hits (53-fold enrichment over investigator-directed screening); the paper reports intended narrow-spectrum activity for B. burgdorferi.
evidence.unknown: Preprint evidence is not independent replication or clinical testing. The cross-species hit-validation experiment is distinct from the closed-loop Borrelia hit-rate comparison. Direct full page retrieval was blocked; checked material was the primary indexed preprint and archived primary article text.
evidence.ai_role: A directed message-passing neural network with an evidential Dirichlet head supported active-learning compound selection for whole-cell inhibition testing; selected compounds were then experimentally screened.

title: Ensemble machine learning identified CDK8 inhibitor hits
summary: A six-model ensemble classified 1.6 million commercial molecules and reduced them to a 1,672-compound CDK8-focused screening library. Docking and visual inspection selected 25 candidates for enzymatic assays; six showed CDK8 inhibition. The most potent hit, T479-0984, had a reported IC50 of 99.9 nM. The paper reports low structural similarity (Tanimoto <0.300) to a comparison set of 30 diverse known CDK8 inhibitors. These are assay hits and starting points, not validated drugs or evidence of therapeutic efficacy.

This entry covers only the nine MSP discoveries. Six slower pulsars were also reported, but five were found in a wider incoherent beam and are not included in the AI-linked result. The authors note earlier optical redback-candidate identification for PSR J1910−5320 and single-pulse reports in the J0657−4657 beam; no claim is made that these were the first observations at all wavelengths.

organization: The University of Manchester; National Astronomical Research Institute of Thailand

The paper also reports six slow pulsars, but five were detected in the wider incoherent beam and are not included in this AI-linked claim. evidence.ai_role: A random-forest model ranked unassociated Fermi-LAT sources for target selection; radio searches of 79 selected targets yielded the nine coherent-beam MSP discoveries.

title: PICS-assisted survey reported seven new Large Magellanic Cloud pulsars

The AI narrowed the candidate set; volunteers performed the final candidate classification and follow-up observations supplied additional checks. Six pulsars were detected again in follow-up; the incoherent-beam pulsar was not. title: A 3D Bioprinted Pseudo-Bone Drug Delivery Scaffold for Bone Tissue Engineering.
summary: ANN-supported optimization selected a 3D-printed simvastatin scaffold with 20-day in-vitro release. The primary abstract reports hardness and resilience near healthy bone in a mechanically fractured human clavicle model. These release and ex-vivo mechanical endpoints do not establish living-organism healing or clinical benefit.
ai_technology: Artificial neural network for scaffold optimization
organization: University of the Witwatersrand

evidence.tested: Thirty-nine scaffold formulations were evaluated with ANN-supported optimization. The selected 14% PPF/16% PF127 formulation released simvastatin in vitro for 20 days. The abstract reports hardness and resilience near healthy bone in a mechanically fractured human clavicle model; specimen and replicate counts were not assessed in this review.
evidence.unknown: Living-organism bone healing and patient benefit are not established by the reported in-vitro release and ex-vivo mechanical model. Specimen and replicate counts were not assessed.
evidence.ai_role: A multilayer feed-forward/back-propagation artificial neural network optimized scaffold formulation using thermogelation and drug-release responses; it did not test biological healing.

source_review.scope: Publisher abstract and indexed publisher Methods/Results passages on ANN/formulations and drug release; complete article and mechanical-model methods not independently reviewed.
